articles.title: Democrats vow to rein in Donald Trump as he shows off White House ballroom
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress

Democrats vowed to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in President Donald Trump, setting ​up two years of possible deadlock in Washington, as Mr. Trump spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom.

A wave of anger over Mr. Trump’s policies, particularly the U.S.-Iran war’s ‌role in pushing the cost of living higher, helped Democrats take the Senate, where they flipped seats in deeply Republican states for ​a majority of at least 54-44. Democrats also gained at least 30 seats in the House of Representatives.
It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that the incoming majority would be focused on affordability and accountability.
U.S. midterm elections witness historic firsts: First Black woman governor to first Muslim senator
Midterm results put U.S.-Israel ties under further strain
U.S. midterm elections: An economy under pressure, political shift and the road ahead

“We don’t work for Donald Trump,” Jeffries, a New York lawmaker who is on track to become the first Black speaker of the ‌House, told reporters on Wednesday. “We work for the American people. And the days of the House of Representatives functioning like a wholly owned subsidiary of the Trump administration are over.”

Mr. Trump, who had devoted his last pre-election public appearance on Monday (November 2, 2026) to talking about his renovations ‌of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, called in reporters on the morning after his party’s sweeping midterm defeat to show off the ballroom he is building at the ‌White ⁠House.

“When I get criticized, like, ‘Why are you working on the White House?’ I’m doing it because the White House is the ultimate symbol ⁠of America, and it’s got to be pristine, it’s got to be perfect,” Mr. Trump said. “For me, it’s relaxing.”

He turned only briefly to the elections during his nearly hour-long appearance, telling reporters, “I’ll get along probably with the Democrats, unless they want to be destructive, but I have the power of the veto.”

Mr. Trump had cast the midterm elections as a referendum on the first half of his second four-year stint in ​the White House, repeatedly urging his Republican base to “pretend I’m on the ballot,” ‌a message that Democratic Party leaders were happy to amplify.

articles.title: Jaishankar urges Commonwealth partners to 'de-risk and diversify'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: S. Jaishankar said Commonwealth partners need to make more efforts to enhance local distribution, adding that more connectivity corridors are good for business
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has urged Commonwealth partners to "de-risk and diversify", emphasising the need to enhance local distribution among member nations.
Mr. Jaishankar arrived in St. John's on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) to attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).

"Commonwealth partners also need to de-risk and diversify. This requires shorter and trusted supply chains," Mr. Jaishankar posted on social media after attending the Commonwealth heads of government and business leaders' breakfast meeting on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Mr. Jaishankar said Commonwealth partners need to make more efforts to enhance local distribution, adding that more connectivity corridors are good for business.
"Promote training and capacity building as it gives more options for partners," he said.
EAM said that the Indian business community spread across the world is an asset for the Commonwealth.
Speaking about the significance of digital public infrastructure for good governance, Mr. Jaishankar said, "Digital is a game changer as it promotes efficiency, good governance and growth."
"International Solar Alliance and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure can be leveraged for climate action," Mr. Jaishankar said.
Sharing India's experiences in Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR), Mr. Jaishankar said, "Our First Responder experiences and HADR activities suggest the need for local hubs."
He said that comfort within the Commonwealth nations "can build business for growth and prosperity", adding that mobility of skills can be an important Commonwealth focus.
The theme of this year's CHOGM is accelerating partnerships and investment for a prosperous Commonwealth.
Mr. Jaishankar also met with the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, Andy Burnham and the Prime Minister of Australia, Anthony Albanese, on the sidelines of CHOGM.

fullParagraphs: Mr. Kim’s powerful sister Kim Yo Jong signalled that there was little appetite for renewed dialogue with Washington, saying Pyongyang had “no need to sit face to face with such unreliable and hostile persons”

A meeting between Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un appears increasingly unlikely when the U.S. president travels to Asia in November, analysts say, after he suffered a crushing midterm election defeat.

Mr. Trump had said he “may” meet Mr. Kim this month and that it “would be exciting”, but appeared to backtrack in October, saying, “I don’t know... I’m not sure that anybody’s asking for a meeting,” while adding that his “relationship with Kim Jong Un is very good.”

Mr. Trump’s focus on Mr. Kim and his scaling back of joint U.S.-South Korean military drills have alarmed Asian allies, while sparking speculation that he is seeking a foreign policy win as his war with Iran stalls.

But Mr. Kim’s powerful sister Kim Yo Jong signalled on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that there was little appetite for renewed dialogue with Washington, saying Pyongyang had “no need to sit face to face with such unreliable and hostile persons”.
“The choice for peace includes dialogue of course, but this is not surely equated with national interests for us,” she said.
Ms. Kim’s statement marked “a shift from defence to offence”, said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University’s Institute for Far Eastern Studies in South Korea.
“The latest statement uses the (cyberattack) issue as an opportunity to condemn the entire US policy of pressure against North Korea,” he told AFP.
In 2019, North Korea’s Kim Jong Un made a 60-hour train journey home from Hanoi empty-handed after a summit with Trump collapsed.
Now, the dynamic has reversed. Trump is making repeated overtures, only to be met with reluctance from Pyongyang.
“For Kim Jong Un, maintaining the status quo is the best option right now,” Lim said.
Analysts say the North Korean leader has even less incentive to meet Trump after his Republican party suffered a thumping defeat in the U.S. midterm elections on November 3.
Voters handed control of Congress to the Democrats in a stunning rebuke to Mr. Trump, leaving him as a lame duck President for the remaining two years of his term.

articles.title: India announces extension of $500 million line of credit for Guyana
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: EAM Jaishankar met Guyanese President Mohamed Irfaan Ali on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting

India has announced an extension of a $500 million line of credit for roads, health and defence projects in Guyana as External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Guyanese President Mohamed Irfaan Ali in Antigua and Barbuda.
Mr. Jaishankar, who arrived in St. John's on Tuesday (November 4, 2026), met President Ali on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) on Wednesday.

"Delighted to meet with President Dr Irfaan Ali of Guyana. @presidentaligy. Reviewed the steady progress in our bilateral cooperation, especially after PM @narendramodi’s visit in 2024," Mr. Jaishankar posted on social media on Wednesday after the meeting.

The two leaders discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, energy, agriculture, infrastructure development, digital technology and capacity building, a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said.
"Announced extension of $500 million Line of Credit for roads, health & defence projects," Mr. Jaishankar said.
India has already completed several development projects in Guyana, and the new line of credit will further strengthen the development partnership between the two countries, the statement said.

The two countries also signed three agreements, including on the supply and installation of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) manufacturing projects and grant assistance for implementation of Quick Impact Projects (QIPs), the statement said.
The third agreement was on cooperation in the field of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and the Functioning of a Unified Payments Interface (UPI)-like System in Guyana, it said.

India and Guyana share longstanding and close relations, rooted in historical, cultural and people-to-people ties. The countries are not only members of the Commonwealth but also Global South partners.
The two countries will continue to work together to strengthen their multifaceted cooperation and advance shared priorities for development and prosperity, the statement said.
Earlier, Mr. Jaishankar attended a Commonwealth heads of government and business leaders' breakfast meeting where he urged Commonwealth partners to "de-risk and diversify”.

Last month, celebrated as Breast Cancer Awareness Month, reminded us, as it does every year, about the importance of mammograms, early diagnosis, and advances in treatment. These messages save lives and deserve continued attention. However, there is another conversation that often receives far less attention: the role of food, physical activity, obesity, diabetes, physical activity, and metabolic health in breast cancer.

In my oncology clinic, patients are often surprised when I bring up these topics. They say, “Doctor, I knew breast cancer was related to family history. I didn’t know that lifestyle diseases such as diabetes and obesity had anything to do with it.”

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: The Amazon is no longer a carbon sink, it is an emitter

fullParagraphs: The Hindu’s weekly Science for All newsletter explains all things Science, without the jargon.

The world’s largest tropical forest, referred to as the ‘lungs of the planet,’ the Amazon rainforest once acted as a vast carbon sink that helped absorb human-induced CO2 emissions. But now, a study startlingly finds that the Amazon releases more CO2 than it absorbs from the atmosphere, as it is decimated by deforestation and forest fires.

Scientists measured CO2 levels at different atmospheric altitudes, using research airplanes, between the years 2010 and 2024 at four Amazonian sites. Their findings indicated that “Amazonia is a net carbon source rather than a sink and cannot offset regional anthropogenic emissions.”

articles.title: Karnataka raises DA for State government staff by from 15.75% to 18%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Dearness Allowance (DA) for the State government employees would now be increased from the present 15.75% to 18% of their basic pay.
Karnataka has announced a Deepavali bonanza for State government employees by increasing the Dearness Allowance by 2.25 percentage points with retrospective effect from July 2026.

According to a notification issued on Thursday (November 5, 2026), the Dearness Allowance (DA) for the State government employees would now be increased from the present 15.75% to 18% of their basic pay. The increase will come into effect from July 1, 2026.
The increase in DA will also apply to the pensioners and family pensioners, according to the notification.

articles.title: Ram Madhav targets Congress Govt in Telangana, predicts BJP victory in 2028
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BJP national vice president says electoral roll revisions were undertaken periodically since Independence

Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national vice-president Ram Madhav on Thursday (November 5, 2026) asserted that the party is the only “viable and undisputed” alternative to the Congress government in Telangana , accusing Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy of neglecting governance and focusing excessively on visits to Delhi.

Addressing a press conference at the BJP State office in Hyderabad, Mr. Madhav alleged that the Congress government had “failed on multiple fronts” and said the BJP would intensify its campaign against what he termed “corruption, policy failures and maladministration” by the ruling party.

“We will take these issues to the grassroots level and expose the Congress government before the people. The BJP will further strengthen its agitations, and it is certain that the party will come to power in Telangana by 2028,” he claimed.

Mr. Madhav also defended the Election Commission of India’s ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and accused the Congress Party of spreading “misinformation” about the exercise. The voters list revision is a “routine process” aimed at ensuring the integrity of electoral rolls, he insisted.

He maintained that electoral roll revisions were undertaken periodically since Independence and that it is the Election Commission’s responsibility to remove duplicate, deceased, relocated and ineligible voters from the rolls

“The Congress Party’s anxiety over the SIR exercise stems from its desire to protect votes of illegal immigrants. Unable to accept electoral defeats, it is attempting to undermine democratic institutions by casting doubts on the Election Commission, electronic voting machines and the electoral process itself,” he alleged.

Citing a statement made by former Union Home Minister Indrajit Gupta in Parliament about “1.2 crore illegal immigrants”, Mr. Madhav alleged that Congress was creating an “unnecessary uproar” over the SIR process for political reasons. He also dismissed the Congress Party’s demand for a return to ballot papers, arguing that t he party had suffered defeats even in elections conducted using paper ballots , including recent local body and MLC elections.

The BJP leader claimed that several leaders who once championed such an alternative, including Mamata Banerjee, Naveen Patnaik and Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, had lost power, while main opposition party in Telangana, the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) party, has become an “iron leg”, he remarked.

articles.title: Bus travel gets costlier in Karnataka; fares hiked by 23% to 35%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In another financial blow to consumers following the recent increase in milk and curd prices, the Karnataka government has announced a hike in bus fares across all four State-run transport corporations, with the revised rates coming into effect from the early hours of Thursday, November 5.

While fares on services operated by the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC), North Western Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (NWKRTC) and Kalyana Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (KKRTC) have been increased by an average of 23%, Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) fares have been raised by 35%.

Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh announced the revision at a press conference held at the KSRTC central office in Bengaluru on Wednesday. He attributed the increase to repeated hikes in diesel prices by the Union government since May this year, rising expenditure on spare parts, higher staff-related costs and mounting financial losses incurred by the transport corporations.

According to the revised fare structure, BMTC fares have increased by ₹4 to ₹12, depending on the distance travelled. For KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC services, the increase ranges from ₹9 to ₹18, depending on the stages of travel and the type of service.

Defending the decision, Mr. Suresh said the government had opted for a comparatively lower increase than the 45% hike recommended by the Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee (PTFRC), chaired by retired IAS officer Atul Kumar Tiwari. The committee had examined the financial position of the four transport corporations before submitting its recommendations to the government. “The boards of the four transport corporations had sought fare increases of up to 90%. However, the government opted for a lower revision, keeping public interest in mind,” he said.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar defended the fare revision, stating that it had become necessary due to the increase in diesel prices effected by the Union government. He said the State government was willing to proportionately reduce bus fares if the Centre rolled back diesel prices. "The State-owned road transport corporations are facing losses. About three weeks ago, the State government had to intervene when the RTCs did not have money to purchase diesel. The government provided the funds,” he told reporters in Bengaluru.

His remarks came in response to the Opposition parties’ announcement of statewide protests against the fare hike on Thursday. The Opposition BJP and JD(S) have announced protests across Karnataka on November 5, accusing the Congress government of burdening the public with repeated price increases. The protests are expected to target the latest bus fare revision, which comes days after the State government increased milk and curd prices by ₹8 per litre or packet across categories.

He attributed the increase to repeated hikes in diesel prices by the Union government since May this year, rising expenditure on spare parts, higher staff-related costs and mounting financial losses incurred by the transport corporations.

articles.title: With no illegal immigrants found on draft electoral rolls, SIR greatly inconvenienced people: Owaisi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Qadeemi Masjid was there before Delhi became the national capital, says AIMIM president

Hyderabad parliamentarian Asaduddin Owaisi on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) said the claim of illegal immigrants being included in electoral rolls had caused considerable hardship, particularly to the poor, who lost at least two days’ wages completing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process, even as officials said there was no evidence of illegal migrants being included in the draft electoral rolls.

Referring to the statement made by Hyderabad District Election Officer R.V. Karnan, that no foreign nationals or illegal migrants were found in the draft electoral rolls after the revision exercise, Mr. Owaisi said the finding had exposed the claims repeatedly made by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Sangh parivar leaders as false. He said that thousands of people were put through the verification process and daily wage earners were forced to forego income to furnish documents and complete enrolment formalities.

Touching upon the issue of Qadeemi Masjid located within the Krishi Bhavan complex in New Delhi , Mr. Owaisi criticised the Union government’s attempts to remove the structure as part of the Common Central Secretariat redevelopment under the Central Vista project. Earlier in the day, he had posted on X that the Centre had informed the Delhi High Court that the masjid was “impermissible and incompatible with the secular character of government property” and therefore needed to be removed.

Mr. Owaisi, who is the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) president, noted that the Central Vista project itself was inaugurated with a Bhoomi Pooja (ground breaking ceremony) and remarked that “secularism is not offended by the use of one faith’s rituals for a public project, but is allergic to a masjid that has stood there even before 1912”. He said the masjid predated Krishi Bhavan and even the development of Lutyens’ Delhi.

The AIMIM chief said the masjid was part of the country’s cultural heritage and had not been included in the land acquisition process undertaken by the British for the development of New Delhi. He sought Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju’s intervention and said the government should recognise the historical and legal status of the mosque. He added that any dispute over the property could be adjudicated before the Waqf Tribunal. “The mosque was there before Delhi became the national capital. What exactly do they want to do with it now?” he asked.

Mr. Owaisi also criticised what he described as attempts to diminish the political aspirations of Muslims. Recalling remarks often made by BJP leaders about “Abdul” being confined to repairing punctures, he said Muslims would no longer be intimidated by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and would emerge as political leaders.

articles.title: Sharjeel Imam moves Supreme Court seeking bail in UAPA case over 2020 Delhi riots
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Activist Sharjeel Imam has moved the Supreme Court against a Delhi High Court order refusing him bail in an Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) case on the "larger conspiracy" behind the February 2020 riots in northeast Delhi.

In his plea before the top court, Mr. Imam contended that he should be granted bail as the prosecution has failed to examine witnesses and the one-year embargo imposed by the top court is about to expire.
The petition contended that the charge sheet was filed on September 25, 2020, in which 18 accused face trial and the prosecution has cited more than 900 witnesses, including 47 protected witnesses.
Mr. Imam submitted that despite spending six years and nine months as undertrial, the prosecution has failed to examine even a single witness.
The Delhi High Court on September 30 refused to grant bail to activists Umar Khalid and Mr. Imam in a case under UAPA on the "larger conspiracy" behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.

Asserting that it is bound by "judicial discipline", the high court said it could not modify the Supreme Court's January 5 order asking the two accused to seek bail either on completion of protected witnesses' examination or expiry of one year, whichever is earlier.
Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam challenged the trial court's July 4 decision rejecting their bail pleas for the third time since their arrest.
The trial court had rejected the bail applications, saying it had "no option but to follow" the Supreme Court's January 5 order and, therefore, could neither entertain the plea nor grant any relief.

The high court had noted that while denying bail to the two accused in January, the top court had said their roles were distinct from the other co-accused, and they were the "ideological drivers" of the alleged conspiracy.
Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam have been booked under UAPA on allegations of being among the masterminds of the February 2020 riots that left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.
The violence erupted during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, and the National Register of Citizens (NRC).

Activist Khalid Saifi and former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain, among others, were also booked for their alleged involvement in the larger conspiracy case, being investigated by Delhi Police's Special Cell.

articles.title: Thousands of troops secure Indonesia trial as tensions run high over wiretap scandal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Three senior generals have already been detained in the wiretapping scandal, including Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who had been named chief of staff to President Prabowo Subianto last month

Indonesian authorities tasked thousands of police and military personnel to provide security on Thursday (November 5, 2026) for a trial involving former President Joko Widodo, as tensions in the capital remained high over allegations that top officers had been involved in intercepting the current President's telephone conversations.
Three senior generals have already been detained in the wiretapping scandal, including Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who had been named chief of staff to President Prabowo Subianto last month.

Gen. Listyo previously served as national police chief under Mr. Widodo, though the former President has not been implicated in the wiretapping investigation. There are allegations that Cabinet officials, politicians, journalists, civil society leaders and business executives were also subjected to unauthorised surveillance.

After losing two Presidential races to Mr. Widodo, Mr. Prabowo aligned himself with the popular leader and campaigned as his successor, choosing Mr. Widodo’s son as his running mate in a move that fuelled concerns about a growing political dynasty in Indonesia’s young democracy.

Mr. Widodo and Mr. Prabowo were once close political allies, with Mr. Widodo backing Mr. Prabowo’s successful 2024 Presidential bid, but their relationship has come under increased scrutiny amid signs of a growing rift since Mr. Prabowo took office.

Retired police Gen. Oegroseno, a former deputy national police chief, told the Forum Keadilan TV podcast on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that investigators should examine all possible lines of command behind the wiretapping, including whether any directives originated from Mr. Widodo.

“Investigators should not hesitate to question a former President if necessary,” Gen. Oegroseno said. “The motive behind the alleged wiretapping operation must be fully uncovered under the leadership of the current police chief.”

The wiretapping operation could also constitute a serious human rights violation and could be used to intimidate critics and weaken civil liberties, said Usman Hamid, Amnesty International's executive director in Indonesia.

“This is not merely about the alleged wiretapping of the President,” Mr. Hamid said in a statement. “Authorities must disclose who else may have been targeted and investigate the full impact of the operation.”

Police allege the unauthorised wiretapping took place between 2025 and 2026, after Mr. Prabowo had been elected and while Gen. Listyo was still national police chief. National Police Legal Division head Sonta Nasution and Eko Hadi Santoso, a senior instructor at the National Police Education and Training Institute, were also detained.

Authorities have called in more than 20,000 troops to Jakarta, and on Thursday (November 5, 2026) said that 6,770 police and military personnel had been deployed to secure Mr. Widodo's hearing. Mr. Widodo was called to testify in a defamation trial stemming from allegations that he used a fake university diploma. The trial is unrelated to the wiretapping case and Mr. Widodo denied the diploma allegations.
As he arrived on Thursday (November 5, 2026) morning at the East Jakarta District Court, the former President was welcomed by hundreds of his supporters chanting messages of encouragement.

articles.title: What the BJP should learn from Trump’s redistricting failure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Gerrymandering assumes that voting preferences remain unchanged between election cycles; but when the traditional supporters of a party turn against it, constituency maps matter little.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has lessons to draw from the Republican Party in the United States in its attempts to undertake a hurried, hushed and partisan redrawing of the country’s electoral map. The BJP has been planning for an out-of-cycle Census and a delimitation exercise by delaying the 2021 Census until 2026. The Republican Party redrew Congressional district boundaries across eight States under the direction of President Donald J. Trump in the hope of flipping seats currently held by Democrats. But they lost most of them and, in addition, lost seats they had hoped to retain, as their heartlands such as Texas and Florida slipped away.

Gerrymandering, the practice of redrawing electoral boundaries by packing or cracking particular social groups, assumes that voting preferences remain unchanged between election cycles. But when the traditional supporters of a party turn against it, constituency maps matter little. The Bankipur by-election in Bihar in August had proved the same point. The constituency is perfectly tailored for a BJP victory, going by its demographic composition. But when the upper-caste supporters of the party changed their minds, the BJP was decimated.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: What the BJP should learn from Trump’s redistricting failure. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

The constituency is perfectly tailored for a BJP victory, going by its demographic composition. But when the upper-caste supporters of the party changed their minds, the BJP was decimated.

articles.title: Climate change increased tropical Cyclone Arnab’s damage by 33%: Study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: “Climate change increased Cyclone Arnab’s maximum wind speed by approximately 5%, and intensified its eyewall rainfall rate by 11% at landfall,” according to the study

Climate change increased the damage caused by the tropical Cyclone Arnab, which struck eastern India on October 28, by 33%, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in additional direct economic losses compared to a pre-industrial climate baseline, according to a new study.
ALSO WATCH Cyclone Arnab batters east coast: 5 dead in Andhra Pradesh, 17 Odisha districts affected
It added that the storm brought intense rain, peak 1-minute sustained winds of up to 202 kilometres per hour, and severe damage to infrastructure across Andhra Pradesh.
The study was carried out by researchers at the Imperial College London’s Grantham Institute and published on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

For their analysis, researchers used the Imperial College Storm Model (IRIS) to simulate Cyclone Arnab under current conditions (plus 1.3° Celsius above pre-industrial levels) versus a counterfactual climate without human-induced warming.
“Climate change increased Cyclone Arnab’s maximum wind speed by approximately 5%, and intensified its eyewall rainfall rate by 11% at landfall,” according to the study.

It also revealed that direct damage to physical assets in India was estimated to be 33% higher than it would have been in a pre-industrial climate baseline, attributing roughly 25% of the total economic damage directly to climate change.
ALSO WATCH Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India

In a statement, Dr. Nathan Sparks, researcher at the Department of Physics, Imperial College London, said: “These findings are a powerful reminder of the price of inaction. The costs of climate change are not hypothetical future projections — they are hitting coastal communities in eastern India today.”

articles.title: Pregnant women in corridors, waiting areas should not be construed as overcrowding: Niloufer superintendent
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Responding to the news report published in The Hindu on allegations of overcrowding and poor sanitation at the government-run Niloufer Hospital in Hyderabad, the hospital superintendent said the institution functions as a tertiary care referral centre catering to high-risk pregnancies. The presence of pregnant women in corridors and waiting areas, therefore, should not be construed as overcrowding, the superintendent said.

He said that women in the early stages of labour, who may take eight to 12 hours to deliver, are advised by the duty medical team to walk in the verandah while being monitored round the clock. This could give visitors the impression that the hospital was overcrowded.

He added that the hospital houses a High Dependency Unit (HDU), Maternal Intensive Care Unit (MICU) and labour room on the same floor. Besides women visiting for routine antenatal check-ups, several pregnant women in critical condition are referred to the hospital for specialised obstetric and gynaecological care, including treatment for conditions such as hypertension, diabetes and severe anaemia.

articles.title: Case booked against madrasa teacher for sexually abusing 11-year-old boy

fullParagraphs: A case has been registered against a teacher on charges of sexually abusing an 11-year-old boy at a madrasa attached to Fatima Masjid in Kurmaguda.

According to the complaint lodged by the boy’s mother, the accused subjected the child to sexual abuse after showing him obscene videos on a mobile phone. The accused also reportedly warned the boy against disclosing the incident to anyone.

Madannapet police registered a case against the accused under Sections 127(2) and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Sections 8 and 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. The boy was sent to Bharosa centre for recording his statement. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: New posting for former Kochi City Police chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar who was recently removed from the post of District Police Chief (Kochi City) was appointed as Inspector General of Police, Crimes-II.

The 2005 IPS officer was removed as Commissioner in October after the Kochi police faced flak over alleged lapses in the probe in the Cheranelloor car crash case involving the 17-year-old son of a judge.
Later, the government appointed R. Nishanthini as the new District Police Chief (Kochi City).
The Home department said in a November 5 order that Mr. Mahesh Kumar will also hold full additional charge of Deputy Inspector General of Police, Anti-Terrorist Squad.

Meanwhile, N. Rajan, the IPS officer functioning as Vigilance Officer in the Kerala State Electricity Board has been transferred. His new posting is as Superintendent of Police (Administration), State Special Branch, Thiruvananthapuram.

articles.title: Telangana, a major poultry hub, to host 18th Poultry India Expo from November 25 to 27
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Expo has expanded tenfold since 2007, from 3,500 sq. metres in one hall to 35,000 sq. metres across seven halls now

Poultry India Expo has expanded tenfold since 2007, from 3,500 sq. metres in one hall to 35,000 sq. metres across seven halls now, reflecting the rapid growth of India’s poultry industry and rising business interest.

The 18th edition of the Expo will be held at HITEX Exhibition Centre in Hyderabad from November 25 to 27. More than 550 exhibitors have registered, and over 51,000 industry professionals from around 120 countries are expected to attend.

Organised by the Indian Poultry Equipment Manufacturers’ Association (IPEMA) under Poultry India, the expo will bring together poultry farmers, equipment manufacturers, feed producers, breeders, veterinarians and technology companies.
The exhibition will showcase innovations in breeding, hatchery management, automated feeding, climate-controlled housing, farm automation, veterinary diagnostics, egg processing and waste management.

IPEMA–Poultry India president Uday Singh Bayas described the event as a “one nation-one expo” gathering that unites poultry associations and industry stakeholders. Poultry Knowledge Day, the expo’s flagship technical conference, will be inaugurated on November 24 at HICC–Novotel. Sessions will cover poultry health, nutrition, vaccination, artificial intelligence, automation and sustainable farming. Union Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj S. P. Singh Baghel will attend.
Mr. Bayas said the expo’s tenfold expansion since its launch in 2007 reflected the industry’s rapid growth and entrepreneurs’ increasing interest in poultry.

India, the world’s second-largest egg producer , produced 149.11 billion eggs in 2024–25, according to Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025. Andhra Pradesh accounted for the largest share at 18.37%, followed by Tamil Nadu at 15.63% and Telangana at 12.98%.

Telangana remains a major poultry hub, with estimated daily sales of 12 lakh broiler birds, according to V. Lakshma Reddy, former Director of Animal Husbandry, Telangana. The State has an estimated 2,000 layer farmers and about 10,000 broiler farmers. It produces about 3.8 crore eggs a day, nearly half of which are sent to Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

articles.title: ECI issues fresh work allocation order; brings back oversight on IT head
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: As per the current order, dated October 4, IT Head Seema Khanna is required to route the files related to IT/ICT and Grievances/PGRS through Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Pawan Kumar Sharma

More than three months after the row over movement of IT Head Seema Khanna’s files , the Election Commission of India has issued a fresh order bringing back oversight over her department through a Deputy Election Commissioner.

An internal order issued on July 28 by Senior DEC Maneesh Garg had removed Deputy Election Commissioner Sanjay Kumar from the charge of IT and ICT and gave Dr. Khanna a free hand, enabling her to directly report to the Commission. Following this, two Election Commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had written to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan on July 29 regarding the working allocation order of Dr. Garg, who had been in interim charge of Administration department.
As per the current order, dated October 4, Dr. Khanna is required to route the files related to IT/ICT and Grievances/PGRS through Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Pawan Kumar Sharma.

Dr. Khanna joined the ECI in 2025 on deputation from the National Informatics Centre (NIC). She heads the commission’s IT department, and oversees its digital infrastructure, including systems for electoral-roll management.

ECI sources though insisted that there is no change in the reporting structure of DG IT as she has always been reporting to a DEC level officer. In an affidavit filed in the Supreme Court the ECI had maintained that the July 28 order had never been implemented.
The sources also said that the work allocation orders were as per unanimous decisions of the Commission.

The letters to the Cabinet Secretary, by Dr. Sandhu and Dr. Joshi obtained through RTI by transparency activist Commodore (retired) Lokesh Batra explained their objections regarding Dr. Garg changing the work allocation of officers “within hours of” getting the charge of administration wing “without discussing or informing” them despite “repeated and explicit oral and written” instructions to all officers.
Both ECs had also said that Dr. Garg had “issued similar orders on one earlier occasion” while he was working as DEC (Administration).

Prakash Rajpurohit, an IAS officer of the 2010 batch, who was appointed as a Deputy Election Commissioner in the ECI filling the vacancy caused by the premature repatriation of Sanjay Kumar, who was earlier in-charge of the Electoral Rolls and IT division, would now be assisting Dr. Garg in Election Planning. Interestingly, he would also be in-charge of delimitation.

Earlier, Sanjay Kumar, who had been DEC from August 2024 till August this year, before his repatriation, had been responsible for the electoral roll and IT divisions of the ECI, and had signed the ECI’s June 24, 2025, order initiating the SIR in the country.
Election Commission of India / Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls

articles.title: Vigilance launches inspection in welfare fund boards functioning under Keralam government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Vigilance director says the inspections were progressing in 78 offices of 16 boards functioning under the State government’s Department of Labour
The Vigilance and Anti Corruption Bureau (VACB) on Thursday (November 5, 2026) launched inspections in 16 welfare fund boards after receiving complaints about financial irregularities and corruption.

Vigilance director Manoj Abraham said in a statement that the inspections, titled ‘Operation Welfare Fund,’ were progressing in 78 offices of 16 boards functioning under the State government’s Department of Labour.
According to the VACB, the complaints that it received with regard to the functioning of the welfare fund boards were of a diverse nature.

There allegedly were instances of officials misappropriating the contribution remitted by employers to the fund. It was also alleged that bribes were taken for including ineligible individuals in the beneficiary list, and that, account details were being tampered with to continue the pension payment even after the deaths of beneficiaries.
Other complaints pertained to the payment of multiple pensions to the same individual, payment of ex gratia benefits to ineligible persons, and diversion of government assistance.
The inspections are being undertaken as part of ‘Pro-Active Vigilance’ initiative in government institutions as part of the VACB’s ‘Project Zero’ aimed at a corruption-free Keralam.
Mr. Abraham also urged the public to inform the Vigilance about corrupt activities on the toll-free number 1064 or on the mobile numbers 8592900900 and 9447789100.

articles.title: Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government as religious party drops Netanyahu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Opposition leader also received a recommendation from a key lawmaker from the Israeli-Arab minority, whose seats in Parliament soared due to outrage over Netanyahu's policies

Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday (November 5, 2026) as the favourite to be tasked with trying to form an Israeli government as a religious party long aligned with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declined to recommend him.

President Isaac Herzog was holding a second day of consultations with political parties after the October 27 election, in which neither Mr. Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Mr. Eisenkot — a former military chief promising to restore national unity — secured enough votes for a majority.
Mr. Herzog will choose for himself whom to ask to form a new government, but traditionally the mandate is given to the person recommended by more parties, which would be Mr. Eisenkot.

The Opposition leader also received a recommendation from a key lawmaker from the Israeli-Arab minority, whose seats in Parliament soared due to outrage over Mr. Netanyahu's policies, even as Mr. Eisenkot has remained unclear on whether he would accept Arab support to form a government.

United Torah Judaism, which backed Mr. Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Mr. Herzog declined to recommend Mr. Netanyahu again as Prime Minister, although it also did not side with Mr. Eisenkot.

The party informed Mr. Herzog "that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government," the President's office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats.

The party — which represents ultra-Orthodox Jews of Ashkenazi origin, who mostly hail from or have roots in Europe — as well as Shas — which represents the same community but of Sephardic, or mostly West Asian and North African descent — have both been backed by Mr. Netanyahu as they push to maintain the exemption from military service for religious students.

Mr. Netanyahu has preserved the exemption but stopped short of enshrining it in law, in the face of major resentment from many other Israelis as reservists serve multiple tours due to the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.
"In whatever government is next formed, our immediate item is sorting out the status of Torah students," United Torah Judaism lawmaker Isaac Pindrus said.
Mr. Eisenkot, who has tried to appeal to secular Israelis from left to right, has been adamant about closing exemptions from military service.
Some of his Opposition allies have criticised the ultra-Orthodox, who make up about 14% of the population but have far higher birthrates than secular Israelis, as a drain on the State.

Observers say United Torah Judaism's tactic is likely aimed mostly at punishing Mr. Netanyahu and showing that their votes cannot be taken for granted, while they would still serve in a government if he were to form one.

articles.title: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's position weakens as ultra-Orthodox party withholds support
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Israel's October 27 election ended in deadlock with neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor his chief political ⁠rival Gadi Eisenkot securing a clear path to ‌a majority in Parliament

Benjamin Netanyahu's position in the post-election battle to stay on as Israel's Prime Minister weakened on ‌Thursday (November 5, 2026) after an ultra-Orthodox Jewish party withheld support for any nominee and an Arab-led party ​endorsed his main opponent.

Israel's President was due to meet Mr. Netanyahu and his chief political ⁠rival Gadi Eisenkot to decide which of the two men to pick to form a government, after holding consultations with smaller parties.
Israel's October 27 election ended in deadlock with neither Mr. Netanyahu nor Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief, securing a clear path to ‌a majority in Parliament.

That has set up a tough task for President Isaac Herzog, whose mostly ceremonial role comes with the post-election responsibility of picking a candidate he believes has ‌the best chance to break the deadlock in a deeply divided country.

Mr. Herzog has until November 11 ‌to ⁠decide. Mr. Netanyahu remains Prime Minister in a caretaker government until a new coalition is formed, ⁠or through another election which must be held if no candidate succeeds.
Though Mr. Netanyahu outperformed expectations in the vote and his own Likud Party won the most seats, his nationalist-religious coalition lost its governing majority.

In a setback for the Prime Minister on Thursday, United Torah Judaism, ​one of two major parties representing ultra-Orthodox Jewish ‌voters and a longstanding Netanyahu coalition ally, declined to recommend any candidate to form a government.

And while Mr. Eisenkot, like Mr. Netanyahu, has so far ruled out forming a government with Israel's two Arab-led parties, one of them endorsed Mr. Eisenkot on Thursday and the other was expected to do so later in the day.

Mr. Herzog will meet separately with Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Netanyahu ​at his residence in Jerusalem on Thursday night, wrapping up party meetings he started on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) after the announcement of official election results.

Mr. Herzog has called on parties to do their ⁠utmost to avert another round of elections. "Any reasonable person need only look at the security and diplomatic challenges before us, at the changing region around us, and remember the issues tearing us apart from within, to understand that ‌an immense responsibility rests upon us," Mr. Herzog said.
He met with smaller factions on Wednesday and plans more meetings with parties in ascending order by size, culminating with Mr. Eisenkot's Yashar and Mr. Netanyahu's Likud.
Likud won the most seats of any single party with 27 in the 120-seat Knesset, but Mr. Netanyahu's wider religious-nationalist coalition garnered only 53 in total.

fullParagraphs: The Union Petroleum Minister was declared elected after the nomination papers of two independent candidates, one of them backed by the Congress, were rejected; the Opposition had criticised his nomination over alleged links with Jeffrey Epstein

Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas Hardeep Singh Puri was on Thursday (November 5, 2026) elected for the Rajya Sabha unopposed from Madhya Pradesh in the byelection for a seat that fell vacant after the resignation of former Union Minister L. Murugan.

While the byelection was scheduled for Thursday (November 12, 2026), Mr. Puri’s election was declared on November 5 two days after the nomination papers of two independent candidates, one of them backed by the Congress, were rejected. November 5 was the last date to withdraw nominations.
Mr. Puri’s election certificate was received by Madhya Pradesh Bharatiya Janata Party president Hemant Khandelwal and Deputy Chief Minister Jagdish Devda at the State Legislative Assembly.
Mr. Puri was announced the BJP candidate for the byelection on October 28, weeks after Mr. Murugan, whose term was to end in 2030, gave up his membership of the Upper House.

His nomination received criticism from the Opposition Congress over Mr. Puri’s alleged links with the convicted U.S. sex offender and trafficker Jeffrey Epstein, as referenced in the files released in that country. The party also claimed that Mr. Murugan had been “forced to” resign to make way for Mr. Puri.
It had also challenged Mr. Puri’s nomination with the Returning Officer Umesh Sharma, alleging that his affidavit was “invalid” due to legal discrepancies.
His election to the Rajya Sabha, however, ends months of speculation over his exit from the Union Cabinet amid the Epstein Files controversy.

Mr. Puri is the only Sikh Minister in the BJP-led National Democratic Allaince government and his continuation in the Cabinet holds significance ahead of the Assembly elections in Punjab in early 2027, especially when BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu was dropped as a Minister in July 2026, after he did not secure a re-nomination for the Rajya Sabha.

articles.title: ‘It’s like a rebirth’: Rescuer-turned-survivor recounts ordeal after boats capsized in Telangana’s lake
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: After 10 personnel from State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and Fire Department scattered across Bethupalli Peddacheruvu in Khammam on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), three of them clung to a tree after two boats capsized.

One of them was an SDRF personnel, B. Naresh, who held on to the tree throughout the intervening night until the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) team rescued him and others early on Thursday. After surviving the ordeal, Mr. Naresh – whose one of the tasks is to rescue people from life threatening situations – said, “It is like a rebirth to me.”

A head constable of the Telangana State Special Police (TSSP)’s 6th Battalion near Kothagudem, Mr. Naresh recounted his terrifying experiences as he reunited with his family members, who had spent an anxious night at the rescue site awaiting his safe return.

Mr. Naresh was among the 10 rescue personnel who were swept away by the gushing floodwaters when two boats capsized during an operation to rescue six fishermen stranded in the lake on Wednesday evening. All the missing personnel as well as nine stranded fishermen were eventually rescued after a strenuous search operation that continued for more than 12 hours.

“Soon after we ventured into the lake in two boats at around 7 p.m. on Wednesday, the water level suddenly rose and the currents became very strong. I, along with two others, jumped into the water just before the boats capsized under the impact of the strong currents. We managed to climb a tree and spent the entire night there amid the raging floodwaters. An NDRF team finally rescued us just before dawn,” Naresh recalled.
Another SDRF personnel recounted how he clung to a tree branch after being swept nearly half-a-kilometer away from the spot where the boats capsized, towards the far end of the lake.

The rescuers wearing life jackets managed to stay afloat before grabbing tree branches along the lake’s course, said a police official who was part of the rescue operation. Their training and perseverance helped them survive until rescue teams reached them, he added.

Officials suspected that a breach in a minor irrigation tank upstream might have contributed to the sudden surge in the water level in Bhupali Peddacheruvu following heavy rainfall triggered by Cyclone Murasu. The strong currents and sudden rise in water levels were believed to have led to the capsizing of the two boats.

The NDRF, SDRF, and Fire Services personnel jointly carried out the strenuous search-and-rescue operation and eventually ensured the safe return of all those caught in the floodwaters. Khammam Collector Divakara T.S. supervised the operation.

Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy visited Bethuapalli Peddacheruvu on Thursday morning, lauded the rescue teams for their tireless efforts and felicitated the personnel involved in the operation.

articles.title: ZPTC, MPTC elections in Andhra Pradesh by and large peaceful
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1.5 crore (58.55%) voters exercised their franchise in 30,994 polling stations by 3 p.m; stray incidents reported in Kadapa, Chittoor and some other districts

Elections to 582 Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs) in the State conducted on Thursday were by and large peaceful barring sporadic incidents of violence, notably in the Rayalaseema region.
Of the 2,53,96,669 voters, 1,48,70,495 (58.55%) exercised their franchise in 30,994 polling stations by 3 p.m. as per the information furnished by the State Election Commission (SEC).

Those standing in queue lines at the close of polling (5 p.m.) at several places were given extra time to cast their votes. A total of 2,169 candidates were in the fray for the ZPTCs. The total number of ZPTCs is 659, of which 77 candidates were declared as unanimously elected.

There were stray incidents in Kadapa, Chittoor and some other districts, including the reported hurling of petrol bombs near a polling station near Pulivendula. Police personnel swung into action and dispersed the clashing activists of the TDP and the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP). Stone-throwing was reported in Jammalamadugu, Rajampeta, Railway Kodur and Badvel areas.

Tension prevailed in the Kotia group of villages bordering Odisha as a large number of supporters of various parties tried to obstruct polling due to a simmering dispute over which State the villages belong to. These villages fall in Salur constituency of Parvatipuram - Manyam district as per the States Reorganisation Act of 1956.

Polling was incident-free in the Maoist-affected areas in Polavaram and East Godavari dstricts, where special care was taken to transport voters to the polling stations which were not easily accessible. Heavy rain caused by the Murasu cyclone played spoilsport at many places as low-lying areas were inundated.

Voting took place amidst tight security arrangements made at 8,904 sensitive and 7,160 hypersensitive polling stations, a majority of which are in Rayalaseema, where violence marred the filing of nominations for elections to the Urban Local Bodies (ULBs).

A total of 7,767 Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTCs) went to polls, where 18,843 candidates were in the arena. The number of MPTCs is 9,821, of which 2,051 candidates were unanimously elected.
Earlier in the day, State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha inspected the voting at various polling stations in NTR and Krishna districts.

articles.title: Banned tobacco products worth ₹7 crore seized in Ernakulam; seven held
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Contraband was seized in a midnight raid conductedat a warehouse in Aluva
The Ernakulam Rural police seized banned tobacco products worth around ₹7 crore from Keezhmad in Aluva and arrested seven persons.
The arrested are alleged kingpin Ayub, 40, of Uliyannoor in Aluva, and Jagaram, 22, Narpat Lal, 28, Bawar Ram, 20, Anil Kumar, 19, Bavesh Kumar, 19, and Swaroop Ram20, all natives of Rajasthan.

The contraband was seized in a midnight raid conducted on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) at a warehouse in the Chakkamkulangara area of Fourth Mile, Keezhmad, based on a confidential tip-off received by District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) K.S. Sudarsan. Banned tobacco products were allegedly found stacked in sacks inside the godown.

The investigation team was led by Mr. Sudarsan and included Narcotics Cell DySP C. Binukumar, Aluva DYSP Baiju Paulose, Circle Inspector P.M. Shameer, and Edathala Station House Officer S.S. Sreelal, among others.

Superintendent of Police Shelke Nachiket Vishwanath visited the polling stations in Vemula mandal and inspected the security arrangements on the ground. He instructed the police personnel to remain vigilant and ensure that the elections are conducted in a peaceful and impartial manner.

The polling commenced in the district from 7 a.m. and concluded by 6.30 p.m.. Special security arrangements were made at 167 highly sensitive, 134 sensitive, and five problematic polling stations. Except few areas, the voting was peaceful with 71.78% turnout.

In the polling held for 55 MPTC seats, 2.06 lakh out of 3 lakh voters cast their votes, recording a turnout of 68.74%.

articles.title: CBG blending at 1.7% in H1; pipeline connectivity key to achieving 3% target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: India has a target of blending 3% CBG into D-PNG and CNG by the end of current fiscal, 4% in 2027-28 and 5% in the subsequent year.

India achieved 1.7% blending of compressed biogas (CBG) with domestic piped natural gas (D-PNG) and vehicular compressed natural gas (CNG) in the first half of the current fiscal, but will need an acceleration in sales during the second half to meet the mandated 3% target, according to the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB).
The country has set a blending target of 4% for 2027-28, rising to 5% in the subsequent fiscal.

CBG sales stood at 115.9 million standard cubic metres (MMSCM) during the April-September period, against combined CNG and D-PNG sales of 6,800 MMSCM. With the combined consumption of the two fuels projected at 13,600 MMSCM for the full fiscal, CBG sales will have to rise to 408 MMSCM to achieve the 3% blending target, requiring an additional 292.1 MMSCM over the first-half volume.
Flagging infrastructure gaps, PNGRB stressed the need to connect CBG plants to gas pipelines to ensure assured offtake and better utilisation of installed capacity.

Of the 210 functional CBG plants in the country, capacity utilisation averages just 44%. More significantly, 247 of the 308 plants under construction currently have no plans for pipeline connectivity.

“A reliable pipeline connection gives CBG plant a buyer every day of the year. Plants with a pipeline, or one being built, use 65-69% of their designed capacity. Better pipeline access means better gas offtake and overall use of every plant,” it said.

Besides expanding pipeline infrastructure, the regulator called on larger entities to establish their own CBG blending targets, increase procurement from independent producers and invest in setting up captive CBG plants.

articles.title: ONGC Q2 net profit jumps 57% on higher crude, gas realisations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Along with the results, the company declared an interim dividend of ₹8 per equity share.

State-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) reported a 57.3% year-on-year (YoY) surge in standalone net profit to ₹15,489 crore for the quarter ended September, supported by higher realisations from crude oil and natural gas.
The company also declared an interim dividend of ₹8 per equity share.

ONGC’s crude oil realisation rose to $92.33 per barrel from $67.34 a barrel in the year-ago quarter. Gas prices from nominated fields increased to $7 per million British thermal units (MMBTU) from $6.75 per MMBTU.
Realisation from new-well gas, previously identified by Chairman Arun Kumar Singh as a key driver of profitability going ahead, climbed to $10.24 per MMBTU against $8.36 per MMBTU a year earlier.
Revenue for the quarter grew 32.8% YoY to ₹43,875 crore.

However, production remained under pressure. Standalone crude oil output declined 4.2% to 4.437 million metric tonnes (MMT), while natural gas production fell 1.6% to 4.839 billion cubic metres (BCM).

Explaining the production dip, ONGC said, “The year-on-year moderation in quarterly production was primarily attributable to reservoir behaviour complexities in KG-98/2 Asset in Eastern Offshore Basin, coupled with monsoon related operational challenges and associated delays in PRP-8 and PRP-9 (Pipeline replacement projects).”
The company added that onshore gas production was affected by lower customer offtake and disruptions at certain major consumer facilities, which temporarily dampened demand.

articles.title: NPCI says MDR charge has been imposed to save the UPI ecosystem from turning ouroboric
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Zero MDR is no longer sustainable; the magnitude of growth places correspondingly greater demands on the security, resilience, and infrastructural capacity of the system, NCPI tells SC

National Payments Corporation of India (NCPI) has said in the Supreme Court that “zero Merchant Discount Rate (MDR)” for all Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions was no longer sustainable, as functional costs for the phenomenally expanding digital payment industry in India would burn into the public exchequer.

UPI processed as many as 24.51 billion transactions, cumulatively worth approximately ₹29.82 lakh crore, in the month of August 2026 alone, marking its highest-ever monthly volume. An average of approximately 791 million transactions were processed every single day in that month. In Financial Year 2025-26, UPI processed approximately 241.62 billion transactions worth approximately ₹314 lakh crore, the NPCI said.

“The figures illustrate not merely growth, but growth of a magnitude that places correspondingly greater demands on the security, resilience, and infrastructural capacity of the system,” the NPCI, represented by Additional Solicitor General N. Venkataraman, submitted in Court.
The Corporation was responding to a challenge in Court to the government’s decision to introduce an MDR of 0.4% on Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above ₹2,000.

Person to person (P2P) transactions, which account for 70% of total UPI transaction value, would remain completely free irrespective of amount, the NCPI said. There would be no transaction or platform fee or other charge permissible for individuals for sending or receiving money through UPI, it added.

It said person-to-merchant (P2M) payments up to ₹2,000 would also remain “entirely free of MDR”. “This threshold is calibrated to shield the overwhelming majority of everyday, low-value merchant payments of the kind made by ordinary consumers and small merchants alike,” the NPCI said.
The affidavit assured that the amended MDR framework targeted only higher value commerce without disturbing low-value transactions that drive the mass adoption of UPI.

The MDR charge, which did not exceed 0.4%, would apply to P2M transactions above ₹2000. “Effectively, MDR will apply to only about 4% of merchant transactions, and approximately 96% of all P2M will remain unaffected,” the NPCI said.
The NPCI countered the petitioners’ contention that an amended MDR framework should have been introduced only through a new legislation and not just through a notification in September.

The NCPI argued that MDR was not a tax, cess, fee, duty or any other statutory levy imposed by or under a legislative enactment. It was plainly a ‘charge’ collected to recover the huge costs associated with the functioning of the payment system, and was in turn, distributed entirely amongst the participants in the UPI ecosystem.

“MDR is a charge collected by the system participants to recover the costs incurred in running the payment system, and not an imposition pursuant to any delegation of legislative or fiscal power by Parliament, the Central Government or RBI,” the NPCI submitted.

In a 100-page affidavit, the NPCI said that, as a system provider, it had the liberty to determine the MDR applicable to transactions processed through the payment system operated by it, subject to the regulatory framework of the Reserve Bank of India and the prohibition under Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, which exempts UPI transactions below ₹2000 from any charges.

Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, ousted in a mass uprising in 2024, has told The Associated Press that she remains committed to returning to Bangladesh from exile in India next month, despite being sentenced to death over her government's deadly crackdown on protesters.
Ms. Hasina fled to India after student-led protests forced her from power and has remained there ever since.

In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity, ruling that she was responsible for ordering the crackdown, which left hundreds of people dead and thousands of others injured.

The United Nations has said in a report that nearly 1,400 people were killed. Ms. Hasina denies any wrongdoing. She has also rejected the tribunal's verdict and challenged the legitimacy of the trial.
Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Ms. Hasina's extradition, but India has declined to hand her over. She had first announced in August her intention to return in December.

“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” she told The Associated Press in response to questions by email. “So, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed.”
Questions were submitted to her last week and she responded on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Ms. Hasina, who was Prime Minister from 2009-2024, didn't disclose how she plans to return from India. She could face arrest upon arrival in Bangladesh.

“I know that I may be arrested when I return. I may be imprisoned, tortured or even killed. I am fully aware of those possibilities. But I cannot spend the rest of my life watching my people suffer from a distance,” she told the AP .
Following Ms. Hasina's ouster, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus took charge of an interim administration, leading the country for the next 18 months.

In February, Tarique Rahman, son of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia and a longtime political rival of Ms. Hasina, swept to power in a landslide election held under Mr. Yunus' administration. Ms. Hasina's Awami League party was barred from contesting the vote.

The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in ‌Yemen said it destroyed a missile launched by the group towards Islam's holy city of ‌Medina. The kingdom's civil defence also issued emergency ‌alerts ⁠for the southeastern area of Sharurah ⁠that borders Yemen.
The Houthis had yet to claim any attack on the kingdom on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

They said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) they had ​attacked Riyadh's International Airport while ‌Syria's President Ahmed al-Sharaa visited the kingdom. Saudi authorities have not confirmed the attack.
The Syrian leader witnessed the signing of a defence agreement alongside Crown ‌Prince Mohammed — their second meeting in Saudi ​Arabia in less than a month.
No details were provided on what the agreement ⁠entails. Reuters reported last month that Damascus was carefully weighing providing military assistance to Riyadh.

Saudi Arabia, the ‌world's biggest oil exporter and a key U.S. ally, has been requesting assistance from countries ranging from the U.S. to Europe and the West Asia, for both defensive and offensive support in its renewed war against the powerful Yemeni militia.
Egypt last ‌month gave approval for its military, one of the region's ​biggest, to provide help to the kingdom.

Meanwhile, Turkey is set to ratify a ⁠mutual defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan that ⁠includes a collective defence clause, committing NATO's second-largest army to Riyadh's defence. articles.title: Iran says five tankers, tugboat caught fire in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: British monitor UKMTO reported a tanker being struck by "two unidentified projectiles" around 50 nautical miles (90 kilometres) off the north coast of Qatar, without providing details on any damage or casualties
Five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards and army said in separate statements, according to local media on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
It regularly attacks ships it accuses of transiting without its authorisation.
The United States military has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait.

"Last night... a large oil tanker attempting to pass through the illegal passageway south of the Strait of Hormuz suffered a fire after striking a mine and was brought to a halt," the Guards told Fars news agency.
"Another supertanker was halted by a massive fire while exiting the eastern Strait of Hormuz. A tugboat that had approached the supertanker to extinguish the fire also caught fire," the Guards said.
The Iranian army later said three more tankers were hit by naval mines.

"Early this morning, a violating oil tanker — navigating through an unsafe area east of the Strait of Hormuz — caught fire and came to a halt after striking a naval mine," the army said, according to the official IRNA news agency.
"Today at around noon, two more oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the unsafe waters east of the Strait of Hormuz," said another army statement carried by IRNA .
There has been no confirmation of the incidents from maritime officials.

British monitor UKMTO reported a tanker being struck by "two unidentified projectiles" around 50 nautical miles (90 kilometres) off the north coast of Qatar, without providing details on any damage or casualties.
That area is around 500 kilometres west of Hormuz, in the centre of the Gulf.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections 2026 LIVE: Democrats vow to rein in Trump as he shows off White House ballroom
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Indian-American physician Amish Shah has made history after becoming the first from the community to represent Arizona in Congress
Mexican ‌President Claudia Sheinbaum on ⁠Thursday said it was “very ‌likely” and “logical” that raids ‌and ‌racism ⁠against ⁠immigrants influenced the Latino vote in U.S. ‌midterm elections.
Democrats won control of ‌Congress in Tuesday’s elections, making gains ⁠deep in Republican-held ‌districts as voters delivered a rebuke to ‌President Donald Trump and his agenda.- Reuters

Following the drubbing of U.S. President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections, Iranians set fire to a giant poster featuring the American leader and his allies at a rally in Tehran.
The cheering audience waved red flags to demand revenge for Khamenei’s death.
“We will kill Trump,” read the slogan on some of the flags waved by the crowd as a song named “We Must Rise” mourning Khamenei blared from nearby speakers.

As Washington navigates the fallout from a sweeping Republican electoral defeat, Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the U.S., Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has launched a blistering critique of American leadership, accusing officials of bringing “losing gambler energy” to the table while America teeters on an “Israel-First cliff”.

In a post on X, Mr. Ghalibaf wrote, “Losing gambler energy, can’t walk away from the table. Boss is prepping the next war phase while America teeters on an Israel-First cliff. Skip the TED talk. Why not say this to your boss?”

Democrats vowed to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in President Donald Trump, setting up two years of possible deadlock in Washington, as Mr. Trump spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom.
It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Wednesday (November 4) that the incoming majority would be focused on affordability and accountability.

Mr. Trump’s announcement showed that even the Republican President, who moved the American embassy to Jerusalem in his first term, cracked down on pro-Palestine protests at home and launched a war, along with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, against Iran, recognised the growing electoral liability of unconditional support for Israel.

The midterm results could accelerate this political churn. The Democrats have secured control of both the House and the Senate. The election was fought largely on domestic issues, particularly the economy and the cost of living, but the war on Iran and its impact on the economy, particularly fuel prices, also figured in the Republican setback. Mr. Trump himself acknowledged that the war had hurt his party.
