articles.title: ISRO’s latest navigation satellite NVS-03 is fully healthy, says Chairman V. Narayanan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: ISRO to conduct in-orbit testing for satellite payload as part of developing NavIC, an indigenous GPS alternative; ISRO chief recalls Indian scientists’ role in saving lives on the Axiom-4 mission; praises Russian support of India’s space programme

ISRO’s next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03, launched on October 30 to strengthen India’s NavIC regional satellite navigation system, is “fully healthy”, ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

Speaking at the inauguration of the statue of legendary astronaut Yuri Gagarin at the Periyar Science and Technology Centre, Mr. Narayanan said, “NVS-03, successfully launched on October 30 midnight, was perfectly placed in the elliptical orbit. From there, we operated the engine of the satellite for 6,400 seconds to the circular orbit. Right now, the satellite is fully healthy. We have to do a lot of in-orbit testing for the satellite payload and others.”

Mr. Narayanan recounted ISRO’s role in ensuring the success of the Axiom-4 mission this summer, which was piloted by Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, the first Indian in space in the last 40 years. Indian scientists had saved the lives of all the astronauts aboard by insisting on scrubbing the initially scheduled launch due to a liquid oxygen leak.

“One day ahead of the scheduled launch on June 11, the countdown had started, and there was a news item about a minor leak. We went ahead with a discussion. I was not satisfied. We insisted on correcting it. Later, we found it was a line crack, not a minor leak,” the ISRO chief explained. “We proved to the world that Indians are second to none, the Indian education system is second to none, Indian training is second to none, to ensure the safety of Gaganyatris [astronauts], including Shubhanshu Shukla,” he added.
The ISRO chief stressed the need to strengthen space technology for better services for citizens. “The work on the fourth launch complex in Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu is under way,” he said.

The ISRO chief recalled Russia’s historic role in boosting India’s space programme. “Then-USSR, and the present Russia has supported us in the space programme a great deal. Using the term MTCR [or Missile Technology Control Regime], nobody was willing to help us. At that point in time, the then-USSR came forward, they were ready to give hardware. USSR was the first country that helped our country send Rakesh Sharma to space and return safely,” said Mr. Narayanan, who spent ten months in Russia in 1993 learning cryogenic technology.

“Today also, we are getting a lot of support. For the Gaganyaan programme also, they are supporting us. We are collaborating in multiple areas. We should not forget the ladder after we have climbed up,” he added.
Russia’s Consul General in Chennai, Valerii Khodzhaev, also said that India and Russia had a “long-lasting relationship.”

articles.title: Postcards from Earth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Voyager I’s forty-nine-year journey into the void

Somewhere above the plane in which the planets orbit, moving away from the sun at some 17 kilometres a second, a machine older than the internet is closing in on no ordinary milestone. On November 18, Voyager I will be one light-day away from earth.

In 1965, a graduate student in the U.S. named Gary Flandro noticed that around the late 1970s, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune would lie on a single line — something that happens only around every 175 years. So, a spacecraft launched at the right moment could use each planet's gravity to arc towards the next, compressing a 30-year crawl to Neptune into a single decade.
NASA dreamed big at first, but as the budget priorities changed, the plan shrank to two probes aimed only at Jupiter and Saturn. These were the Voyagers.

Scientists and engineers built two nearly identical spacecraft, and launched them 16 days apart: Voyager II first on August 20, 1977, then Voyager I. As it happened, Voyager I would take a faster path that let it overtake its sibling and reach Jupiter first. And from here the two machines lived very different lives.

Voyager I is built like a decagon-shaped drum to pack the electronics and the propellant tank into a light frame. Sixteen thrusters keep a 3.7-metre dish antenna pointing at earth. Three nuclear generators sit at the end of a long boom to keep their radioactivity from corrupting the instruments.
The Voyagers couldn't afford a gram of decoration. They're purely functional objects.
Voyager I and Voyager II each carry a golden phonograph record bolted to their exteriors.

The idea was that the mission ought to carry some kind of message explaining ourselves and our planet to any interstellar intelligence it may encounter that shared none of our biology, language, or history.

Project manager John Casani handed the problem of designing a message to Carl Sagan, who invited the radio astronomer Frank Drake. Their official budget was $1,500 for six weeks — an absurd sum for a message meant to represent an entire species, and in practice it took most of the following year to compose.

They assembled 116 photographs of human anatomy, cities, farms, a mother nursing a child, the structure of DNA, a 12-minute audio collage of surf, thunder, birdsong, humpback whales, and a baby's first cry; greetings in more than 50 languages; and 90 minutes of music from Bach to a Navajo night chant to Chuck Berry's 'Johnny B. Goode'.

At Sagan's request, the documentary maker Ann Druyan spent an hour in a lab with electrodes on her scalp, thinking her way through the history of earth. Two days after she and Sagan had privately agreed to marry, she thought of what it felt like to fall in love. That hour of brain activity was encoded onto the record as sound as well.

Whimsical though it sounds, the record's design posed a significant challenge: how do you write instructions for an alien entity with a different alphabet, units or even senses? So its designers picked something universal: physics. The playback speed was set by the oscillation of a hydrogen atom, location marked by a map of pulsars, the cover plated with uranium-238, whose decay lets a finder calculate exactly how long it has been travelling.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: on India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme. And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Trump debacle: on the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Democrats must use their win to influence policy and improve lives

President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. articles.title: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, a joint press release stated

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on Thursday (November 5, 2026) met Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu, with discussions focused on “possible outcomes and initiatives” from the upcoming visit of the Himalayan nation’s leader to New Delhi.
Concluding his official engagements in Nepal that spanned Wednesday and Thursday, Mr. Misri also met Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal.

“The Foreign Secretary of India highlighted the wide-ranging engagement and overall progress in diverse areas of bilateral cooperation, and discussed possible outcomes and initiatives in the context of the upcoming visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India,” stated a joint press release issued by the Ministry of External Affairs and Kathmandu’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Mr. Misri held detailed talks with his host, Nepali Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, on the “mutually beneficial partnership” between India and Nepal.

Mr. Shah had earlier this year highlighted the border dispute with India in the Lipulekh-Kalapai-Limpiyadhura area that is part of India’s Uttarakhand but claimed by Nepal as a sticking point in ties.
Mr. Shah had sought to involve other countries, such as the United Kingdom and China, in talks on the issue. But India wants the matter to be resolved bilaterally.
The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, the joint press release stated.

Mr. Misri’s discussions with Nepali stakeholders included a “commerce and development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management, energy and people-to-people ties”, as well as new areas like digital connectivity and AI.
Mr. Misri also met Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal.
Mr. Shah was sworn in as Prime Minister in March this year following the Gen-Z uprising in Nepal in September 2025 that led to the ouster of the previous government.

fullParagraphs: Indian-American physician Amish Shah has made history after becoming the first from the community to represent Arizona in Congress
Mexican ‌President Claudia Sheinbaum on ⁠Thursday said it was “very ‌likely” and “logical” that raids ‌and ‌racism ⁠against ⁠immigrants influenced the Latino vote in U.S. ‌midterm elections.
Democrats won control of ‌Congress in Tuesday’s elections, making gains ⁠deep in Republican-held ‌districts as voters delivered a rebuke to ‌President Donald Trump and his agenda.- Reuters

Following the drubbing of U.S. President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections, Iranians set fire to a giant poster featuring the American leader and his allies at a rally in Tehran.
The cheering audience waved red flags to demand revenge for Khamenei’s death.
“We will kill Trump,” read the slogan on some of the flags waved by the crowd as a song named “We Must Rise” mourning Khamenei blared from nearby speakers.

As Washington navigates the fallout from a sweeping Republican electoral defeat, Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the U.S., Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has launched a blistering critique of American leadership, accusing officials of bringing “losing gambler energy” to the table while America teeters on an “Israel-First cliff”.

In a post on X, Mr. Ghalibaf wrote, “Losing gambler energy, can’t walk away from the table. Boss is prepping the next war phase while America teeters on an Israel-First cliff. Skip the TED talk. Why not say this to your boss?”

Democrats vowed to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in President Donald Trump, setting up two years of possible deadlock in Washington, as Mr. Trump spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom.
It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Wednesday (November 4) that the incoming majority would be focused on affordability and accountability.

Mr. Trump’s announcement showed that even the Republican President, who moved the American embassy to Jerusalem in his first term, cracked down on pro-Palestine protests at home and launched a war, along with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, against Iran, recognised the growing electoral liability of unconditional support for Israel.

The midterm results could accelerate this political churn. The Democrats have secured control of both the House and the Senate. The election was fought largely on domestic issues, particularly the economy and the cost of living, but the war on Iran and its impact on the economy, particularly fuel prices, also figured in the Republican setback. Mr. Trump himself acknowledged that the war had hurt his party.

articles.title: Iranians burn giant poster of Trump and allies, demand revenge

fullParagraphs: In the capital's central Enghelab square, crowds gathered to observe the burning of the poster featuring U.S. President Donald Trump, his Vice President J. D. Vance, special envoy Steve Witkoff, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu

Following the drubbing of U.S. President Donald Trump's Republican Party in the midterm elections, Iranians set fire to a giant poster featuring the American leader and his allies at a rally in Tehran.

In the capital's central Enghelab square, crowds gathered to observe the burning of the poster which also featured his Vice President J. D. Vance, special envoy Steve Witkoff and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The war was started by Mr. Trump and Mr. Netanyahu, who launched a massive wave of surprise attacks against Iran which killed supreme leader Ayatollah Khamenei and others on February 28 and sparked the wider West Asia war.
The cheering audience waved red flags to demand revenge for Khamenei's death.
"We will kill Trump," read the slogan on some of the flags waved by the crowd as a song named "We Must Rise" mourning Khamenei blared from nearby speakers.
Earlier, thousands of Iranians had mocked Mr. Trump at an annual rally commemorating the U.S. embassy takeover and hostage crisis that followed the 1979 Islamic revolution.
Wednesday's (November 4, 2026) public displays took place following the Republicans' crushing losses in the midterm elections in which the Democrats seized control of Congress.
Mr. Trump admitted that the war he launched with Israel against Iran in February was a key factor in the electoral defeat.

Iranian officials have since taunted the U.S. President, with security chief Mohsen Rezaei saying it marked a "political defeat" after Tehran "handed Trump a strategic defeat on the battlefield and in the Hormuz" strait.

OpenAI has announced a set of commitments for communities hosting its future AI data-centre campuses in the United States, pledging to bear the full cost of electricity and grid infrastructure, disclose environmental impacts and not use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials, subject to limited exceptions.

In an announcement on November 5, 2026, the company published its National Community Compact, setting out commitments for future computing campuses it owns and operates in the U.S., and a separate Compute Campus Policy Blueprint proposing measures for governments to make data-centre developers more accountable to local communities.

“We’ll pay the full cost of the electricity we use and the infrastructure needed to serve us,” OpenAI said. It added that it would provide financial assurances to protect other electricity consumers if a project were delayed, reduced or cancelled.

The electricity commitment builds on assurances the company had made for individual projects, including its Stargate initiative. The latest announcement seeks to establish a common set of commitments for future campuses it owns and operates in the U.S.

OpenAI also committed to developing a water plan for each campus, prioritising closed-loop or low-water cooling systems, and publishing site-level water and electricity consumption. It said it would publish construction plans and independent noise studies before operations begin and annually thereafter.
The company said it would not use NDAs with public officials, with narrow exceptions for legitimate security information, trade secrets, and proprietary or competitively sensitive information.

On employment, OpenAI said it would publish expected job creation, work with unions and training providers to prepare local residents for employment opportunities, and report annually on hiring and apprenticeships. It also pledged to make sustained investments in priorities identified by local communities.

Alongside these commitments, OpenAI released a Compute Campus Policy Blueprint proposing measures for federal, state and local governments to make data-centre developers more accountable. The blueprint calls for large electricity consumers to pay for the additional grid infrastructure and power costs they create, and proposes measures to protect consumers if projects are abandoned.
It also calls for greater transparency on tax incentives offered to data-centre developers, including measurable commitments and mechanisms to recover benefits if companies fail to meet them.

Citing its planned campus in Effingham County, Georgia, OpenAI said its agreement with Georgia Power allows the utility to reduce electricity supplied to the facility by up to 1,000 megawatts during periods of high demand.

The announcement comes against a backdrop of growing political and public opposition to data-centre expansion in the U.S., an issue that featured in the November 3, 2026 midterm elections. However, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane told Reuters that the policy measures had been in development since August, before the elections. The company had also begun outlining community commitments under its Stargate initiative in January. The issue is also becoming relevant in India, which is attracting large investments in AI infrastructure.

Here, OpenAI has partnered with Tata Group and TCS to develop AI infrastructure in India through TCS’s HyperVault business, with an initial capacity of 100 MW and the potential to scale to 1 GW. OpenAI will be the first customer. Meta has agreed to lease capacity at a 168 MW AI-enabled data centre that Reliance Industries is developing in Jamnagar, Gujarat. Google is also developing a gigawatt-scale AI hub in Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, as part of a planned $15-billion investment in India.

articles.title: Business, unusual: On engaging with the Myanmar junta
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Engaging with the Myanmar junta is a short-sighted move

Months after a sham election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as Myanmar’s civilian President, the military continues to wage war on its own people even as the world has largely looked away. More than a lakh people are estimated to have died since the 2021 coup, many in fighting between the junta and the anti-coup People’s Defence Forces and ethnic armed organisations. The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance. With wars affecting Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan and Yemen, and Iran, the world has grown numb to such violence. The junta has exploited that indifference and a shifting geopolitical situation to act with impunity. Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians. Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory. It also backed the January election. Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India , Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states. ASEAN still swears by its Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence and dialogue. Yet, its members seem more than eager to do business with a regime that has flouted every point. Meanwhile, U.S. officials reportedly held secret talks with the junta in Tokyo in June and October, and a senior delegation met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw in September. Japan is reportedly pressing the Financial Action Task Force to take Myanmar off its blacklist.

The motives are not hard to understand. China wants an outlet to the Indian Ocean and security for its oil and gas pipelines. It has also played both sides, dealing with the junta and powerful rebel groups such as the Kachin Independence Organisation, whose territory is rich in rare earths and jade, and the United Wa State Army, which runs a massive tin mine. New Delhi wants to revive its stalled Act East policy, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project. The U.S. eyes access to mining vital heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium, for use in electric vehicles and weapons systems. What these short-sighted overtures miss is that trade thrives in a country at peace, not one where armed groups are perennially battling for control. The junta which has killed its citizens and has scuttled every move towards democracy cannot deliver that peace. Unless the generals are made to answer for their war crimes, Myanmar will remain a war zone. It will be ruinous not only for its hapless people but also for businesses seeking to trade with it.

articles.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Binance’s reaction to the hack shows how the crypto industry has matured

The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself. Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.

So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. If the fear is that cryptocurrencies are not backed by any asset, then Indian policymakers can choose to allow only stablecoins, which do have real assets underpinning them. Indians are not at higher risk from cryptos than they are from fake stock market scams. The best defence is awareness. By refusing to regulate the crypto space in India and, indeed, taxing it at a prohibitive rate, the government is driving Indians towards either the black market, where such scams proliferate, or foreign exchanges. The government can take a leaf out of Binance’s book and mandate an industry-maintained emergency fund. There is ample international legislation to emulate now. The point is, crypto risks have fallen and adoption is rising. Now is the time to regulate the industry.

articles.summary: Binance’s reaction to the hack shows how the crypto industry has matured
articles.keyPoints:
• Binance’s reaction to the hack shows how the crypto industry has matured
• The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself. Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.
• So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. If the fear is that cryptocurrencies are not backed by any asset, then Indian policymakers can choose to allow only stablecoins, which do have real assets underpinning them. Indians are not at higher risk from cryptos than they are from fake stock market scams. The best defence is awareness. By refusing to regulate the crypto space in India and, indeed, taxing it at a prohibitive rate, the government is driving Indians towards either the black market, where such scams proliferate, or foreign exchanges. The government can take a leaf out of Binance’s book and mandate an industry-maintained emergency fund. There is ample international legislation to emulate now. The point is, crypto risks have fallen and adoption is rising. Now is the time to regulate the industry.

articles.title: DVAC conducts drone survey of irrigation tank in illegal sand mining charge against DMK’s E.V. Velu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) conducted a drone survey of an irrigation tank in Malappambadi village near Tiruvannamalai in connection with allegations of illegal sand mining by former PWD and Highways Minister and senior DMK leader E.V. Velu for the party’s Northern Zone Youth Wing Conference held on December 14, 2025.

DVAC sources said that the drone survey was conducted in coordination with the Revenue Department, Tiruvannamalai Corporation, and the police to assess the extent of damage done to the water body. It will also provide total depth and width of the tank that was mined for the purpose. by illegal sand mining. The survey was monitored by Ganesan, Deputy SP, DVAC (Ranipet), K.Selvam, Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO), Tiruvannamalai, and K. Balasubramanian, Corporation Commissioner.

The assessment comes in the wake of a complaint filed by Arappor Iyakkam , an NGO, with the DVAC at its headquarters in Chennai on August 13 this year. The complaint alleged that large volumes of sand was illegally mined from the irrigation tank reportedly based on directions by the then PWD and Highways Minister Mr. Velu. The sand theft has reportedly incurred a loss to a tune of ₹8 crore to State exchequer, the complainant claimed.

The sand was mined to reportedly level an open land of 124.56 acres, to organise the DMK’s conference. The conference was attended by former Chief Minister and DMK president M.K. Stalin and his son and former Deputy Chief Minister Udhayanidhi Stalin.

The complaint also alleged that Mr. Velu, who was appointed as DMK’s northern zonal in-charge for 2026 Assembly polls, for personally overseeing and directing the logistical arrangements for the conference. “The sand from the tank bed was illegally mined to a depth of around 10 feet to 23 feet to an extent around 12 acres as against the permissible limit of one metre in depth under Tamil Nadu Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1959. The excavated sand can be used only for local agricultural, pottery and domestic purposes,” the complaint said.

articles.title: Probe launched into derailment of goods wagons at Jolarpet Railway Station
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Southern Railway has ordered an inquiry into the derailment of seven goods wagons at a yard near Jolarpet Railway Station in Tirupattur.
Railway officials said that seven wagons got derailed for around 400 metres, when the train was being moved from a loop line to the main line in the yard near the railway station.

Railway officials said that no untoward incident happened as the route towards Bengaluru, where the derailment occurred, had less traffic movement. The incident occurred around 7.15 p.m. on November 1.

Railway officials said that the Bengaluru SBC to Jolarpet JTJ MEMU train was short-terminated at Somanayakkanpti Railway Station in Tirupattur. Senior officials and engineering crews from the Salem and Chennai railway divisions immediately rushed to the spot to restore train services, which resumed around 12.30 a.m. on November 1.
This is the second incident after five wagons of an empty goods train, coming from Chennai port, derailed at Kethandapatti village near Jolarpet Railway Station in November, 2024.

articles.title: Rajanna is free to quit party if he wishes: Balakrishna
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress leader and Minister for Municipal Administration H.C. Balakrishna lashed out at senior Congress leader and MLA K.N. Rajanna on Tuesday, saying he was free to quit the party if he so wished, and accusing him of “betraying the party while being part of it.”
This comes against the backdrop of Mr. Rajanna’s son and MLC R. Rajendra recently meeting JD(S) leader and Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy.

Speaking to reporters in Chitradurga, he said, “If Mr. Rajanna wants to leave the party and join another party, he is free to do so. Let him honestly answer whether his son contested the election fairly. The election process had not even concluded when he posed for a photograph with Mr. Kumaraswamy. If the Congress party does not pay attention to such issues, it may have to face serious problems in the future. Mr. Rajanna is betraying the party while remaining in it. The party does not belong to any one individual. He has engaged in anti-party activities, and strict action should be taken against him. We will lodge a complaint against Mr. Rajanna with the party high command.”

articles.title: Bengaluru: South corporation shuts 63 commercial establishments in residential layouts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bengaluru South City Corporation has sealed 63 commercial establishments operating “illegally” in residential areas across its jurisdiction during a special enforcement drive conducted by officials.

The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut. This was followed by 10 in the Bengaluru South constituency, nine in Bommanahalli, eight in Padmanabhanagar, four in Jayanagar, and two within the limits of the Anekal Assembly constituency (part of which falls under the South City Corporation).

According to Corporation officials, the action targeted commercial establishments operating in residential areas in violation of regulations. Officials said they were causing inconvenience to residents and obstructing vehicular movement. Bakeries, eateries, condiment stores, salons, beauty parlours, fruit and vegetable outlets, hardware stores, and other commercial establishments were among those sealed.

The Corporation said commercial establishments operating on roads narrower than 40 feet in residential areas were prohibited. However, several establishments had continued operations without valid trade licences despite being issued notices and instructions to vacate.

The drive was conducted simultaneously across several wards in Kumaraswamy Layout, J.P. Nagar, Madiwala, Koramangala, Ejipura, Jakkasandra, Begur, Singasandra, Yelachenahalli, Uttarahalli, Gottigere, Bilekahalli and Arakere, among others.
Commissioner K.N. Ramesh warned of strict legal action against establishments operating illegally or without the necessary licences.

The Bengaluru South City Corporation has sealed 63 commercial establishments operating “illegally” in residential areas across its jurisdiction during a special enforcement drive conducted by officials.

The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut. This was followed by 10 in the Bengaluru South constituency, nine in Bommanahalli, eight in Padmanabhanagar, four in Jayanagar, and two within the limits of the Anekal Assembly constituency (part of which falls under the South City Corporation).

According to Corporation officials, the action targeted commercial establishments operating in residential areas in violation of regulations. Officials said they were causing inconvenience to residents and obstructing vehicular movement. Bakeries, eateries, condiment stores, salons, beauty parlours, fruit and vegetable outlets, hardware stores, and other commercial establishments were among those sealed.

The Corporation said commercial establishments operating on roads narrower than 40 feet in residential areas were prohibited. However, several establishments had continued operations without valid trade licences despite being issued notices and instructions to vacate.

The drive was conducted simultaneously across several wards in Kumaraswamy Layout, J.P. Nagar, Madiwala, Koramangala, Ejipura, Jakkasandra, Begur, Singasandra, Yelachenahalli, Uttarahalli, Gottigere, Bilekahalli and Arakere, among others.

Commissioner K.N. Ramesh warned of strict legal action against establishments operating illegally or without the necessary licences.

articles.title: Trump says U.S. cutting $3.8 billion annual security assistance to Israel
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Donald Trump said Israel was “fine” with him ending the assistance, which began in 2019 and was signed under his predecessor, Barack Obama, three years earlier

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that Washington is ending a 10-year security assistance accord with Israel that allowed $3.8 billion in annual assistance to its ally until 2028.
Mr. Trump said Israel was “fine” with him ending the assistance, which began in 2019 and was signed under his predecessor, Barack Obama, three years earlier.
“We’ll help Israel if they need it,” Mr. Trump added in an interview on “Fox and Friends,” saying that he had agreed with Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cut the assistance.
“Israel’s our number one; we give them more than anybody else, and they no longer need it... If they did need it, I would say keep it going,” Mr. Trump added.
Under the deal, Israel receives financial assistance for the purchase of around $3.8 billion in weapons a year.

Since its founding in 1948, Israel has received more than $300 billion, adjusted for inflation, in U.S. economic and military assistance, according to the Council on Foreign Relations, far more than any other country since 1946.
The Israeli premier has said he wanted to end Israel’s reliance on U.S. support.
In June, Mr. Netanyahu called for his country to increase its military autonomy and reduce its reliance on Washington.
In January, he told The Economist that he hoped to do so within a decade, while in May he told CBS that he wanted support to reach “zero”.
Tuesday’s (November 3, 2026) announcement was nonetheless met with backlash from Israeli opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot, who said it showed that Mr. Netanyahu must go.

“The fact that Israel’s defense establishment is learning of a shift in our strategic relationship through the media, at the same time as the Israeli public, shows just how dangerous Benjamin Netanyahu’s conduct is,” Mr. Eisenkot said in a statement.

On Tuesday (November 3, 2026), Mr. Trump cited attacks by leftist Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who is running for the U.S. Senate in Tuesday’s (November 3, 2026) midterm elections after harnessing popular discontent and anti-Israel sentiment, as part of the reasoning behind the decision to end aid.

articles.title: U.S. Midterm Elections 2026 LIVE: Trump says midterm results will be ‘better than you think’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats, and governorships in 36 States are up for election, with about 210 million people registered to vote

On polling day, Donald Trump sprung a surprise by announcing that the U.S. will stop providing Israel USD four billion in aid from next year, which Democrat Ro Khanna described as a desperate attempt to stave off a “Blue tsunami”.
On the eve of the elections, the U.S. launched limited strikes on Iran’s Qesham island in the Hormuz Strait. Officials said that the strikes were in response to Iran firing at a U.S. aircraft.

U.S. rock legend Bruce Springsteen, a staunch Democrat, urged election officials Tuesday to resist any government voting interference amid fears President Donald Trump’s administration may intervene in the midterms.

“I’m speaking to election officials and representatives of our government on election day. You have sworn an oath to preserve, protect and defend our Constitution,” the 77-year-old said in a video on Instagram.

“That means you have a solemn duty to ensure that our votes are securely counted,” he said. “You who represent us must never consent to any directives that undermine our constitutional right to a free and fair election.”
“Our vote is our voice, and it’s up to you to ensure that our voice is heard,” added Springsteen, wearing a brown flannel shirt.

Europe’s benchmark equities index slipped on Tuesday, as doubts over a potential West Asia peace deal ⁠kept markets on edge ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, while investors also assessed a slew of earnings.
The pan-European STOXX 600 index closed 0.58% lower at 645.66 points, with mining ‌shares leading declines on weaker copper prices.

Iran and the United States are still far from a deal to end their war, a senior ‌Iranian official told Reuters. Overnight, the United States carried out what it ‌called ⁠defensive strikes on Iran’s Qeshm island.

State officials who run U.S. elections are braced for possible intervention by President Donald Trump’s administration in Tuesday’s midterms -- fearing federal authorities could disrupt voting, challenge ballot counts or try to block unfavourable results.

Mr. Trump, whose Republicans face an uphill battle to keep control of Congress, has repeatedly questioned the integrity of US elections and urged his party to “nationalise” voting in at least 15 places.
The White House says it is protecting election security, and many of the feared scenarios remain hypothetical.

articles.title: Ramalinga Reddy flags substandard civic works in HSR Layout, seeks halt
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Forest Minister and BTM Layout MLA Ramalinga Reddy has written to the Greater Bengaluru Authority’s Chief Commissioner, flagging substandard civic works in HSR Layout and demanding an immediate halt to the project.

Mr. Reddy referred to the construction of a 1.2-metre-wide stormwater drain on 14th Main Road in HSR Layout Stage 5, ahead of the white-topping works being undertaken by Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Limited (B-SMILE).

“Due to the poor quality of work, the underground drainage system in the area has been affected. In addition, smooth traffic movement has also been disrupted due to the poor condition of the road, causing inconvenience to local residents and other commuters,” Mr. Reddy said in the letter.

The Minister noted that during a site inspection, they had observed that the ongoing works were of poor quality. The issue was subsequently brought to the notice of the B-SMILE engineer in charge. However, he alleged that the engineer had failed to address the problem.

Mr. Reddy has demanded that the civic authority immediately halt the ongoing works and review the work completed so far. He has also sought action against the contractor, citing the alleged poor quality of work.

articles.title: Staggering white-collar success of Bengaluru has left a non-urban world behind, says Bagchi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: While the IITs have marched confidently forward since the 1950s, the ITIs have walked backwards. These two paths must operate stereophonically, cooperating in the exact same direction, says newly appointed Chairman of Karnataka’s Skill Vision Group

Warning that mounting global youth unrest could spread to India, the newly-appointed chairman of Karnataka’s Skill Vision Group, Subroto Bagchi, called for a radical transformation of the nation’s vocational education system at the Bengaluru Skill Summit, a three-day event that opened here on Wednesday.
He argued that the staggering white-collar success of Bengaluru’s information technology, biotechnology, and aerospace sectors has left a non-urban world behind.

To correct this imbalance, Mr. Bagchi championed the execution of Karnataka’s inclusive skill policy, which aims to give school dropouts from the fifth, eighth, and tenth standards the same transformative economic roles once reserved for corporate professionals.

The Mindtree co-founder and technocrat advocated that India must bridge the disparity between its premier engineering institutions and its grassroots technical schools. Evoking a metaphor shared by academic S. Sadagopan, Mr. Bagchi explained that India features two critical eyes: the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) and the Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs).

While the IITs have marched confidently forward since the 1950s, the ITIs have walked backwards. He emphasised that these two paths must operate stereophonically, cooperating in the exact same direction. Without a synchronised focus, the country risks producing visionaries who can design, but completely lacking a skilled workforce that can execute.

To turn this vision into a living reality, Mr. Bagchi outlined a comprehensive roadmap built on eight strategic pillars, anchored heavily in pervasive high school technology access, advanced manufacturing, services, healthcare, and the creative economy.

Addressing a packed audience at the Bengaluru Skill Summit organised Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood, he placed particular emphasis on scaling agricultural skills and nano-entrepreneurship, noting that if there was no bread on the table, artificial intelligence could always wait.
Highlighting recent societal unrest in France, Bangladesh, and Nepal, Mr. Bagchi insisted that the core driver was the genuine need for youth transparency and livelihood security.

Mr. Bagchi said, the Skill Vision Group would build the Bangalore Skill Summit into the global Davos of the skill sector within five years, drawing international CEOs to India to deliberate on human capital.

He also reminded the audience that the historic foundations of Karnataka’s tech industry were laid because early pioneers saw skill development as an absolute necessity for institution-building, rather than an optional luxury. He urged leaders to ground their upcoming structural programmes in quality, systems driven by deep empathy, and a total commitment to rural community inclusion.

Staggering white-collar success of Bengaluru has left a non-urban world behind, says Bagchi

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

While the IITs have marched confidently forward since the 1950s, the ITIs have walked backwards. These two paths must operate stereophonically, cooperating in the exact same direction, says newly appointed Chairman of Karnataka’s Skill Vision Group

Warning that mounting global youth unrest could spread to India, the newly-appointed chairman of Karnataka’s Skill Vision Group, Subroto Bagchi, called for a radical transformation of the nation’s vocational education system at the Bengaluru Skill Summit, a three-day event that opened here on Wednesday.

He argued that the staggering white-collar success of Bengaluru’s information technology, biotechnology, and aerospace sectors has left a non-urban world behind.

To correct this imbalance, Mr. Bagchi championed the execution of Karnataka’s inclusive skill policy, which aims to give school dropouts from the fifth, eighth, and tenth standards the same transformative economic roles once reserved for corporate professionals.

The Mindtree co-founder and technocrat advocated that India must bridge the disparity between its premier engineering institutions and its grassroots technical schools. Evoking a metaphor shared by academic S. Sadagopan, Mr. Bagchi explained that India features two critical eyes: the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) and the Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs).

While the IITs have marched confidently forward since the 1950s, the ITIs have walked backwards. He emphasised that these two paths must operate stereophonically, cooperating in the exact same direction. Without a synchronised focus, the country risks producing visionaries who can design, but completely lacking a skilled workforce that can execute.

To turn this vision into a living reality, Mr. Bagchi outlined a comprehensive roadmap built on eight strategic pillars, anchored heavily in pervasive high school technology access, advanced manufacturing, services, healthcare, and the creative economy.

Addressing a packed audience at the Bengaluru Skill Summit organised Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood, he placed particular emphasis on scaling agricultural skills and nano-entrepreneurship, noting that if there was no bread on the table, artificial intelligence could always wait.

Highlighting recent societal unrest in France, Bangladesh, and Nepal, Mr. Bagchi insisted that the core driver was the genuine need for youth transparency and livelihood security.

Mr. Bagchi said, the Skill Vision Group would build the Bangalore Skill Summit into the global Davos of the skill sector within five years, drawing international CEOs to India to deliberate on human capital.

He also reminded the audience that the historic foundations of Karnataka’s tech industry were laid because early pioneers saw skill development as an absolute necessity for institution-building, rather than an optional luxury. He urged leaders to ground their upcoming structural programmes in quality, systems driven by deep empathy, and a total commitment to rural community inclusion.

articles.title: State’s responsibility is to equip people for emerging opportunities, not just for current jobs: Sharanprakash Patil
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Held under the theme ‘Workforce 2030: Scale, Systems, Synergy’, the summit brings together policymakers, industry leaders, employers, educational institutions, skill development organisations, and other stakeholders to discuss the future of workforce development, industry-aligned skills, and employment pathways

The government’s responsibility is not simply to prepare young people for the jobs that exist today, but to equip them for the opportunities that will emerge tomorrow, said Sharan Prakash Patil, Minister for Medical Education and Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood, here on Tuesday.

Mr. Patil was speaking at the inaugural session of the Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026. The three-day event is organised by the Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood (SDEL ) and hosted by the Karnataka Skill Development Corporation (KSDC), in collaboration with the Karnataka Skill Development Authority (KSDA). The Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) is the knowledge partner for the summit. The Hindu is the media partner, and Japan is the country partner.

Held under the theme ‘Workforce 2030: Scale, Systems, Synergy’, the summit brings together policymakers, industry leaders, employers, educational institutions, skill development organisations, and other stakeholders to discuss the future of workforce development, industry-aligned skills, and employment pathways.

M.B. Patil, Minister for Large and Medium Industries, stated that Karnataka offers a strong industrial ecosystem, investor-friendly policies, and a skilled workforce to support future-ready industries.

Guruprasad Mudlapur, president of the Bosch Group in India and managing director and chief technology officer of Bosch Limited, noted that India’s economic opportunity depends entirely on the capabilities of its people, making skill development a profound economic and social imperative. “The industry cannot remain at the end of the skilling value chain waiting to recruit; we must actively participate in anticipating future capabilities, shaping learning, and strengthening trainers,” he urged.

Rangesh Raghavan, corporate vice-president and MD of LAM Research India, stated that building advanced industries like semiconductors requires a greater focus on talent than infrastructure. While Karnataka produces many engineering graduates, the industry critically lacks domain-skilled workers, including technicians, operators, and equipment service engineers, he opined.

Priyank Kharge, Minister for Information Technology, Biotechnology, and E-Governance, said, “We don’t pitch Karnataka as an investment destination. We pitch it as the knowledge and skill capital of the country. One great thing about the talent pool that Karnataka has is the ability to learn, unlearn, and relearn.’’
Other senior Ministers who attended the opening ceremony included Basavaraja Rayareddy, Minister for Higher Education, and Zamir Ahmed Khan, Minister for Food, Civil Supplies, and Consumer Affairs.

Dignitaries present at the event included: Shivakantamma (Kanta) Naik, Chairperson, KSDC, and Karnataka Vocational Training & Skill Development Corporation (KVTSDC), E. V. Ramana Reddy, IAS, Chairman, KSDA, Subodh Yadav, IAS, Principal Secretary to Government, Department of SDEL, Vasireddi Vijaya Jyothsna, Mission Director, National Livelihood Mission. Shilpa M., Commissioner, Department of Industrial Training and Employment, Ravi M. Tirlapur, Managing Director, KSDC and KVTSDC, Nawata Hiroshi, Consul General of Japan in Bengaluru, Steven Connolly, Acting Consul General of Australia in Bengaluru, Harshbir Sangha, British Deputy High Commissioner to Karnataka, Giandomenico Milano, Consul General of Italy in Bengaluru.

Several publications were released at the event, including Karnataka Kaushalya Sampada: The Skill Handbook (2026 Edition), Karnataka Talent Landscape 2026, and Karnataka’s Workforce Blueprint 2030 (Second Edition). The event also recognised Karnataka’s achievements in skill development by felicitating the state’s participants at the 48th WorldSkills Competition 2026, held in Shanghai, China. The accolades included a Silver Medal and the ‘Best of Nation’ Award in the Bakery category, along with eight Medallions for Excellence across various skill categories such as Additive Manufacturing, Electrical Installations, Industry 4.0, Mechatronics, and Robot Systems Integration. These achievements highlight the state’s skilled talent and their contribution to representing India on the global stage.

articles.title: Recruitment exams: KEA decided to appoint two invigilators for every exam hall
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Taking into account the irregularities reported at the Shiggaon examination centre of Haveri district in the Village Administrative Officer (VAO) recruitment examination recently, the Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) has decided to introduce several additional security measures.

A candidate in Haveri, who was flagged for poor academic record and emerging as a topper in VAO exam, has now been found to have used a mobile phone during the exam. Haveri police are probing the case now.

To prevent such instances, from now on, two invigilators will be appointed for every examination hall. One invigilator will stand at the rear of the hall to monitor candidates, while the other will remain at the front. They will also be responsible for ensuring that the mobile signal jammer in the examination centre is functioning properly.
Although candidates are required to undergo thorough frisking before entering the examination centre, it was found that this rule had not been implemented seriously.
Therefore, KEA has decided to conduct a second round of checking inside the examination hall as well.

All candidates must reach the examination centre at least 30 minutes before the examination begins. Candidates arriving at the last minute will not be permitted to enter, H. Prasanna, Executive Director, KEA said.

“Instructions have already been issued to establish district-level monitoring systems to oversee examination centres through webcasting. Going forward, KEA has also decided to appoint a separate invigilator at each examination centre to monitor CCTV footage,” he added.

The KEA has published a list on its website showing the marks obtained by the top 5,000 candidates in the VAO recruitment examination, along with their scores in previous recruitment examinations for Civil Police, KSRP, CAR/DAR Constable and Land Surveyor posts.

Mr. Prasanna said that the list was published as part of its efforts to ensure transparency. Cases involving significant variations in marks have been forwarded to the respective District Commissioners, requesting them to examine the CCTV footage.
The Haveri candidate in question had scored low marks in the KSRP examination, secured the first rank across Karnataka in the VAO examination, raising suspicions.

Mr. Prasanna appreciated those who helped expose the Shiggaon examination irregularities. He urged the public to bring any suspicions or concerns regarding future examinations to KEA’s notice through email.

He also cautioned against spreading unverified information on social media. There may be several candidates with identical names in different examinations. KEA has taken serious note of instances where marks belonging to one candidate are wrongly attributed to another, leading to unnecessary criticism on social media.

articles.title: Kochi Corporation clears 30 projects worth ₹1,500 crore for Urban Challenge Fund
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Projects include mobility hubs, civic tower, cultural district and waste-processing facility under Kochi@2050 vision; Union government to provide 25% of project cost as grant; Opposition councillors raise concerns over prioritising revenue-generating projects and use of land earmarked for welfare initiatives

The Kochi Corporation Council on Tuesday approved a concept note covering 30 projects worth over ₹1,500 crore identified by the civic body for potential funding under the Centre’s Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) as part of its Kochi@2050 vision.

The concept note will initially be forwarded to the State government. Detailed project reports (DPRs) will be prepared only for projects approved by the government for submission to the Centre. The UCF seeks to bring about a fundamental shift in the development vision by encouraging urban local bodies to adopt market-based financing mechanisms for urban development. Under the scheme, which will run from 2026 to 2031, the Union government will provide 25% of the project cost as a grant, with the stipulation that at least 50% of the cost be raised through bonds, bank loans and public-private partnerships (PPPs).

Major projects include the Kaloor integrated mobility hub (₹150-₹200 crore), Kochi civic tower project at Kacheripady (₹175 crore), Vypeen integrated mobility hub (₹75-₹100 crore), city-wide bus stand modernisation (₹50-₹75 crore), development of Palluruthy relief settlement into an integrated rehabilitation, care and livelihood campus (₹70 crore), Koker’s cultural district (₹80 crore), Kochi 3D digital twin and urban intelligence platform (₹35 crore), Brahmapuram construction waste processing and circular resource recovery facility (₹32 crore), and a modern slaughterhouse in West Kochi (₹20 crore).

Mayor V.K. Minimol said Kochi would be the first municipal body to submit concept notes for the UCF, under which ₹5,000 crore had been allocated to the State and would be distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. “Revenue-generating projects have been prioritised as per the UCF guidelines. The concept note will be updated based on feasible projects proposed by councillors and the identification of more land. Municipal bonds and green bonds will be prioritised as funding sources apart from the UCF,” she said.

V.A. Sreejith, LDF parliamentary party leader, said the Corporation could not afford to prioritise revenue-generating projects alone, as the livelihood and welfare of all sections of society had to be taken into account for the sustainable development of the city. He criticised the decision to overlook literary critic M.K. Sanoo and ghazal singer Umbayi while proposing an institution named after K.J. Yesudas. The Mayor said the proposal would be revised as a cultural centre.

BJP councillor Priya Prasanth raised concerns over the use of identified tracts of land, where the Corporation’s welfare projects were already under way, for revenue-generating projects under the UCF. She also pointed to a possible conflict in remodelling the Palluruthy relief settlement, a welfare project, by incorporating commercial facilities. Welfare standing committee chairperson Antony Painuthara said the project would be implemented without affecting the peaceful lives of the settlement’s residents and that the revenue generated would help ensure the settlement’s long-term sustainability.

articles.title: Top UN court to rule November 19 on Rohingya genocide case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Judges at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) have for seven years been weighing accusations by The Gambia that Myanmar’s brutal repression of the Rohingya breached the 1948 UN Genocide Convention

The top United Nations court will on November 19 deliver a landmark ruling on whether Myanmar’s crackdown against its mostly Muslim Rohingya minority constituted a genocide , officials said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

Judges at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) have for seven years been weighing accusations by The Gambia that Myanmar’s brutal repression of the Rohingya breached the 1948 UN Genocide Convention.

While the ICJ has no means of enforcing its decisions, a ruling that Myanmar committed genocide would heap more international pressure on its military junta and be seen as justice for hundreds of thousands of Rohingya.

Legal experts are closely watching the decision from the ICJ, which rules in disputes between countries, for clues as to how the court might sway in the seminal genocide case brought by South Africa against Israel over its campaign in Gaza.

Myanmar has always denied carrying out a genocide against the Rohingya, arguing its actions targeted a military uprising from insurgents after a series of attacks left a dozen security personnel dead.

The crackdown by the Myanmar army and Buddhist militias forced hundreds of thousands of Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh, bringing with them harrowing accounts of gang rape and mass executions.
More than one million Rohingya still live across the border in Bangladesh, in the world’s largest refugee settlement.
During hearings on the case in January, Gambian Justice Minister Dawda Jallow told the court the Rohingya had suffered “the most horrific violence and destruction one could imagine”.
“It is not about esoteric issues of international law. It is about real people, real stories and a real group of human beings,” said Mr. Jallow.
“The Rohingya of Myanmar. They have been targeted for destruction,” added the Minister.
The Gambia has brought the case to the ICJ under the terms of the UN Genocide Convention, which allows any state to sound the alarm if it suspects genocide is being committed.
The alleged violations of the convention “are a stain on our collective conscience and it would be irresponsible to pretend that it is not our business,” Mr. Jallow said.

articles.title: Iranian woman moves Madras High Court wanting to know procedure for obtaining X-Miscellaneous visa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Thirty-year-old Pegah Ansari complains of having been detained in a special camp for foreigners in Tiruchi even after she obtained bail in a criminal case booked for overstaying in India

A 30-year-old Iranian woman, reportedly born in a Zoroastrian family but forced to practice Islam in her country before converting to Christianity, has approached the Madras High Court seeking a direction to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Chennai to explain to her the procedure for obtaining X-Miscellaneous Visa so that she could step out of a special camp for foreigners in Tiruchi.

Pegah Ansari, daughter of Ansari Shapour, told the court that she was born and raised in a Zoroastrian family in Tehran. Claiming that all citizens at birth get registered as Muslims, irrespective of their actual religious background or personal faith, in her country; the petitioner said: “As a result, despite being born into a Zoroastrian family, I was officially recorded as a Muslim in government records.”

She went on to state: “Throughout my life in Iran, I lived under constant fear of persecution on account of my religious beliefs and personal convictions. Over time, I came to believe in and follow the teachings of Christianity. Due to the strict restrictions imposed on religious conversion in Iran, I was compelled to practice and profess my Christian faith only in private and in secrecy.”

Ms. Ansari said, she had no other option but to flee her country in 2019 because her private conversion to Christianity came to the notice of the authorities in Iran where she faced a genuine and imminent threat of persecution, harassment and possible arrest. She flew first to Georgia and underwent conversion through appropriate religious process. She resided there till 2022.

Her second stop was Sri Lanka where stayed approximately for a month before flying down to India on a one-month-long tourist visa in April 2022. “I came to India in search of safety, stability, and the freedom to live without fear of religious persecution,” the petitioner said and claimed to have obtained refugee status from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees in March 2025.

She said, the Anjugramam police in Kanniyakumari district had arrested her on December 10, 2025 when she had gone to a resort over there for decorating the venue of a birthday party. The charge levelled against her was that she had overstayed in India despite the expiry of her tourist visa on May 12, 2022. The police personnel also found that the petitioner’s Iranian passport had expired on February 17, 2024.

The petitioner was lodged at the women’s prison at Puzhal near Chennai until the Kanniyakumari Principal District and Sessions Court granted her bail on January 29, 2026. Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to the Tiruchi special camp for foreigners on the basis of a December 23, 2025 Government Order which authorised her detention in the camp until the disposal of the criminal case or her deportation.

Claiming that the State could not curtail her free movement even after grant of bail, the petitioner said, she would be able to approach the appropriate authorities for getting relocated to some other country only if she was allowed to move freely without being confined to the boundaries of the special camp. The petitioner wanted to know the procedure for obtaining the visa required to face court proceedings.
The petitioner said that she had made a representation in this regard to the FRRO on June 25, 2026 but complained that the officer did not respond.

articles.title: Ladakh administration asks activist Sonam Wangchuk’s wife to stop ‘unauthorised activities’ at their Leh school
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: On September 22, Gitanjali Angmo, wife of Mr. Wangchuk, requested the Deputy Commissioner, Leh, for the issuance of a No Objection Certificate and clearance for the proposed members of the Managing Committee of the school

The Ladakh administration on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) asked the Himalayan Institute of Alternatives, Ladakh’s (HIAL) Desert Flower School, run by activist Sonam Wangchuk’s wife, “to stop unauthorised activities of the school”, citing the matter pertaining to the allotment of land as “sub judice”. Meanwhile, Mr. Wangchuk extends support to people of Arunachal Pradesh resisting the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project.

“Desert Flower School of the HIAL Ecosystem has commenced functioning of the school without necessary clearance/approval from the competent authority. The administration asks HIAL to strictly maintain the status quo and avoid causing any prejudice to the case pending before the High Court of J&K and Ladakh,” said a spokesman of the L-G administration.

It claimed that the school “commenced activities without obtaining the requisite consent, clearances and approvals from the concerned authorities”. The administration pointed out that the matter concerning HIAL was pending adjudication before the court.

On September 22, Gitanjali Angmo, wife of Mr. Wangchuk, requested the Deputy Commissioner, Leh, for the issuance of a No Objection Certificate and clearance for the proposed members of the Managing Committee of the school located at Phyang, Leh. The Administration had cancelled the land allotment to HIAL in August 2025.

“Accordingly, the notice issued by Tehsildar, Leh, has strongly advised HIAL to maintain strict status quo and not undertake any action whatsoever towards the functioning or commencement of activities,” said the L-G order.

Meanwhile, Mr. Wangchuk, who has been campaigning for a special status for Ladakh and was jailed last year under the National Security Act (NSA), on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) wrote a letter to President Droupadi Murmu and appealed for intervention “to protect the rights of indigenous communities, democratic freedoms, and the fragile Himalayan ecology in Arunachal Pradesh”.

“I write to you with a heavy heart, as an environmental activist from Ladakh who has spent decades working to protect our fragile Himalayan environment. I urgently seek your intervention in the disturbing situation unfolding in the Siang Valley of Arunachal Pradesh, where indigenous communities, particularly the Adi people, are resisting the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. We in Ladakh understand their pain,” reads the letter.

Mr. Wangchuk said for years, people of Ladakh have been peacefully demanding constitutional safeguards under the Sixth Schedule to protect fragile ecology, ancestral lands and cultural identity. “We know what it feels like when decisions affecting our future are taken without adequately consulting us. Coming from an indigenous tribal community yourself, you understand that for us, nature is not merely a resource to be exploited, but a mother to be protected,” the letter reads.

In the letter, Mr. Wancghuk highlighted the reports about thousands of security personnel being deployed, young activists arrested, and villagers subjected to intimidation and restrictions on movement.

“There are serious allegations of police excesses, including against elderly villagers, and criminal cases against those opposing the project. What pains me particularly is the attempt to portray people raising legitimate concerns as anti-national or foreign-funded,” said Mr. Wangchuk.

He said it was deeply unfortunate that people who have stood by the nation in its most difficult times should face such accusations. “We have witnessed such allegations in Ladakh over the past year, and now similar accusations are being made against the people of Arunachal Pradesh. Such shortsighted accusations, particularly when made without credible evidence, do not strengthen national security. They weaken it. In sensitive border regions, the trust, goodwill and active cooperation of local communities are among our country’s greatest strategic strengths,” said Mr. Wangchuk.
He also appealed for de-escalation, protection of democratic rights and biological safeguards.

articles.title: SIT report says charges against KSU activists in Veena George case cannot be sustained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: SIT finds no grounds to sustain charges of rioting, wrongful restraint and trespass; says black flag protest is not a criminal offence; final report says KSU activists did not obstruct police or wrongfully restrain former Health Minister

The Special Investigation Team (SIT) has submitted its final report to the court, stating that the charges levelled against Kerala Students Union (KSU) activists in connection with the alleged attack on former Health Minister Veena George at Kannur railway station cannot be sustained.
The SIT found that the protesters had not committed the offences alleged in the original chargesheet and stated that waving black flags as a form of protest did not constitute a criminal offence.

The final report was submitted by SIT chief U. Preman before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court in Kannur. The investigation team concluded that the protesters had not committed offences such as rioting, wrongful restraint, obstructing public servants from discharging their official duties or criminal trespass on railway premises.
The charge of attempted murder, which was initially included in the first information report, was subsequently dropped by the first investigation team while filing the chargesheet.

According to the SIT report, the responsibility of the police personnel accompanying Veena George was to prevent the protesters from approaching her. However, the protesters did not obstruct the police from discharging their official duties. Instead, the police stopped those waving black flags. The SIT also found that the Minister had not been wrongfully restrained by the protesters.

The report further stated that the protesters had entered the railway station after purchasing valid platform tickets. Therefore, the charge of trespassing on railway premises was not sustainable. The SIT also cited court observations that black flag protests did not constitute a criminal offence.

Meanwhile, the SIT had earlier submitted a separate report to the Director General of Police, recommending action against Veena George’s former gunman, Abhilash, for allegedly giving a false statement, as well as against officials who had allegedly failed to conduct the preliminary investigation properly.
The court will now decide on further proceedings based on the final report submitted by the SIT.
