articles.title: Vigilance wing pulls up Kochi Metro Rail Limited over lapses in auctioning commercial spaces
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Vigilance finds that auctions were conducted without advertisements and in a less transparent manner, with most cases attracting only a single bidder; it observes that changes in base rates and EMD conditions deterred prospective bidders and created a sense of differential treatment among existing vendors

The Vigilance wing of Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) has pulled up the agency for a slew of alleged omissions in the leasing of commercial spaces at the 22 metro stations along the Aluva-M.G. Road-Thripunithura phase-one corridor, which resulted in substantial revenue loss over the past few years.

The metro agency’s Vigilance wing observed that the auction of commercial spaces at the stations was conducted without advertisements and in a “less transparent” manner. The auctions were conducted outside the scope of the procurement manual, and the basic principles of transparency, competition, fairness and elimination of discretion were not followed in letter and spirit. Base rates were not fixed on the basis of objective data. Instead, a trial-and-error method was adopted.

Changes in rates and other conditions, such as the earnest money deposit (EMD), resulted in prospective bidders adopting a wait-and-see approach, while creating a sense of differential treatment among existing vendors. A level playing field was missing. Moreover, e-auction or forward auction through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) was not considered. In most cases, there was only a single bidder. The absence of a standard operating procedure for conducting auctions led to ad hoc practices and subjectivity in the process, further reflecting the lack of transparency.

The Vigilance wing also took note of the absence of a finance member in the auction committee, in contravention of the provisions of the procurement manual. There were also several corrections, overwritings and omissions in the registration forms and the auction register. Adding to the concerns, the terms and conditions of the auction were relaxed midway through the process without public notice. The EMD amount kept changing from one auction to another, and it was eventually decided not to collect it at all.

In view of these findings, the Vigilance wing recommended that base rates be fixed on the basis of objective data. It also called for a consistent policy on the auction of spaces for hiring or advertising to avoid the trial-and-error approach to fixing base rates, ambiguity in deciding the mode of auction and confusion over the auction procedure.

In this regard, a forward auction module of GeM or its e-auction module should be considered, after due preparation, instead of outdated and less transparent methods such as physical or hybrid auctions. Adequate publicity, including through the media, should be ensured to prevent ad hoc practices and subjectivity in conducting auctions. A standard operating procedure (SOP) for conducting auctions should be drawn up, and a finance member should be included in the auction committee. The mandatory declaration of ‘Conflict of Interest’ by auction committee members should also be ensured.
Other recommendations include continuous videographing or recording of the auction or tender process through CCTV and preparation of the minutes after the auction.

articles.title: BJP leaders criticise Mamata-Congress bonhomie
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari accused Mamata Banerjee of allying with ‘anarchists’ in Delhi

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leadership continued to criticise and raise questions about the bonhomie between the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the Trinamool Congress and the Congress party for the second consecutive day on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) and accused the former Chief Minister of joining forces in Delhi to create anarchy in the country.

BJP president Nitin Nabin made a similar charge against Ms. Banerjee during a procession in Kolkata on Monday (November 2, 2026). On Tuesday (November 3, 2026), West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and BJP leader and former Union Minister Smriti Irani criticised the coming together of the Mamata Banerjee and Congress party.

Mr. Adhikari, who participated in a ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ march at Siliguri in North Bengal, said that the former Chief Minister was not invited to inaugurate a single Durga Puja in Kolkata and that she is going to Delhi to ally with anarchists.

The Chief Minister tried to paint most of the Opposition parties that had assembled at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on November 1 with the same brush, calling them dynasty parties and saying that they are four-generation, three-generation, and two-generation parties.

Mr. Adhikari referred to Congress as a “4G” party, referring to (Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi, Rajiv Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi), Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) as “3G” (Karunanidhi, M.K. Stalin and Udhayanidhi Stalin), and Mamata Banerjee’s Trinamool Congress and Lalu Prasad Yadav Rashtriya Janata Dal as “2G” (Mamata Banerjee-Abhishek Banerjee and Lalu Prasad-Tejashwi Yadav). He added that Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has “no G”.

BJP leader Smriti Irani, who held a press conference in Kolkata also spoke in a similar vein accusing the Trinamool Congress of trampling democracy in the State by unleashing attacks on BJP workers and committing atrocities on women workers. “Today those political goons are joining hands with the Congress at Ramlila Maidan,” she said. Ms. Irani called Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi as “perpetual prince in the waiting” and said that he is undermining the democratic institutions of the country.

The remarks by the BJP leadership come at a time when speculations are rife in the political circles about a larger Opposition unity taking place in the State. West Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) called on all the Opposition parties to come together, keeping their flags aside and instead using “white flags”. Only a few weeks ago, Mamata Banerjee had decided to support Congress candidates in the Nandigram by-polls after her party’s nominee withdrew candidates at the last moment.

Reacting to the signs of new political alignment emerging, State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya called Mamata Banerjee, Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury and CPI(M) State Secretary Md. Salim to hold a procession “hand in hand”.

articles.title: Mobile phone, power banks seized from Kannur Central Jail
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Food items suspected to be used to smuggle prohibited articles into prison
A mobile phone and accessories, including two power banks, a charger and three data cables, were seized from Kannur Central Jail during a search by prison officials on Monday.

The prohibited articles were found hidden beneath stone slabs behind the jail’s second block. The Town police have registered a case and launched an investigation based on a complaint lodged by jail Joint Superintendent A. Shaiju.

The repeated seizure of prohibited articles from within the jail compound has raised concerns over security checks. Inadequate inspection of food items and cooking materials brought into the prison is suspected to be facilitating the smuggling of such articles.

Food items suspected to be used to smuggle prohibited articles into prison

A mobile phone and accessories, including two power banks, a charger and three data cables, were seized from Kannur Central Jail during a search by prison officials on Monday.

articles.title: 60-day long prohibitive orders passed ‘ex-parte’ to prevent unrest in key capital zones: Delhi Police in Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Six orders issued on August 20 or immediately before or after this date, came a month after the July 20 protests witnessed violence in New Delhi district; one of them imposes prohibitions from September 26 to November 24

Seven separate prohibitive orders passed by the Delhi Police under Section 163 Bharatiya Nagarik Duraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in the national capital show restrictions concerning free movement were imposed way before protests erupted demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Six orders issued on August 20 or immediately before or after this date, came a month after the July 20 protests against alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leaks witnessed violence in New Delhi district, the power and commercial heart of the capital city. One of them imposes prohibitions from September 26 to November 24.

The prohibitive orders are for a maximum period of 60 days, till the latter half of October. They are ex-parte or without hearing any objections, saying “notice cannot be served individually on all concerned”.

The orders, which are part of an affidavit filed by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar in the Supreme Court, said “reports have been received indicate that such conditions now exists that unrestricted holding of public meetings, processions/demonstrations, etc, in the area are likely to cause obstruction to traffic, danger to human safety and disturbance of public tranquility”.
The police reasoned in the orders that it was necessary to take “speedy measures” to “prevent danger to human life or safety and disturbance to public tranquility”.

The seven orders comprise the police sub-divisions of Connaught Place, Tughlak Road, Parliament Street, Chanakya Puri — where the Prime Minister’s residence, Rashtrapati Bhavan, foreign embassies, and other vital installations are located — Barakhamba Road, Safdarjung Enclave in south-west Delhi, and Defence Colony.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Anti-CEC protest fallout: Supreme Court issues fresh directions to Centre, Delhi Police

The orders prohibited activities, including the holding of any public meeting, shouting of slogans, making speeches, picketing or dharnas, assembly of five or more persons, carrying fire arms, banners, placards, lathis, spears, swords, sticks, brickbats, etc.

The affidavit from the police chief came in response to a host of petitions filed by politicians, party leaders, activists, lawyers and private individuals — including CPI(M) state secretary M.A. Baby, Rajya Sabha MP A.A. Rahim, senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy, advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi and others — against the indiscriminate detentions of leaders, former Chief Ministers, students, youths, journalists, lawyers, and others by the Delhi Police, against the rule of law and democratic dissent on October 10-11 during protests seeking the resignation of the CEC.

The petitioners had alleged around 7,000 en masse illegal detentions during the protests, and shutting down of vital public transport systems, including the Delhi Metro, leaving thousands of commuters stranded in the national capital. Major roads had been heavily barricaded with the heavy presence of security personnel, and trains to Delhi were cancelled on October 10 amidst the detentions.

Mr. Tripathi, through his counsel Chand Qureshi, had argued in the apex court that the shutdown was in clear violation of an October 9 order of the Supreme Court, which had emphasised that the authorities must not cause any hardship or suffering to ordinary commuters through a blanket ban.
This had led the Supreme Court to direct the Delhi Police to place on record the specific prohibitive orders.

articles.title: Why is there variation in India’s fertility rates? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: What is the Total Fertility Rate of India? How does it impact policy interventions?

The story so far: The Sample Registration System (SRS) Statistical Report of 2021, released by the Office of the Registrar General of India recently, showed that India has maintained its Total Fertility Rate (TFR) at 2.0 — the same as reported in 2020. While the national average for TFR has remained the same, there is a wide regional variation in TFR data for States and Union Territories (UTs) reported independently.

The highest TFR was recorded in Bihar at 3.0 and the lowest was reported for West Bengal and Delhi at 1.4. The data went on to reveal that in the decade between 2009-11 and 2019-21, TFR has been on an overall decline, in States, and nationally, albeit at different rates.

articles.title: Row over Dia Mirza’s appeal for a noise-free Deepavali | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BMC uploaded the videos on November 1, but soon after the video of actor Dia Mirza went up, BJP Mumbai president Ameet Satam is learnt to have called the BMC administration to pull it down

The story so far: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) expressed strong displeasure and asked the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) to restore a video of actor Dia Mirza, in which, the actor appealed for a noise-free and pollution-free celebration of Deepavali. The message was a part of the official anti-firecracker campaign of the BMC. The civic body pulled down the video earlier this week after objections by the BJP leaders.

In a suo motu Public Interest Litigation about noise and air pollution caused by religious processions across Maharashtra, the Bombay High Court had urged to the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) to rope in celebrities for pollution awareness.

articles.title: Vijayawada civic poll result: Jana Sena’s Vangaveeti Radhakrishna elected Mayor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jana Sena’s Vangaveeti Radhakrishna is elected Mayor by a margin of 1,30,912 votes
The National Democratic Alliance of the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) , the Jana Sena Party (JSP) and the BJP has won a landslide victory in Vijayawada in the urban local body elections.

Delayed by continuous rain, the counting process , which began at around 3 p.m. on Tuesday, continued till late night. Election personnel worked till around 4 a.m. on Wednesday (November 4, 2026). The final results were announced by the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation on Wednesday morning.
The city has 8,05,797 voters across 86 divisions, of whom 4,46,021 exercised their franchise on Sunday (November 1). Of these, 4,27,385 votes were declared valid.

విజయవాడ మున్సిపల్ కార్పొరేషన్ మేయర్ గా కూటమి బలపరచిన జనసేన పార్టీ అభ్యర్థి శ్రీ వంగవీటి రాధాకృష్ణ గారు భారీ మెజారిటీతో ఘన విజయం సాధించిన సందర్భంగా శుభాకాంక్షలు. #NDAsweepsAP #APLocalBodyElections #JanaSenaStrikesAgain #CheppaamChestunnaam https://t.co/lY6g9acvuy

According to the final report on votes secured by each Mayoral candidate, JSP candidate Vangaveeti Radhakrishna got 2,65,968 votes. YSRCP candidate and former Mayor Rayana Bhagyalakshmi came second with 1,35,056 votes.

Independent candidate and former Vijayawada Police Commissioner A.B. Venkateswara Rao, who was supported by the Congress and the CPI and the CPI(M), secured 12,657 votes. His entry had made it a three-way contest, but Mr. Venkateswara Rao could not save his deposit: he failed to secure one-sixth of the total number of votes polled.

Vangaveeti Radhakrishna, with TDP leaders Buddha Venkanna and Gadde Anuradha, at a rally in Vijayawada on October 18, before filing his nomination for the Mayor’s post. He was elected Mayor by a margin of 1,30,912 votes. File | Photo Credit: G.N. Rao
Aam Aadmi Party candidate Kambhampati Rama Gopala Krishna Murthy got 499 votes. There were 19 candidates in the fray for the Mayor’s post, ten of them independents.

The TDP and its alliance partners also swept the division elections. The TDP won 53 divisions, the Jana Sena Party 19 and the BJP four. In total, the alliance won 76 of the 86 divisions of the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation.

The YSRCP, which won the municipal elections in Vijayawada in 2021, was reduced to eight divisions. The CPI(M)’s candidate, former corporator Boye Satya Babu, held his division, and an independent candidate won another.

The divisions the YSRCP won are 34, 53 and 58 in the Vijayawada West Assembly constituency, 78 in Vijayawada Central, and 6, 8, 10 and 26 in Vijayawada East. Mr. Satya Babu won Division 52 in the West constituency.

The TDP won the most divisions, 20, in the Vijayawada Central constituency, and 17 and 16 in the East and West constituencies respectively. The JSP won seven divisions each in the East and West constituencies and five in Central. The BJP won one division each in West and East and two in Central.

articles.title: Rescue operation at landslide-hit south Odisha village halted; families prepare for final rituals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The decision to temporarily suspend the operation was taken after experts assessed that the remains, if any, could be buried under nearly 30 feet of debris, Kandhamal District Collector Vedbhusan said

The multi-agency search and rescue operation at landslide-ravaged Gidipabali village in south Odisha was halted on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) due to inclement weather, as families of 10 missing persons prepared to perform their final rituals, a senior official said.

The decision to temporarily suspend the operation was taken after experts assessed that the remains, if any, could be buried under nearly 30 feet of debris, Kandhamal District Collector Vedbhusan said.
He, along with Ganjam District Collector V Keerthi Vasan, met the victims’ family members at a shelter camp and discussed the situation at the site where the search and rescue operation was underway.
The State Government had launched the search and rescue operation on Friday (October 30, 2026) following the landslide triggered by heavy rains brought by Cyclone Arnab last week.

“According to experts, there is at least 30 feet of debris, which is difficult to remove due to at least three successive landslides in the area. Further blasting is likely to trigger fresh landslides and may also endanger the lives of rescue personnel. Therefore, with the consent of the family members, the rescue operation was halted on Wednesday,” Kandhamal Collector Vedbhusan told reporters.
He said the families, understanding the difficult circumstances and challenges involved, had requested the administration to help them perform the final rituals and find closure.

“The administration has assured the families of all possible assistance to help them restart their lives. However, we want to make one more final attempt to ensure closure for everyone,” the collector said.

“Although operations have been temporarily halted on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) due to the weather, we will make another round of efforts as soon as the weather remains clear for a couple of days before closing the operation, as per the wishes of the families,” he added.

The official said the State Government had mobilised multiple agencies and deployed all possible resources, including life-detection equipment, dog squads, experts from IIT, the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Railway teams and controlled blasting, for the rescue operation.
However, no significant breakthrough was achieved, as the houses affected by the landslide are believed to be buried under nearly 30 feet of debris following successive landslides.
Of the 26 residents of Gidipabali, a hilltop village on the Kandhamal-Ganjam district border, 13 managed to escape the landslide on the night of October 29 and were shifted to a shelter in Udayagiri.
The search operation was launched for the remaining 13 residents.

articles.title: ECI still insisting on Form 6 for excluded voters in Delhi SIR, petitioners make urgent mentioning in Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: On October 28, the Supreme Court made it clear that the ECI was in “error” to force pre-existing voters, deleted from the electoral rolls, to apply as new voters under Form 6 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960

Advocate Prashant Bhushan, on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), said that the Election Commission of India (ECI) was still insisting that voters excluded after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Delhi, under the Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate (ASDD) categories, must fill up Form 6, meant exclusively for new voters. fill up Form 6, which is meant exclusively for new voters.

On October 28, the Supreme Court made it clear that the ECI was in “error” to force pre-existing voters, deleted from the electoral rolls, to apply as new voters under Form 6 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

Petitioners, activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, represented by advocates Mr. Bhushan, Cheryl D’souza and Neha Rathi, had submitted on October 28 that the ECI was compelling voters to misrepresent themselves as new applicants, an offence which attracts imprisonment.
On October 28, the apex court had orally nudged the ECI that such purged voters should be allowed to use Form 8/enumeration form.
On Wednesday (November 4, 2026), the CJI said the case would be heard after Deepavali holidays, the voters need not fear when the Supreme Court was already dealing with the case.
The CJI noted that the ECI has extended the deadline for filing claims and objections to November 25 from the earlier deadline of October 30.
Mr. Bhushan said the voters feared that making a declaration in Form 6 that they were fresh voters would invite prosecution.
“They are in the horns of a dilemma,” Mr. Bhushan submitted.
“We are dealing with the matter, how can they feel like that,” the CJI assured.
The Bench asked the petitioners to file an application on this aspect, and said the matter would be heard on November 19.
Editorial | Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
If required, the Bench further stated that the ECI could be asked to extend the date further.

articles.title: Union Cabinet to discuss capex support for critical mineral processing, VGF for RE grid-scale storage system
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The Hindu had learnt previously that the potential scheme could provide support of about 30% for setting up of these processing plants

The Union Cabinet is expected to take up two major schemes for consideration, the first of them concerns according capital expenditure support for promoting critical mineral processing and the other being a viability gap funding (VGF) scheme for development of grid-scale storage system, according to a memo seen by The Hindu.
The Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Although the memo did not specify the contours of the scheme and its ambit, the policy has been in the works for some time now.
The Hindu had learnt previously that the potential scheme could provide support of about 30% for setting up of these processing plants.

At an event of the industry body FIMI in September this year, Secretary at the Union Ministry of Mines Keshav Chandra had indicated that the government would institute a scheme for domestic processing of lithium and nickel.

Back in April, the Piyush Goyal, the former secretary, had indicated that the government had identified two minerals for initiating the scheme that were, among other things, expected to provide resilience the electric vehicle battery chain.

Grid-scale energy storage systems are deployed at transmission and distribution for greater grid stability, absorb excess electricity when supply exceeds demand and discharge them during peak hours or when necessary.

About 1,835 million units (MUs) of renewable energy was curtailed, according to data compiled by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) during July and August this year. This includes 1,462 MU of solar energy and 373 MU of wind energy.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries is already implementing a production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for establishing 50 GWh of advanced chemistry cell manufacturing capacity, of which 10 GWh would account for grid-scale stationary storage.

articles.title: Oil rises on Iran war uncertainty after Trump’s Republicans face election rout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: In the previous session, Brent settled at its lowest level in nearly four weeks ‌as traders weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran

Oil prices rose on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) in a volatile session as investors ​awaited Washington’s next move in the war with Iran, with ⁠Democrats capturing control of US Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republicans in midterm elections.
Brent futures rose 82 cents, or 0.8%, to $104.42 a barrel at 0510 GMT. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude ‌futures gained 50 cents, or 0.5%, to $96.59, reversing earlier declines.
In the previous session, Brent settled at its lowest level in nearly four weeks ‌as traders weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran.
Vote ‌counting ⁠was underway in the U.S. midterm elections, with Democrats snaring majorities ⁠in both houses of Congress for the rest of Trump’s second term.

“President Trump’s conflicting signals, with military strikes continuing alongside statements downplaying further escalation, have made it difficult for traders to build strong directional ​conviction,” said Priyanka Sachdeva, head ‌of market insights at Phillip Nova.
“I believe some profit-taking and reduction in speculative long positions are justified, particularly after the sharp rally in October,” said Sachdeva.

“However, the underlying supply disruption risks around the Strait of Hormuz have not disappeared. ‌An unexpected drawdown in U.S. crude inventories is also offering some fundamental ​support,” she added.

The U.S. had carried out “defensive” strikes on Iran’s Qeshm island targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, a US official said ⁠on Tuesday. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations.
Markets remained on watch for any progress in talks ‌to end the US-Israeli war with Iran, as Qatar stepped up mediation efforts to avert an escalation of attacks after the US elections.
A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday that Iran and the United States remain far from a deal to end their war.
U.S. President Donald Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that the United States had no immediate plans to strike Iran.
Meanwhile, crude ‌stocks fell by 5.27 million barrels in the week ended October 30, market sources said on ​Wednesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.

articles.title: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed claims victory in Michigan Senate battle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: El-Sayed won despite a last-minute hiccup in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed said early on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that he had won a US Senate seat in Michigan over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, which would make him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.
“Michigan, we did it!” Mr. El-Sayed said in a speech at his election headquarters in Detroit.
“I am so proud and honored to stand here as your senator-elect from the great state of Michigan.”
Mr. El-Sayed won despite a last-minute hiccup in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour.
The Michigan doctor rallied voters on leftist campaign promises, including universal health care, to hold a key U.S. Senate seat for Democrats, taking over from the retiring Gary Peters.
Republicans ran a scorched-earth campaign to paint Democrats as communists and branded Mr. El-Sayed a terrorist who would endanger Americans.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: As Speaker, Mr. Jeffries, representing a New York ​City congressional district, would preside over a majority that will be sworn in the first week of January, taking the reins from Republicans ⁠who controlled the House for the past four years

The Democrats’ midterm election win puts Hakeem Jeffries in line to become the first Black speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives, with the dual challenge of opposing President ‌Donald Trump while bridging the gap between his party’s moderates and its more vocal progressives.

As Speaker, Mr. Jeffries, representing a New York ​City congressional district, would preside over a majority that will be sworn in the first week of January, taking the reins from Republicans ⁠who controlled the House for the past four years.
“Today begins the great American comeback,” Mr. Jeffries proclaimed in a victory speech late on Tuesday after media outlets projected the likelihood of Democratic majorities in the House and Senate.

He attacked the Trump-led Republican agenda in Congress over the past two years, pledging to pass legislation reversing steep spending cuts — enacted into ‌law on July 4, 2025 — to the Medicaid healthcare program for the poor and people with disabilities.

“The American people have spoken and made clear that they’ve had enough of the extremism, enough of the corruption. They want a Congress that’s going to deliver for the ‌American people,” Mr. Jeffries said.

articles.title: US midterm election results 2026: List of Indian-origin winners
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Indian-Americans Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives, while Vivek ‌Ramaswamy‌ was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor

Several Indian-origin candidates too notched up victories as Democrats made significant gains in the US midterm elections, positioning themselves to wrest key Senate seats from Republicans, delivering a stinging rebuke to President Donald Trump.

Indian-American candidates Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives from Virginia and Florida, respectively. On the other hand, Republican ‌Vivek ‌Ramaswamy ‌was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor.

Suhas Subramanyam, who served as an advisor to former president Barack Obama, has been re-elected as a member of the US House of Representatives. The 40-year-old won from Virginia’s 10th congressional district , polling over 61.5% of the vote against Republican Dave Beckwith, who managed to win 36.4 per cent of the ballots cast.

A former high school principal, Pia Dandiya became the newest Indian-American to be elected to the US House , defeating Republican Casey Askar in Florida’s 22nd Congressional district. Dandiya bagged 51.9% of the votes, while her opponent Askar polled 49.1% of the votes.

Trump favourite Indian-American Vivek Ramaswamy was defeated in Ohio’s gubernatorial race, the home state of Vice President J. D. Vance, by Democrat Amy Acton after a bitter campaign that left the Republican Party divided.

Other Indian-American candidates are awaiting their results as vote counting is still under way. Democrat Nithya Raman, who was born in Keralam, is locked in a keen contest with her former boss Karen Bass for the post of Mayor of Los Angeles, the US’s second-largest city. Indian-American lawmakers Ro Khanna, Ami Bera, Pramila Jayapal are seeking re-election to the US House of Representatives, while fellow Democrat Amish Shah is in the fray in competitive races to make their debut as Congresspersons.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The research found that producing green hydrogen in desert areas in Australia, Chile and north Africa needs far more water than the industry claims. It also found serious environmental risks that had been overlooked

Green hydrogen is a form of renewable energy that, if taken up widely, could reduce global greenhouse gas emissions. It is produced by splitting water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen using renewable power. This clean, zero-emissions fuel is mainly used by industries like steel manufacturing and chemical refining. Heavy transport sectors such as maritime shipping, aviation and long-haul trucking could also use it.

But green hydrogen comes at an environmental cost too: huge amounts of water are needed to produce it. In Africa, the regions that have the best solar and wind resources to produce this clean energy are also those with the least water on the planet.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: The Milky Way grew by devouring galaxies, leaving a trail of ghost stars
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Galactic archaeologists are using precise measures and larger sample sizes afforded by new missions to tease apart minute differences between groups of stars, revealing the history of the Milky Way going back almost 12 billion years

There have always been stories about them. Australian Aboriginal tales tell of an old couple called the Jukara, while for Chile’s Mapuche people they are Rvganko or water ponds. To modern astronomers, they are the Small and Large Magellanic clouds, two of the closest galaxies to us that are in the process of being swallowed by the Milky Way.

They are evidence of a kind of snowball effect that characterises the formation and evolution of galaxies, which scientists believe are the result of a series of violent collisions. As galaxies fall into one another, the smaller ones are ripped apart by tidal forces of the larger, leaving behind streams and clusters of stars that don’t move in lockstep with the rest of the galaxy. They also stand out for their chemical compositions, which allow astronomers to group stars that were born together and piece back their rough ages.

Science, Space & Environment Report: The Milky Way grew by devouring galaxies, leaving a trail of ghost stars. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

articles.title: Many parts of Delhi reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 379 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on November 4, 2026, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data

The overall air quality of Delhi continued to be in the “very poor” category on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) morning, while many parts of the city reeled under “severe” level of air pollution , according to official data.
Many parts of the city, including ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri witnessed “severe” level air pollution.
Other cities and towns in north India, including Noida, Gurugram, and Panipat also witnessed “very poor” air quality, on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) morning.
The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 379 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
“Severe” level air pollution affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases, as per the CPCB.
The overall air quality of Delhi is likely to be in the “very poor” category for three days, as per the Central government’s ‘Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi’.

The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 350 (very poor) at 4 p.m. on Tuesday, up from 324 (very poor) a day earlier, as per the Central Pollution Control Board’s daily bulletin, which is treated as the day’s AQI.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

articles.title: Cancer registry in Telangana has logged 35,000 cases, government advisor informs Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Minister for Health C. Damodar Raja Narasimha says Telangana government has expanded cancer treatment services to all 33 districts in the State

The Telangana government has expanded cancer treatment services to all 33 districts in the State, with day-care cancer centres providing chemotherapy locally to reduce the need for patients to travel to Hyderabad, Minister for Health C. Damodar Raja Narasimha said on Tuesday, November 3. The government has also initiated steps to establish Regional Cancer Centres to further strengthen cancer care infrastructure, he added.
The Minister made these remarks during a review meeting on medical services being provided to cancer patients in government hospitals.

Oncologist Dr. Nori Dattatreyudu, who also serves as the advisor to the Telangana government on preventive, curative and affordable cancer care, said 35,000 cancer cases have been registered on the dedicated cancer portal. “Declaring cancer a notifiable disease and effective use of cancer registry will help strengthen the State’s efforts in monitoring and controlling the disease,” he added.

Citing the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme as an example, Dr. Nori also appreciated the State’s efforts in prevention, screening and early detection of cancer. Of the 3.4 lakh eligible girls in Telangana, 2.3 lakh of them have been vaccinated against the HPV, achieving a coverage of 67%, he said.

During the meeting, officials briefed the Minister on cancer treatment facilities available at the MNJ Cancer Hospital and the Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), besides the functioning of day-care chemotherapy centres established across the State. They explained that while patients initially receive treatment at MNJ or NIMS, chemotherapy services are subsequently provided at district-level centres. Patients are also being mapped district-wise to facilitate treatment and follow-up.

The Minister directed officials to improve facilities for patients receiving chemotherapy at district centres and ensure that the services were readily available at the district headquarters. “Patients should not have to travel to Hyderabad for chemotherapy when treatment could be provided closer to their homes,” he added.

fullParagraphs: On One Health, gender disparities in healthcare, emerging research, infectious diseases and more

Today, the world observes One Health Day, a period set aside to to remember that human, animal and environmental health are intricately inter-connected, a fact the human species seems to be increasingly forgetting or ignoring. It’s not for lack of reminders though: the natural world tells us, from time to time, in no uncertain terms that unless we give equal priority to all three -- and that means attention, funds and resources -- that we risk the spread of illnesses, the loss of cattle and crops, and increase climate disasters.

articles.title: IndiaAI Mission releases indigenous foundation models EKA-1, Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: These three indigenous models are a key milestone under the IndiaAI Mission, showcasing India's progress in creating homegrown AI technology

The IndiaAI Mission, under the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY), on Tuesday released indigenous foundation models EKA-1, developed by Soket Labs Technology and Research, and Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B, developed by ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations, marking another step in the country's push to build homegrown AI capabilities.
The models were unveiled at an event attended by IT Secretary S Krishnan, senior officials from the ministry and IndiaAI, as well as the leadership of both companies.
These three indigenous models are a key milestone under the IndiaAI Mission, showcasing India's progress in creating homegrown AI technology.

Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B enable offline-capable, document-grounded automation, knowledge retrieval and citizen or enterprise services across defence, government, industrial and educational sectors, particularly in low-connectivity or sensitive environments.
Both firms are among the teams selected under the IndiaAI Innovation Centre (Foundation Models) pillar, which aims to build indigenous AI capabilities and large language models.

The government said access to subsidised national AI compute infrastructure, along with support for ancillary research expenses, enabled the development of the models. It cited this as an example of how public AI infrastructure can speed up homegrown innovation.

Built for Indian languages, banking and cybersecurity, the EKA-1 has 26.3 billion parameters and was trained on about 7.5 trillion tokens. It covers all 22 scheduled Indian languages along with English. Soket describes it as an open, sparse hybrid language model designed for math, code, reasoning and agentic use.
EKA-1 can be used even without a mobile data or WiFi connection, as it has the capability to do certain inferencing on the local device, say a smartphone.

Soket CEO Abhishek Upperwal said the model has been tailored to India's banking, financial services and cybersecurity landscape. It is meant to address sector-specific requirements and understand the country's evolving digital ecosystem, he said.
ZenteiQ's Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B are open-source models that support English and 10 Indian languages. They can be deployed as secure, on-premise multilingual assistants.
According to an official release, the focus is on low-connectivity or sensitive environments.

ZenteiQ CEO Prof. Sashikumar said the models can run on different computing platforms, including GPUs and TPUs. Their lightweight architecture also allows on-device deployment on mobile phones without depending on cloud connectivity, he said.

articles.title: Suriya’s ‘Scene’: What’s the hype surrounding this Tamil Deepavali release?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil cinema’s Deepavali spotlight falls on Suriya’s ‘Scene,’ a quirky investigative drama directed by Jithu Madhavan that is releasing this weekend in theatres

Scene is the scene this Deepavali in Tamil Nadu. Tamil star Suriya ’s upcoming film, Scene , directed by Malayalam filmmaker Jithu Madhavan, has single-handedly taken on the Ramayana storm down South, becoming one of the most anticipated releases this Deepavali weekend.
But what is the whole hype surrounding this Deepavali release all about?

The biggest expectation for the film is whether it will become a hat-trick of hits for Suriya at the box office in 2026. With Karuppu , Suriya became a saving grace for Tamil cinema during a devastatingly poor first half of the year, while Vishwanath & Sons offered a refreshing detour from the gore- and action-heavy films we have been getting from the industry's top stars. And now, with Scene , Suriya might just as well claim the throne as one of the few modern-day stars to deliver three hits in a calendar year. Additionally, Scene is also set to feature Suriya as a cop. And we all know what happens when Suriya takes charge. All hail ‘The One’.

It’s been 12 years since Nazriya Nazim last appeared on the big screen in Tamil cinema. After 2013’s Raja Rani , Nazriya was one of the most promising young female leads in Tamil cinema, and everyone expected her to make big moves to the top. However, after her wedding in 2014 to Malayalam star Fahadh Faasil, Nazriya took a long hiatus from Tamil cinema, with Thirumanam Enum Nikkah as her last release. Even in Malayalam, the actor has been quite choosy with her roles, though her scene-stealing turn in the Telugu film Ante Sundaraniki came as a sweet surprise for fans. And now, with Scene , Nazriya is eyeing a comeback to Tamil cinema.

The craze young Tamil women have for Naslen has to be studied. Since 2024’s Premalu , Naslen has enjoyed a tremendous following across southern states, and with Scene , the Mollywood Times star is finally making his Tamil debut. However, that’s not particularly why Naslen fans might turn up to the theatres this Deepavali. With Scene , Naslen is shedding his chocolate-boy image by playing a serial killer, in what might be one of the first negative roles of his career. Talk about making an entrance!

No, we are not talking about the song from Theri . One of the key highlights of Scene is that it is helmed by Malayalam filmmaker Jithu Madhavan, a filmmaker whose previous two films, Romancham and Aavesham , got tremendous reception in Tamil Nadu. Jithu’s knack for humour and the hangover of watching Fahadh play the quirky gangster Ranga are enough promotion for Scene .

Open any ticketing platform on your device, and you will see a surprise. Yes, the early morning shows are back in Tamil Nadu. Scene will be one of the first films to enjoy six shows a day. This comes after the Tamil Nadu government on Tuesday announced that theatres across the State could now screen newly-released Tamil films for up to six shows a day, from 6 a.m. to 2.30 a.m. the following day, for one week from the date of release. This is the news cinema fans who know the allure of the early morning shows had been waiting for. It’s going to be a Scene festival at the theatres.

Content creator ‘Lungiboys’ Rajpriyan has played a pivotal role in Scene , while YouTuber Dravid Selvam of Parithabangal fame has penned the dialogues. If you have seen their sketches on social media, you know what to expect.

From the trailer, Scene seems to be a rather quirky investigative drama. Jithu’s frequent collaborator, music composer Sushin Shyam, is making his Tamil debut with Scene . Vineeth Augustian is the cinematographer, Ashwini Kale is the production designer, and Ajmal Sabu is the editor. Chethan D’Souza serves as the stunt choreographer. Suriya and Jyotika produce Scene under their Zhagaram Studios and 2D Entertainment banners.

articles.title: Telangana bus conductor Pravalika, who was pushed off moving bus, dies; she took up RTC job after father’s death
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Her death sparks outrage. TGSRTC staff protest across Khammam region.

The death of 24-year-old Telangana State Road Transport Corporation ( TGSRTC) conductor G. Pravalika, who succumbed to her injuries after allegedly being pushed off a moving bus by a woman passenger, triggered widespread protests by the Corporation’s employees across the Khammam region on Wednesday.

Drivers and conductors boycotted duties, demanding stringent punishment for the accused and justice for Pravalika’s bereaved mother, whose hopes of seeing her daughter build a better future were shattered by the tragedy.

Pravalika, a conductor attached to the Manuguru depot, was allegedly pushed off the moving bus by a woman passenger near Mittagudem in Aswapuram mandal on October 25 following an argument over the money due after issuing a ticket to the passenger’s son.

The conductor’s legs came under the rear wheels of the bus, leaving her critically injured. She succumbed to her injuries on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) night after battling for life for nearly 10 days.
Police had already arrested the accused, identified as Mounika of Mittagudem, and initially registered a case of attempt to murder. The case was reportedly altered following Pravalika’s death.
TGSRTC employees paid homage to Pravalika at the Khammam bus depot and staged a demonstration wearing black badges under the aegis of the TGSRTC Khammam Region JAC.
Recalling her dedication to duty, employees said Pravalika had joined the corporation on compassionate grounds following her father’s death over 10 months ago.
They demanded stern punishment for the accused as per law and foolproof safety measures for drivers and conductors.
Meanwhile, bus services across seven depots in the erstwhile undivided Khammam district were disrupted until Wednesday afternoon.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: All 70 gates of Prakasam Barrage opened; 71,000 cusecs released into Krishna
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The inflows come largely from the Keesara, Munneru and Budameru streams after heavy rain in NTR district

Heavy rain continues in the Krishna basin under the influence of Cyclone Murasu . The Water Resources Department (WRD) has suspended water supply to canals and opened all 70 gates of the Prakasam Barrage to send the surplus flow downstream.

The Prakasam Barrage was receiving 71,000 cusecs at 8 a.m. on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), and the entire quantity was being released into the Krishna river towards the Bay of Bengal. The water level stood at 12 feet.

Floodwater flows through the open gates of the Prakasam Barrage across the Krishna in Vijayawada on Wednesday. All 70 gates have been opened after two days of heavy rain from Cyclone Murasu. Video: K.V.S. Giri https://t.co/GtrzTzb0N2

To facilitate the discharge, 30 gates had been raised by two feet and another 40 by one foot. WRD officials have stopped releases into the Krishna Eastern, Krishna Western and Guntur canals as a precaution against possible flooding.

The inflows are being fed largely by the Keesara, Munneru and Budameru streams, which drain into the Krishna from the local catchment areas. Surplus releases from the barrage began on Tuesday night after inflows increased.
The decision to regulate the discharge comes amid reports of exceptionally heavy rainfall in NTR district and forecasts of more rain by the India Meteorological Department.

Officials are keeping a close watch on the river’s inflows and the situation in the upstream catchment areas. Residents in low-lying settlements along the Krishna riverbanks have been asked to exercise caution and comply with instructions from the authorities.

Edlapadu in Palnadu district received the most rain in the State in the 24 hours ending 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday, 269.45 mm, according to the Andhra Pradesh Directorate of Economics and Statistics (APDES). Sixteen automatic weather station gauges in the state stations crossed 204.5 mm mark, the India Meteorological Department (IMD)’s threshold for extremely heavy rain.
In NTR district, Chintalapadu in Tiruvuru mandal recorded 178.25 mm. Ghantasala in Krishna district got 222.75 mm.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: Ramanaidu puts irrigation officials on high alert over swollen rivers, drains
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Nallamada and Parchur drains are flowing above their maximum levels around Parchur, Bapatla and Chirala

Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Minister Nimmala Ramanaidu has directed irrigation officials to remain on high alert in view of heavy rainfall triggered by Cyclone Murasu and take immediate steps to drain rainwater stagnating in agricultural fields to prevent further damage to crops.

During a teleconference with senior irrigation officials on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), the Minister called for continuous monitoring of flood flows in rivers, streams, drains and reservoirs and coordination with other departments to manage the situation.

The Minister said heavy rainfall had been reported in Palnadu, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Krishna, Eluru and West Godavari districts. The Nallamada and Parchur drains were flowing above their maximum levels in areas around Parchur, Bapatla, Chirala and Prattipadu. He asked officials to remain vigilant and take precautionary measures.

Mr. Ramanaidu directed officials to ensure that rainwater accumulated in agricultural fields was drained immediately through canals and drains. He also asked them to monitor field conditions continuously and ensure that farmers did not face difficulties.

He instructed officials to keep a close watch on flood inflows into the Budameru, Errakalava, Goneruvagu, Tammileru and Yeleru rivers and streams, as well as reservoirs, particularly in view of heavy rainfall in their upstream catchments.

The Minister said the Prakasam Barrage was receiving an inflow of 71,000 cusecs from streams in Guntur and Palnadu districts. Water from the Budameru catchment was being diverted into the Krishna through the Budameru Diversion Canal, he added.

Floodwater flows through the open gates of the Prakasam Barrage across the Krishna in Vijayawada on Wednesday. All 70 gates have been opened after two days of heavy rain from Cyclone Murasu. Video: K.V.S. Giri https://t.co/GtrzTzb0N2
He called for continuous monitoring of inflows into the Prakasam Barrage and effective flood management.
Referring to the heavy rainfall in Vijayawada over the past two days, Mr. Ramanaidu said 3,000 cusecs of water was being diverted into the sea through the Enikepadu under-tunnel.

He also asked officials in the north coastal districts to take advance precautions in view of heavy rainfall. In East Godavari district, where widespread rain was reported, officials were instructed to visit affected areas, assess the situation regularly and take all necessary measures to prevent inconvenience to the public and farmers.

Irrigation Special Chief Secretary Shashi Bhushan, adviser Venkateswara Rao, Engineer-in-Chief Narasimha Murthy and several chief engineers and superintending engineers participated in the teleconference.

articles.title: 60-day prohibitive orders passed ‘ex-parte’ to prevent unrest in key capital zones: Delhi Police in Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Six orders issued on August 20 or immediately before or after this date, came a month after the July 20 protests witnessed violence in New Delhi district; one of them imposes prohibitions from September 26 to November 24

Seven separate prohibitive orders passed by the Delhi Police under Section 163 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in the national capital show restrictions concerning free movement were imposed way before protests erupted demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Six orders issued on August 20 or immediately before or after this date, came a month after the July 20 protests against alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leaks witnessed violence in New Delhi district, the power and commercial heart of the capital city. One of them imposes prohibitions from September 26 to November 24.

The prohibitive orders are for a maximum period of 60 days, till the latter half of October. They are ex-parte or without hearing any objections, saying “notice cannot be served individually on all concerned”.

The orders, which are part of an affidavit filed by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar in the Supreme Court, said “reports have been received indicate that such conditions now exists that unrestricted holding of public meetings, processions/demonstrations, etc, in the area are likely to cause obstruction to traffic, danger to human safety and disturbance of public tranquility”.
The police reasoned in the orders that it was necessary to take “speedy measures” to “prevent danger to human life or safety and disturbance to public tranquility”.

The seven orders comprise the police sub-divisions of Connaught Place, Tughlak Road, Parliament Street, Chanakya Puri — where the Prime Minister’s residence, Rashtrapati Bhavan, foreign embassies, and other vital installations are located — Barakhamba Road, Safdarjung Enclave in south-west Delhi, and Defence Colony.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Anti-CEC protest fallout: Supreme Court issues fresh directions to Centre, Delhi Police

The orders prohibited activities, including the holding of any public meeting, shouting of slogans, making speeches, picketing or dharnas, assembly of five or more persons, carrying fire arms, banners, placards, lathis, spears, swords, sticks, brickbats, etc.

The affidavit from the police chief came in response to a host of petitions filed by politicians, party leaders, activists, lawyers and private individuals — including CPI(M) state secretary M.A. Baby, Rajya Sabha MP A.A. Rahim, senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy, advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi and others — against the indiscriminate detentions of leaders, former Chief Ministers, students, youths, journalists, lawyers, and others by the Delhi Police, against the rule of law and democratic dissent on October 10-11 during protests seeking the resignation of the CEC.

The petitioners had alleged around 7,000 en masse illegal detentions during the protests, and shutting down of vital public transport systems, including the Delhi Metro, leaving thousands of commuters stranded in the national capital. Major roads had been heavily barricaded with the heavy presence of security personnel, and trains to Delhi were cancelled on October 10 amidst the detentions.

Mr. Tripathi, through his counsel Chand Qureshi, had argued in the apex court that the shutdown was in clear violation of an October 9 order of the Supreme Court, which had emphasised that the authorities must not cause any hardship or suffering to ordinary commuters through a blanket ban.
This had led the Supreme Court to direct the Delhi Police to place on record the specific prohibitive orders.

articles.title: Trump-backed Indian-American Vivek Ramaswamy loses Ohio Governor’s race
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Vivek Ramaswamy lost to Amy Acton, who became the first woman to be elected Governor of the state
Indian-American Vivek Ramaswamy, who was backed by U.S. President Donald Trump, lost Ohio's gubernatorial race to Democrat Amy Acton.
Mr. Ramaswamy, 41, lost to 60-year-old Ms. Acton, who became the first woman to be elected Governor of the state.
Ms. Acton bagged over 51% of the votes while Mr. Ramaswamy won over 45%.

In concession remarks in Ohio after losing the Governor's race, Mr. Ramaswamy said: "It was a tough race. It was bitter at times in both directions... All of us in this room should be rooting for the success of her administration," C-SPAN quoted him as saying.
The billionaire also thanked his parents, his wife and her parents for their support.
Mr. Ramaswamy lost despite having top strategists from his and Vice President JD Vance’s political teams advising him, NBC News reported.

Mr. Ramaswamy, who made an unsuccessful bid against Trump for the Republican presidential nomination in 2024, pumped more than $36 million in loans from his personal fortune into the race, The Washington Post reported.
He also received millions of dollars in donations from fellow billionaires Elon Musk and Jeffrey Yass, NBC News reported.

Days ahead of the election, Mr. Ramaswamy drew criticism for the decision to air an ad in which Acton’s mother, Donna Arthur, called her daughter a liar and urged Ohioans not to vote for her, the report said.
Ms. Acton said she has not seen or spoken with Arthur in nearly 50 years and has accused her mother’s then-husband of sexually abusing her as a child, it said.
Mr. Ramaswamy helped Elon Musk plan President Donald Trump’s Department of Government Efficiency initiative to overhaul the federal government.
After quitting the post, Mr. Ramaswamy received an endorsement from Mr. Trump. The President travelled to Ohio to lend his support to Mr. Ramaswamy.

articles.title: Israel's unassuming President Herzog holds keys to next government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Isaac Herzog said he would do everything he could to avoid a fresh election — a possibility if neither camp can cobble together a coalition — including backing a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot
Israel's President Isaac Herzog is known for his unassuming and mild manner, but all eyes will be on him as he decides whom to task with forming the next coalition government.
The decision is a weighty one as neither the camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor that of his rival Gadi Eisenkot secured a majority in parliament.

Mr. Herzog starts consultations on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) with party representatives as he decides on a candidate who has the best chance of forming a government — not necessarily the one whose party holds the most seats.
Under the law, the president, whose position is otherwise largely ceremonial, is afforded broad discretion, with no guidelines on how to make the choice.
Mr. Herzog has called for all efforts to be made to avoid a new election. "I expect everyone who comes here to come with an open mind," he said shortly after the election.

Ahead of the October 27 vote, Mr. Herzog acknowledged there would be tremendous pressure, but vowed not to let outside influence, notably from U.S. President Donald Trump, sway his decision. "I don't think the president of the United States or anybody else can intervene in my discretion," he told U.S. outlet MS Now.
"It's Israel's democracy and Israel's constitution, and that's what counts for me."

Mr. Herzog said he would do everything he could to avoid a fresh election — a possibility if neither camp can cobble together a coalition — including backing a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot.
Modest, diplomatic and with a strong political pedigree, 66-year-old Herzog was sworn in as Israel's president in 2021 after being elected by lawmakers in a landslide.
Yair Lapid, now a member of Eisenkot's broad opposition bloc, praised Herzog at the time as "a worthy and wonderful man who is always focused on the good of the country and the Jewish people".
As president, Mr. Herzog has faced pressure from Mr. Trump to grant Mr. Netanyahu a pardon in his long-running corruption trials, which could land him in prison if he loses power.
In April, Mr. Herzog invited Mr. Netanyahu's lawyers and prosecutors to his residence for talks on the issue.

Under the law, the president, whose position is otherwise largely ceremonial, is afforded broad discretion, with no guidelines on how to make the choice.

Mr. Herzog has called for all efforts to be made to avoid a new election. "I expect everyone who comes here to come with an open mind," he said shortly after the election.

Ahead of the October 27 vote, Mr. Herzog acknowledged there would be tremendous pressure, but vowed not to let outside influence, notably from U.S. President Donald Trump, sway his decision. "I don't think the president of the United States or anybody else can intervene in my discretion," he told U.S. outlet MS Now.

"It's Israel's democracy and Israel's constitution, and that's what counts for me."

Mr. Herzog said he would do everything he could to avoid a fresh election — a possibility if neither camp can cobble together a coalition — including backing a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot.

Modest, diplomatic and with a strong political pedigree, 66-year-old Herzog was sworn in as Israel's president in 2021 after being elected by lawmakers in a landslide.

Yair Lapid, now a member of Eisenkot's broad opposition bloc, praised Herzog at the time as "a worthy and wonderful man who is always focused on the good of the country and the Jewish people".

As president, Mr. Herzog has faced pressure from Mr. Trump to grant Mr. Netanyahu a pardon in his long-running corruption trials, which could land him in prison if he loses power.

In April, Mr. Herzog invited Mr. Netanyahu's lawyers and prosecutors to his residence for talks on the issue.

articles.title: Why psoriasis can sometimes be hard to diagnose and when you need to see a doctor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Psoriasis can often resemble other skin conditions, making it important to know the signs and seek medical help early when necessary

Psoriasis is an autoimmune condition that causes thick, scaly patches on the skin. However, it often remains unidentified and undiagnosed because it does not look the same on all parts of the body: it could be mistaken, for instance, for dandruff on the scalp, persistent eczema on the palms, or a fungal infection. You can’t always judge psoriasis by looking only at visible parts of the skin.

Why does this happen? Our skin isn’t the same everywhere. The thickness of the skin can vary considerably depending on the diversity of the environmental conditions that it is exposed to and the kind of treatment given to it. These factors can contribute to how psoriasis appears and feels.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu takes baby steps towards conservation of Bengal fox, golden jackal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The State government has sanctioned ₹1.3 crore this year for comprehensive assessment of current threats, habitat use, and distribution patterns to develop an effective, long-term conservation roadmap.
The Tamil Nadu government is taking baby steps towards conservation of Bengal foxes and golden jackals which are critical to ensure the ecological balance of the habitats.

In his March 2025 Budget speech, the then Forests Minister K. Ponmudy had announced in the State Legislative Assembly of a conservation plan for the Bengal fox and jackal, which are critical to maintain the ecological balance of the habitats.

Tamil Nadu, renowned for its exceptional biodiversity, has diverse ecosystems — from coastal plains to mountainous terrains. Among the many species that inhabit these landscapes are the Indian Bengal fox (Vulpes bengalensis) and the golden jackal (Canis aureus), both of which play vital roles in maintaining ecological balance as predators and scavengers.

Both species are presently listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, affording them the highest level of legal protection in India. The level of their decline in the recent past was made out from the fact that the Indian Bengal fox and the golden jackal were both listed in Schedule V (Vermin category) when the Wildlife (Protection) Act was enacted in 1972.

Advanced Institute for Wildlife Conservation (AIWC) had conducted a preliminary study to identify their presence in landscapes across Tamil Nadu and found that their numbers and ranges had dwindled over the past three to four decades. The survey indicated that they had disappeared in many districts and were found only in pockets in the districts of Dharmapuri, Tiruvannamalai, Salem, Villupuram and Madurai.

The government then decided that immediate conservation interventions were necessary keeping in mind their ecological importance and growing threats faced by them. The Chief Wildlife Warden had sent a proposal to the government for funding for comprehensive assessment of current threats, habitat use, and distribution patterns to develop an effective, long-term conservation roadmap.

The objectives were identification of critical habitats in and outside Protected Areas (PA)and Reserved Forests, habitat protection and improvement measures and control of poaching, creation of awareness on the need to conserve these species amongst the various stakeholders and an establishment of a captive breeding centre in Salem Zoo.

The erstwhile DMK government accorded administrative and financial sanction for ₹2 crore but it required the approval of the Legislature by inclusion in the revised Supplementary Estimates for the year 2025-26. Now, the Chief Wildlife Warden has sent a proposal for ₹92.5 lakh and use the unspent balance from the last fiscal. The State government, after careful consideration, agreed to the proposal and sanctioned ₹1.3 crore this year.

However, forest officials said the conservation plan would require an inter-departmental coordination as these two are considered edge-species, living between the forests and the agricultural landscapes.

articles.title: AgriNova: When a farm can text and call you!
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Coming from the minds of two young innovators, this machine serves to form a line of communication between a farm and its farmer.

According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, 40% of global food crops are lost each year due to pests. The importance of protecting crops from pests, animal intruders, and over-irrigation holds great importance not just within the boundaries of a farmer’s field, but even the places and actions that lay beyond it.

Whenever you wish to ask someone for help or send an important message, giving it directly to the recipient is usually far more efficient than using many middlemen, where the message could easily get changed or altered. The game Chinese Whisper demonstrates this. However, in the real world, inaccurate messages can lead to major consequences. Hearing a message directly from the (reliable) source is the best way to avoid these consequences.

In the same way, what if a farm had the ability to call or send out an alert to its farmer when something feels wrong, or tell him or her exactly what it needs? Well, thanks to the work of two seventh-standard students Rohan Lanka and Sarthak, the foundation for this solution may have just taken the first step in its creation!

The concept of this machine is quite simple. Think of it as a communication device for a farm. Built to be a machine controlled either by Telegram or WhatsApp (the latter currently still in the works), AgriNova allows a farmer to receive messages from their own farm regarding the soil moisture, intruders, etc. Because of this, a farmer can be alerted as and when a problem is detected, and ensure that their farm is in good shape without having to actually go outside. They could also receive messages when they are travelling. The alert can come in the form of a phone call from the farm. Yes, that’s right. A ‘phone call’ from the farm! If there were a problem, the sensors on the farm would detect it, narrow down the issue, and immediately call the farmer to let them know!

(From left) Rohan Lanka and Sarthak, Class VII, Army Public School Shankar Vihar, with AgriNova — their ₹2,500 smart farm that texts, and even phones, the farmer — at the Purple Umbrella Festival 2026, New Delhi. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

In an interview with The Hindu TeenDigest , the seventh-standard students behind AgriNova – Rohan Lanka and Sarthak, from Army Public School Shankar Vihar, New Delhi – provided explanations on the inspiration behind AgriNova, as well as the creation process, the obstacles they faced, and their future plans for their machine.

Rohan stated that it had been a trip to his hometown that brought attention to the problem. What was witnessed had brought light to the issue. “Some farmers turn on the water supply for their crops and leave it running throughout the night.” This sparked attention to the first problem: “That wastes a lot of water, and most of the crops end up dying,” he explained. Sarthak added that they had learnt of two instances when the farmers lost their crop. “Once, to the stray animals at night,” and second, to the act of “watering by habit, instead of by need.”

When plants are given more water than they need, that could lead to many problems, including soil erosion and waterlogging. While there are many other causes for crop loss, these two (stray animals and over-irrigation) were some of the main causes that drew the attention of Rohan and Sarthak and slowly motivated them to build AgriNova. Agricultural runoff is also said to be one of the main sources of contamination of water bodies. So, it is important to ensure that the soil is provided with the right amount of water (not too much) and moisture, which will allow the crop to grow in a healthy manner.

The process of creating AgriNova came with its ups and downs. “We created a blueprint on a piece of paper first before starting,” Rohan explained. They then showed it to the person in charge of their school’s ATL (Atal Tinkering Lab). “He’s the one who supervised us and sent us to the Purple Umbrella Festival, a national-level competition, where AgriNova was selected as a finalist.”
The model used to demonstrate the machine, and its various parts. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

a. IR sensor: “First,” Rohan began, “we added the IR sensor, just in case somebody comes when they are not supposed to come. It sends an alert to the farmer.” Through this, the farm will call the farmer to “tell them that somebody has entered, and send them a video or a photo.” Thus, the farmer will have a visual warning (as well as evidence) in the case of any unwanted party entering their fields. When it comes to the replication of the model into the field, “if an IR sensor lies, we will remove it.” Sarthak said, emphasising the importance of ensuring the efficiency of their machine.

b. Soil moisture sensor & water module: This part of AgriNova answers the problem of understanding the right amount of water a crop requires. “When the soil is detected as dry,” Rohan explained, “it (the machine) just starts spraying water to make it wet again. That’s auto-irrigation.”

The importance of protecting crops from pests, animal intruders, and over-irrigation holds great importance not just within the boundaries of a farmer’s field, but even the places and actions that lay beyond it.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: b. articles.title: Urologists work as casualty medical officers in emergency depts. owing to lack of vacancies across T.N.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Sources say no new posts had been created in urology departments over the years. Several government medical college hospitals have only one urologist, while those in Karur, Sivagangai, Tiruppur, Tiruvannamalai, Ariyalur, and Kallakurichi have no urology services, despite urologists having been posted in emergency departments

With no vacancies in their super speciality department, 12 government urologists, who completed their M.Ch. Urology in 2025, have been working as casualty medical officers (CMO) at emergency departments (EDs) of government medical college hospitals for nearly a year, providing emergency care and making entries in accident registries every day.

The urologists were among service postgraduates who completed DM/M.Ch. in 2025. While most of them were posted to their parent departments, some, were assigned as CMOs, including in new medical college hospitals functioning without super speciality departments.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections impact on India: faster trade deal talks and higher tariffs likely
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Trade and geopolitical experts say that losing control of the U.S. Congress will push President Donald Trump to increase tariff pressure on India to seal a deal. Indian negotiators, for their part, will smell an opportunity

The results of the U.S. midterm elections, which show that the Democrats have gained control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, will likely speed up talks between India and the U.S. on a trade deal but could also see higher tariffs on India until the deal is closed, according to experts.

On the one hand, a desire to now quickly close the trade deal to show strength domestically could induce Mr. Trump to increase his tariff pressure on India, while on the other, Indian negotiators will likely see this election result as an opportunity to push through a favourable deal for India.
U.S. midterm elections: Follow LIVE updates from the results on November 4, 2026

According to Ajay Srivastava, founder of the trade think-tank Global Trade Research Initiative, this loss will push U.S. President Donald Trump to increase his exercise of his executive powers to pressure India into accepting a deal.
“With foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win,” Mr. Srivastava said. “Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout.”

Leaders in the U.S. and India have repeatedly said over the last few months that the deal between the two countries is nearly ready and is awaiting final approvals. India, in particular, has been holding out until it receives an assurance that it will win a clear advantage over its competitors.

“Trump will now use his executive powers to pressure India for a quick deal that secures market access for U.S. agricultural and industrial goods, alongside other major concessions for U.S. companies,” Mr. Srivastava said.

While the U.S. Supreme Court in February defanged Mr. Trump’s reciprocal tariff policy that had seen tariffs of up to 50% being levied on India, the President has other tools through which he can levy tariffs.

According to Deep Pal, Director of Geopolitics and Policy at the Koan Advisory Group, the implications of these election results might lead to some difficulty for Mr. Trump in gaining support for his policies.

“For this administration, especially after tonight, any decision has to look like a win domestically, to core Republican voters,” Mr. Pal said. “With Congress out of his hands, a lot will depend on how much control Mr. Trump has over the Republican party and if there will be any purchase for his ideas.”
However, Mr. Pal pointed out that the Indian government might view this new reality in the U.S. with greater optimism.

“Indian negotiators, on the other hand, may think that the new realities will make the Trump administration amenable to a better trade deal for India, breaking the current deadlock, and leading to a flurry of new conversations,” Mr. Pal said.
