articles.title: SC stays Madras HC order on Chidambaram temple
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Questions whether High Courts have parens patriae jurisdiction only over public temples and not places of worship of other faiths

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) questioned whether State High Courts have parens patriae (guardian) jurisdiction only over public temples and not places of worship of other faiths while staying a Madras High Court order that constituted a Board of Management to administer the ancient Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple in Tamil Nadu back to glory.

A Bench of Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi issued notice to the State of Tamil Nadu and froze the implementation of the October 30 High Court order, which said the Podhu Dikshidar (a hereditary community of priests) had maladministered the temple ever since its running was handed over to them following orders passed by the Supreme Court in 2014.

The High Court had appointed retired judges V. Bharathidasan and R. Suresh Kumar to chair the Board of Management (BoM). Retired IAS officer C. Rajendran was designated its member, and the secretary of the Podhu Dikshidar’s association and the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department secretary would be the ex-officio members.

The BoM, in consultation with the Tamil Nadu Heritage Commission, was ordered to undertake the removal of unauthorised constructions put up on the temple premises that caused damage to the ancient structure. The High Court Bench had tasked the BoM to take steps to retrieve the temple properties under encroachment with the help of the district administration.

Appearing for Tamil Nadu government, senior advocates Shekhar Naphade and Jaideep Gupta submitted that there was severe damage caused to the property and the Podhu Dikshidars had not shared the full accounts of the income derived from the temple in the last 12 years.
Mr. Naphade said the High Court had parens patriae jurisdiction over public temples to protect the interest of the presiding deity, considered as juristic person by law.
“Is this parens patriae only for temples or other places of worship?” Justice Kumar asked the State government.
Mr. Naphade responded that the law only recognised parens patriae jurisdiction for public temples, not churches or other places of worship of faiths.
Senior advocate Sai Deepak Iyer, for the opposite side, submitted that the court should look into why parens patriae doctrine applied to temples alone.
“Please, do not make any sweeping statements,” Justice Kumar said.
Mr. Gupta said the primary question was whether the temple was in danger or not. Mr. Naphade said, “This is a prime instance of what maladministration would happen on returning a temple”.

articles.title: Why even a strong El Niño does not guarantee a poor Indian monsoon
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Seven Indian monsoons since 1950 have run into a moderate or strong El Niño. Of these, in five years, including 2026, monsoon rainfall levels were at least 10% lower than the long-term average. The IMD refers to this level as 'deficient’. The 2023 season was something of an exception with ‘below average’ rainfall. However, 1997 had ‘average’ rainfall

In the summer of 1997, one of the strongest El Niños of the 20th century took shape in the Pacific Ocean. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicted a monsoon rainfall deficit of 8% below the average, as was expected in El Niño years. However, by the end of September that year, rainfall levels were nearly normal.

This year, a “ferocious” El Niño is taking shape, and is expected to peak only in December. The 2026 southwest monsoon ended nearly 13% below the long-term average of 87 cm. East and Northeast India had their driest season since records began in 1901.

articles.title: With no illegal immigrants found on draft electoral rolls, SIR greatly inconvenienced people: Owaisi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Qadeemi Masjid was there before Delhi became the national capital, says AIMIM president

Hyderabad parliamentarian Asaduddin Owaisi on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) said the claim of illegal immigrants being included in electoral rolls had caused considerable hardship, particularly to the poor, who lost at least two days’ wages completing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process, even as officials said there was no evidence of illegal migrants being included in the draft electoral rolls.

Referring to the statement made by Hyderabad District Election Officer R.V. Karnan, that no foreign nationals or illegal migrants were found in the draft electoral rolls after the revision exercise, Mr. Owaisi said the finding had exposed the claims repeatedly made by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Sangh parivar leaders as false. He said that thousands of people were put through the verification process and daily wage earners were forced to forego income to furnish documents and complete enrolment formalities.

Touching upon the issue of Qadeemi Masjid located within the Krishi Bhavan complex in New Delhi , Mr. Owaisi criticised the Union government’s attempts to remove the structure as part of the Common Central Secretariat redevelopment under the Central Vista project. Earlier in the day, he had posted on X that the Centre had informed the Delhi High Court that the masjid was “impermissible and incompatible with the secular character of government property” and therefore needed to be removed.

Mr. Owaisi, who is the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) president, noted that the Central Vista project itself was inaugurated with a Bhoomi Pooja (ground breaking ceremony) and remarked that “secularism is not offended by the use of one faith’s rituals for a public project, but is allergic to a masjid that has stood there even before 1912”. He said the masjid predated Krishi Bhavan and even the development of Lutyens’ Delhi.

The AIMIM chief said the masjid was part of the country’s cultural heritage and had not been included in the land acquisition process undertaken by the British for the development of New Delhi. He sought Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju’s intervention and said the government should recognise the historical and legal status of the mosque. He added that any dispute over the property could be adjudicated before the Waqf Tribunal. “The mosque was there before Delhi became the national capital. What exactly do they want to do with it now?” he asked.

Mr. Owaisi also criticised what he described as attempts to diminish the political aspirations of Muslims. Recalling remarks often made by BJP leaders about “Abdul” being confined to repairing punctures, he said Muslims would no longer be intimidated by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and would emerge as political leaders.

articles.title: Cabinet clears ₹14,500 crore viability gap funding scheme for 92 GWh battery energy storage systems
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh storage capacity across three technologies — Battery Energy Storage System (30 GWh), Pumped Storage Projects (60 GWh) and Emerging Storage Technologies (2GW)
The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) approved ₹14,500 crore in viability gap funding for 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage systems between FY27 and FY31.
This development is significant given India's ambitious target of 500 GW of renewable energy by 2030.

The scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh storage capacity across three technologies — Battery Energy Storage System (30 GWh), Pumped Storage Projects (60 GWh) and Emerging Storage Technologies (2GW), Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said in a media briefing in New Delhi.
The Minister said the scheme will be implemented for five years till 2030-31.

articles.title: Union Cabinet approves ₹14,500 crore VGF scheme to develop large scale energy storage in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The scheme is designed to provide for the development of hydro pumped storage plant (PSP) capacity, battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity, as well as alternative energy storage technologies

The Union Cabinet has approved a ₹14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme for the development of grid-scale energy storage systems for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31, the government announced on Wednesday.
According to the government, the scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh of fresh, yet-to-be-commissioned, energy storage capacity across the country.

“The scheme will support creation of new capacities equivalent to 170% of the present-day grid scale energy storage system capacity in the country and help meet the required grid scale ESS capacity of 411 GWh by 2031-32,” the government said in a release.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Can battery storage save India’s renewable energy grid? | Business Matters

The scheme is designed to provide for the development of 60 GWh of hydro pumped storage plant (PSP) capacity, 30 GWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity and 2 GWh of capacity through alternative energy storage technologies, with a total estimated investment of ₹97,600 crore.

“The VGF support will help improve the financial viability of these projects and accelerate the deployment of large-scale energy storage infrastructure in the country,” the government said, adding that the scheme will also provide an impetus to domestic manufacturing of battery energy storage systems.

As per the government’s release, energy storage capacity will be allocated through a tariff-based competitive bidding process with both public and private sector electricity distribution companies eligible for VGF support for BESS and hydro PSP projects.
Projects based on alternative energy storage technologies, too, will be implemented by public and private sector entities.

“To promote indigenous manufacturing, BESS projects will be subject to a minimum Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) of 40%,” the government added. “The requirement will encourage domestic manufacturing, create opportunities for Indian industry and complement existing supply-side incentives for battery manufacturing.”

articles.title: Supreme Court upholds States’ power to levy additional sales tax, says case has become academic
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The seven-judge Bench, led by CJI Surya Kant, said the reference in the Orissa Sales Tax Act case no longer requires adjudication since the challenged provisions have been amended and GST governs the issue moving forward

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) held that a 1974 Constitution Bench ruling upholding States’ power to impose additional sales tax or surcharge calculated as a percentage of the existing sales tax continues to hold the field, saying a reference on the issue had become academic.

A seven-judge Constitution Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant unanimously held that the legal question referred to it nearly 27 years ago no longer required adjudication, as the statutory provisions under challenge had since been replaced or amended and the Goods and Services Tax (GST) law had come into force.

“The question referred to is of no practical significance and now academic. Consequently, the question referred to does not survive for adjudication by a seven-judge Bench, and the reference has to be answered accordingly,” the CJI, who wrote the judgment on behalf of himself and five other judges, said.
The Bench also comprised Justices K.V. Viswanathan, S.V.N. Bhatti, Joymalya Bagchi, N.V. Anjaria, Arun Palli and V. Mohana.
Justice Viswanathan wrote a separate concurring verdict.

While declining to undertake a fresh adjudication on the reference, the Court clarified that the five-judge Constitution Bench ruling in S. Kodar vs State of Kerala (1974) continued to hold the field.
The earlier judgment had upheld additional sales tax, rejecting the argument that such a levy amounted to a tax on the income of dealers.

“We have clarified that the case clearly held that an additional tax or surcharge computed as a percentage of the sales tax payable is an enhancement of the rate of sales tax and a tax on the sale or purchase of goods within Entry 54 of List II, as it then stood. That decision continues to hold the field,” the CJI said.
The Court further held that the question of the legislative competence of State legislatures to impose the surcharge would be governed by the law laid down in S. Kodar.

The reference arose from a challenge to Section 5A of the Orissa Sales Tax Act, 1947, which provided for additional tax at the rate of 10% on dealers with an annual turnover between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore, and 15% on dealers whose turnover exceeded ₹1 crore.

The appellants questioned whether the State legislature was competent to impose such a levy under Entry 54 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, which empowered States to tax the sale or purchase of goods, or whether it effectively amounted to a tax on income, a subject falling within Parliament’s domain under Entry 82 of List I.

The controversy stemmed from differing interpretations in earlier Supreme Court decisions. In S. Kodar vs State of Kerala, a five-judge Bench had upheld additional sales tax, ruling that a levy calculated with reference to the sales tax payable was an enhancement of the sales tax rate and not a tax on the dealer’s income.

articles.title: Services sector activity hits 4-month high in October as business conditions improve cautiously
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Survey participants identified new business growth as the main driver behind the rise in output, the survey said

India's services sector activity recorded the strongest pace of expansion in four months in October as demand buoyancy fuelled growth in business activity and new orders amid easing cost pressures, a monthly survey said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Companies were cautiously optimistic about the outlook, and they lifted jobs to the least extent in four months. The latest expansion in international sales was the weakest in almost four years.
The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Services PMI Business Activity Index rose from 55.2 in September to 55.8 in October, indicating the strongest pace of growth for four months.
In the Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) parlance, a print above 50 means expansion, while a score below 50 denotes contraction.

"India's services PMI rose to 55.8 in October, a four-month high, as business conditions improved cautiously. Although overall demand remained fairly strong, new export orders recorded the slowest pace of expansion since February 2023," Pranjul Bhandari, Chief India Economist at HSBC, said.

Survey participants identified new business growth as the main driver behind the rise in output, the survey said, adding that favourable demand conditions, new client wins and successful advertising boosted new order intakes.

On the prices front, there was a substantial decline in cost pressures. "Input and output prices continued to rise, but at a slower pace than in the previous month, signalling some relief from inflation pressures," Bhandari said.
Employment growth also slowed to its weakest pace since June, suggesting that some service sector businesses have sufficient capacity to meet current staffing requirements, she said.
Companies were, however, cautiously optimistic about the outlook, and they lifted jobs to the least extent in four months.
Meanwhile, India's composite PMI increased to 56.2 in October, from 55.9 in September, marking the fastest rise in aggregate output in four months and reflecting healthy business activity.

"New business intakes at the composite level also expanded at a quicker rate, one that was the most pronounced since June. Yet, job creation softened, and businesses were less upbeat towards growth prospects than they were in September," the report said.
Cost pressures receded at manufacturing firms and their services counterparts, dragging down the aggregate rate of inflation to an 11-month low.

articles.title: China must make extradition request if it wants two Uyghur men returned: Thailand
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The two men, in letters shared last week, pleaded not to be sent back to China

Thailand said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that China must make a formal extradition request if it wants two Uyghur men returned, in response to growing concerns and fears of abuse or torture if they are returned. The two men, in letters shared last week, pleaded not to be sent back to China.

Thailand’s head of the National Security Council Chaipruak Doungprapat said his agency will not make a decision on their deportation, unlike the case of 40 Uyghur men who were sent back to China last year . He said the process will go through the courts and the men will be able to defend themselves. If the court rules in their favour, it’s possible for them to be sent to another country for resettlement.
“But if the court rules against them, they will be extradited according to the treaty. This is the judicial process,” he said.

Human rights activists and some Thai politicians have raised concerns in recent days that the two men, who have been held in Thailand for more than a decade, will be sent back to China imminently. The two men were released from prison in late October and are currently held at the Suan Plu immigration detention centre in Bangkok.

China has consistently pushed for the return of a group of 300 Uyghurs who were detained by Thai authorities in 2014 when they were on their way to the Thai-Malaysia border, saying they were terrorists.

China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Mao Ning on Wednesday said “China and Thailand’s cooperation in combating cross-border crimes, including illegal immigration, is in accordance with the laws of both countries, as well as international law and international practice.” Ms. Mao didn't comment on whether China had sent an extradition request.

The two men, a 26-year-old and a 35-year-old, wrote letters that were then shared publicly last week. “Every time we are worrying from China to take back us,” one of them wrote in a letter shared by Kannavee Suebsang, a former lawmaker and founder of the Peace Rights Foundation, a human rights group that represents the men. “We aren’t terrorist," the Uyghur man wrote.

Sasinan Thamnithinan, a lawmaker from the Opposition People's Party, said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that Thailand is obligated by both domestic and international law to ensure that no individual is returned to a country where they could face torture or inhumane treatment.

“Maintaining international relations is important, but it must not take precedence over human rights and the rule of law. No one should be sent back to face danger simply because the government wants to end a problem,” Ms. Sasinan said in a statement.

Uyghurs are a Turkic, majority Muslim ethnic group native to Xinjiang in China's northwest. After decades of conflict with Beijing over discrimination and suppression of their cultural identity, the Chinese government launched a brutal crackdown on the Uyghurs that some Western governments have called a genocide.

The two men were part of a group of more than 300 Uyghurs fleeing China that were detained in 2014 by Thai authorities near the Malaysian border. Of this group, Thailand sent a group of mostly women and children to Turkey. Then in 2015, Thailand deported 109 of those still detained to China against their will, prompting an international outcry which saw the Thai embassy in Turkiye ransacked in protest. For more than a decade, the Thai government put off a decision on what to do about the group.
In February 2025, Thailand sent back 40 Uyghur men to China, despite pleas from Thai lawmakers and UN officials not to deport them.

articles.title: Israel election commission rejects Benjamin Netanyahu charges of fraud
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Central Elections Committee said it had conducted an audit of 9,069 polling stations following complaints and was confident that the announced results accurately reflect the will of the voters

Israeli electoral authorities on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) rejected allegations promoted by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of fraud by Arab parties, who could hold the key to removing him from power after a divisive vote.

President Isaac Herzog will at noon (10:00 GMT) officially receive the results of the October 27 election as he decides whether to give Mr. Netanyahu or his rival, Gadi Eisenkot, the first chance to form a government, with neither commanding enough votes alone.
The Central Elections Committee said it had conducted an audit of 9,069 polling stations following complaints and was confident that the announced results "accurately reflect the will of the voters".
"All complaints submitted by political factions have been reviewed and there were no findings indicating harm to the integrity of the election," it said in a statement.

Mr. Netanyahu has repeatedly alleged fraud by Arab-majority parties, pointing to the arrests of several people with envelopes of cash on election day and later saying lawmakers received money from Qatar -- allegations that have been levelled at his own aides in the past.

Late on Tuesday (November 3), Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara said she would not question anyone without evidence after reports that the head of the domestic security service Shin Bet, a Netanyahu ally, had asked to interrogate Arab parties.
Mr. Netanyahu's Likud party lashed out at her, saying that she was trying to "obstruct the investigation and to cover up this serious case of manipulation of the electoral process by foreign actors".

Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief trying to unite centrists and the centre-right and turn the page on Mr. Netanyahu's long, polarising reign, accused Likud of attempting a "pogrom against democracy".

He had earlier warned Mr. Netanyahu against launching a new war with his close ally U.S. President Donald Trump against Iran, which could help the Israeli Prime Minister push for a unity government or to run out the clock until new elections.
Yair Lapid, a former Prime Minister and key force in the opposition bloc, pointed to the midterm elections in the United States in which Democrats resoundingly trounced Trump's Republicans.
The Shin Bet "outbursts" paired with the U.S. election results "eliminate any possibility of a unity government led by Netanyahu".
Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister who has been in power on and off for nearly two decades, has called for a "broad national government" -- with himself at the top.

articles.title: Who are the Indian-origin candidates in U.S. midterm elections?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress
Indian-origin candidates are seeking office across the United States in the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, the polls are so called because they fall midway through a President’s four-year term

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are due for election, since members serve two-year terms. In the Senate, where members serve six years, 35 of the 100 seats are up for election, including special elections in Ohio and Florida.

The Indian-origin candidates are contesting from States including California, Washington, Virginia, Arizona, Florida, Texas, Ohio, New York and Maryland. Their races span different levels of government, from the U.S. Congress and State executive offices to city leadership positions.

Several Indian-Americans are in the fray across Texas, Florida, Arizona, Ohio, New York and Los Angeles. Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress.
Here are some of the prominent Indian-origin candidates contesting the midterm elections

Congressman Ro Khanna is a member of the progressive wing of the Democratic Party. His grandfather, Amarnath Vidyalankar, was a freedom fighter who was imprisoned alongside Mahatma Gandhi and later served as a Congress Member of Parliament.

Mr. Khanna is a second-generation immigrant. His father, a chemical engineer from the Indian Institute of Technology, and his mother, a school teacher, migrated to the United States from Punjab. Born in Philadelphia, Mr. Khanna studied economics at the University of Chicago before earning a law degree from Yale Law School. He later worked as an intellectual property lawyer with clients from the technology sector.

A Democrat from California, Mr. Khanna is seeking re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, which includes parts of Silicon Valley. He has criticised President Donald Trump’s policies as “utterly destructive”, described him as a “lame duck”, and said Democrats would prevail in the 2026 midterm elections and the 2028 presidential election.

Congresswoman Jayapal, who was born in Chennai, is seeking another term from Washington’s 7th Congressional District. In 2020, she became the second Indian-American woman elected to the U.S. House of Representatives.
Ms. Jayapal traces her roots to Kerala. Her mother, Maya Jayapal, is a writer and counsellor and the author of Bangalore: Roots and Beyond .
Ms. Jayapal was the first Indian-American woman elected to the U.S. House of Representatives and has represented Washington’s 7th Congressional District since 2017.

On October 14, 2026, Ms. Jayapal voiced concern over reports about the removal of 13 crore names from draft electoral rolls in India. The Democratic lawmaker said she supported non-violent protests against what she described as anti-democratic efforts.

articles.title: Jaishankar highlights importance of digital public infrastructure at Commonwealth meet in Antigua and Barbuda
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Mr. Jaishankar also spoke about India's recent Free Trade Agreements and other ongoing negotiations at the meeting

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has highlighted the significance of digital public infrastructure for "good governance and financial responsibility" at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Executive Session in Antigua and Barbuda.

Mr. Jaishankar arrived in St. John's on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) to attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM). He was welcomed at the airport by Foreign Minister Everly Chet Greene and Tourism and Civil Aviation Minister Charles Fernandes.

"Highlighted the value of digital public infrastructure for good governance and financial responsibility. Has helped democratise our economies by expanding opportunities. The Indian example is instructive," Mr. Jaishankar posted on social media after the meeting on Tuesday (November 3).
Mr. Jaishankar also spoke about India's recent Free Trade Agreements and other ongoing negotiations at the meeting.
"Such understandings will contribute to predictable trade and resilient supply chains," he said.
The theme of this year's CHOGM is accelerating partnerships and investment for a prosperous Commonwealth.

articles.title: Attack on vessel near Hormuz Strait: Deceased sailor hailed from Gujarat, kin plan burial in Oman
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Nahim Ajij Gandhar was among the 14 crew members on board the vessel, which was registered at Bedi port in Gujarat’s Jamnagar district

A 25-year-old sailor who died after a suspected drone attack on an Indian-flagged cargo vessel off the Oman coast near the Strait of Hormuz hailed from Gujarat’s Devbhumi Dwarka district, a relative of the vessel owner said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Nahim Ajij Gandhar was among the 14 crew members on board the vessel, which was registered at Bedi port in Gujarat’s Jamnagar district. He said all the crew members were residents of Salaya.
The sailor’s family has decided to conduct Gandhar’s burial in Oman, citing delays in completing formalities, he said.

The projectile hit, which triggered strong condemnation from India, destroyed the mechanised sailing vessel (MSV) and the consignment of dates it was carrying, said Akbar Ahmed Sumbhaniya, whose younger brother Jusab owns the vessel.

An MSV is a hybrid watercraft that retains traditional sailing rigs and hull designs (such as wooden cargo dhows or kotias) while also being fitted with a mechanical propulsion engine (typically a diesel engine) and a propeller.

The vessel, Al Jusufi, was carrying nearly 900 metric tonnes of dates from Hamriyah port in the United Arab Emirates to Porbandar when it was struck on November 2 off the Oman coast near Limah, said Mr. Sumbhaniya.

articles.title: Hackers target France’s blood bank freezers, reprogram storage to 110°C
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: They reprogrammed cold storage units, typically kept at a freezing −30°C to safely preserve blood products, by pushing temperature settings up to 110°C (230°F)

A major cyberattack targeted cold storage facilities of France’s national blood agency , Etablissement Francais du Sang (EFS), after hackers breached systems to remotely heat freezers holding donor blood samples and plasma.
The incident was reported between November 1 and 2, when unknown bad actors compromised Coolworld, a key refrigeration maintenance contractor for EFS.
They reprogrammed cold storage units, typically kept at a freezing −30°C to safely preserve blood products, by pushing temperature settings up to 110°C (230°F).

However, an on-duty technician noticed this abnormal overnight temperature spike on monitoring systems, and averted the damage. Rapid emergency protocols allowed technical teams to intervene before permanent damage affected the inventory.
France’s Ministry of Health confirmed that the breach was contained with zero operational disruption to hospital supplies or transfusion services.

While the EFS initially reported that the impacted containers held routine health-monitoring blood samples, official statements later confirmed that frozen plasma meant for medical transfusions was also stored within the affected refrigeration units.
The incident coincided with a broader wave of cyber intrusions targeting networked industrial cooling systems, including supermarket refrigeration across roughly a dozen European nations.

articles.title: Government approves strengthening, extension of 850 fast track special courts to deal with child abuse, rape cases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Launched on October 2, 2019, following a Supreme Court directive, the scheme currently covers 29 States and Union Territories

The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) approved continuation of a Central scheme to strengthen fast track special courts to deal with child abuse and rape cases and increase their number from 779 to 850.

Launched on October 2, 2019, following a Supreme Court directive, the scheme currently covers 29 States and Union Territories. Since the inception of the scheme, these special courts have disposed of more than 4.02 lakh cases related to rape and offences under the POCSO Act , 2012. The scheme has now been extended for a period of five years till March 2031.
Briefing reporters on the decisions taken by the Cabinet, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the government is committed to firmly dealing with cases of atrocities against women and children.
He said the decision is part of efforts to fully utilise and implement prevailing laws and draft new legislations to deal with such cases.

"The scheme will be implemented with a total outlay of ₹3,788.04 crore to ensure speedy trial of rape and child sexual abuse cases. Each court will be staffed with a dedicated judicial officer, a special public prosecutor, and six support personnel to enhance efficiency in case disposal," an official statement said.

"As part of the expansion, the number of FTSCs (fast track special courts) will increase from 779 to 850 across participating States and Union Territories. The Centre will contribute ₹2,353.15 crore through the Nirbhaya Fund, while States and UTs will provide ₹1,434.89 crore. The Department of Justice in the Union Law Ministry will oversee implementation in collaboration with State governments and UT administrations, with additional districts to be included based on the pendency of rape and POCSO cases," it added.

The scheme also focusses on creating a victim-friendly judicial environment through vulnerable witness deposition centres and child-friendly court facilities, helping survivors testify with dignity and minimal trauma.
The Department of Justice will continue to monitor court performance through an online dashboard, regular progress reviews, and consultations with high courts and State governments.

articles.title: TDP candidate wins Tirupati Mayoral seat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Manne Srinivasa Prasad wins the Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC) Mayor seat with a majority of 61,582 votes over YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) candidate Y. Vasudeva

Telugu Desam Party (TDP) candidate Manne Srinivasa Prasad (J.B. Srinivas) won the Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC) Mayor seat with a majority of 61,582 votes over YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) candidate Y. Vasudeva by the end of counting at S.V. Arts College in Tirupati on Tuesday.

Of the overall 1.36 lakh votes polled, Mr. Srinivas received 94,937 votes and Mr. Vasudeva bagged 33,355 votes. While 3,176 votes were achieved by other candidates together, 3,149 votes were considered as invalid and 1,389 votes came under none of the above (NOTA).

Among the 66 wards in the TMC limits, TDP candidates emerged victorious in 38 wards and YSRCP candidates were successful in 19. The candidates of Jana Sena Party (JSP), Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and others won three wards each.

TDP’s Mayoral candidates were leading in Kadapa, Nellore and Ongole Municipal Corporation elections. Due to heavy rain in Ongole, the counting process, which was originally scheduled to begin by 8 a.m. on Tuesday, commenced by 12 p.m. at RISE Engineering College centre.

In Kadapa, TDP’s Mayoral candidate Malli Suvarna was leading with 80,819 votes, while YSRCP candidate Bandi Deepthi got 41,020 votes by the end of two rounds of counting at Maulana Azad National Urdu University (MANUU) Polytechnic College.

In Nellore, TDP’s Mayoral candidate Poluboina Roop Kumar Yadav was leading with 88,792 votes and his YSRCP counterpart Anam Vijaya Kumar Reddy received 45,150 votes after the second round of counting.

Among the 66 wards in the TMC limits, TDP candidates emerged victorious in 38 wards and YSRCP candidates were successful in 19. The candidates of Jana Sena Party (JSP), Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and others won three wards each.

TDP’s Mayoral candidates were leading in Kadapa, Nellore and Ongole Municipal Corporation elections. Due to heavy rain in Ongole, the counting process, which was originally scheduled to begin by 8 a.m. on Tuesday, commenced by 12 p.m. at RISE Engineering College centre.

In Kadapa, TDP’s Mayoral candidate Malli Suvarna was leading with 80,819 votes, while YSRCP candidate Bandi Deepthi got 41,020 votes by the end of two rounds of counting at Maulana Azad National Urdu University (MANUU) Polytechnic College.

In Nellore, TDP’s Mayoral candidate Poluboina Roop Kumar Yadav was leading with 88,792 votes and his YSRCP counterpart Anam Vijaya Kumar Reddy received 45,150 votes after the second round of counting.

articles.title: Thunderstorm forecast in 13 Telangana districts on November 5
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Cyclone Murasu weakened into deep depression
India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a thunderstorm forecast in 13 Telangana districts for Thursday (November 5, 2026).
The cyclone Murasu has weakened into a deep depression and is likely to further weaken into a depression by the evening of Wednesday (November 4, 2026) according to the IMD.

According to IMDs latest bulletin, thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds are very likely to occur at isolated places in Karimanagar, Peddapalli, Jayashankar Bhupalpaly, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Nalgonda, Suryapet, Mahabubnagar, Warangal, Hanumakonda, Jangaon and Rangareddy districts.

Hyderabad city and its surrounding areas for the next 24 hours will see a partly cloudy sky. “Light rain or thundershowers accompanied with gusty winds are likely to occur in parts of the city towards afternoon or evening. The maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be around 31C and 22C respectively,” the bulletin said.

articles.title: Draft report on implementation of Labour Codes moots higher minimum wages, wider eligibility for bonus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Higher minimum wages and wider eligibility for bonus and other benefits are some of the recommendations in a draft report on implementation of the four Labour Codes in the State.
The draft report was submitted by Minister for Labour Bindhu Krishna to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday.
The report proposes more elbow room for the State government in matters such as lockouts and lay-offs.
Keralam is yet to frame rules for the four Labour Codes that were notified by the Union government in November last year

A meeting chaired by the Chief Minister on October 22 had decided to form a committee that included trade union representatives for submitting practical recommendations on framing State rules for the Labour Codes. The committee, with the Labour Commissioner as convener and Law additional secretary, seven trade union representatives, and Labour department officials as members, held discussions and enquiries over 10 days before submitting its report to the Labour Minister.
The report proposes amendments to laws and recommendations to ensure workers’ welfare, job security, wages, and benefits.

It recommends expanding a worker’s family unit from the current three members to five by including parents with the aim of amending guidelines for deciding minimum wages. When the minimum wages are calculated, the amendment will result in workers getting more wages.
It recommends a provision for free medical check-ups for workers engaging in hazardous and dangerous occupations.
Strict safety guidelines will be included in conditions that permit women workers to work at night. Provisions that ensure women’s security will be included in the State rules too.
The report recommends bringing more workers within the purview of benefits, including bonus.
Apprehensions in Keralam regarding the Labour Codes and the recommendations made by trade unions were examined by the committee.
Ms. Krishnasaid the rights and interests of workers will be protected during implementation of the Labour Codes.

articles.title: Prime Minister Modi speaks to A.P. CM Naidu, pledges Central support in dealing with damage caused by two cyclones
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chief Minister briefs him on the losses caused by ‘Arnab’ and ‘Murasu’, particularly to agriculture, horticulture, roads and electricity infrastructure, and seeks immediate Central assistance; he also flags the issue of chilli consignments stranded at Colombo port

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday spoke to Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu over phone and reviewed the impact of cyclones Arnab and Murasu that hit the State within a week, assuring the State of the Centre's support in dealing with the damage.
Mr. Naidu briefed the Prime Minister on the losses caused by the cyclones, particularly to agriculture, horticulture, roads and electricity infrastructure.

He said heavy rainfall and strong winds had caused extensive damage to crops and disrupted life in several districts, and sought adequate financial assistance from the Centre to provide relief to the affected farmers and restore damaged infrastructure.

Mr. Modi appreciated the State government’s handling of the cyclone-related situation and commended Mr. Naidu for remaining alert and addressing the difficulties faced by the people in the affected areas.

Meanwhile, the Chief Minister intensified his efforts to secure immediate Central assistance. Besides writing to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, the Chief Minister spoke to him four times and requested for early deployment of Central teams to assess the losses, officials in the Chief Minister's Office said.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu urges the Centre to announce interim assistance without delay to help restore normalcy and provide relief to the affected farmers. File | Photo Credit: ANI

In its preliminary assessment of the damage caused by Cyclone Arnab, the government estimated the losses at ₹4,563 crore. As many as 781 villages across 16 districts had been severely affected. Agricultural crops in over three lakh hectares and horticultural crops in over 13,600 hectares suffered damage. The cyclone also damaged about 29,000 electricity poles and 7,981 km of power lines.
Mr. Naidu sought ₹4,563 crore as immediate assistance to address the damage caused by the cyclone.

In a separate communication to Mr. Shah, the Chief Minister said that Cyclone Murasu had affected 465 villages in seven districts. Paddy in over 50,473 hectares and commercial crops in an extent of 1,985 hectares were damaged, he said. Preliminary assessment put the damage caused to properties at ₹343 crore.
The Chief Minister urged the Centre to announce interim assistance without delay to help restore normalcy and provide relief to farmers.

Apart from the cyclone-related losses, Mr. Naidu sought the intervention of Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal to resolve the issue of more than 150 containers of chilli stranded at the Colombo port in Sri Lanka.
The consignments, valued at nearly ₹60 crore, were meant for export to China, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Thailand and Singapore. They were reportedly held up over objections relating to moisture content.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections impact on India: Faster trade deal talks and higher tariffs likely
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Trade and geopolitical experts say that losing control of the U.S. Congress will push President Donald Trump to increase tariff pressure on India to seal a deal. Indian negotiators, for their part, will smell an opportunity

The results of the U.S. midterm elections, which show that the Democrats have gained control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, will likely speed up talks between India and the U.S. on a trade deal but could also see higher tariffs on India until the deal is closed, according to experts.

On the one hand, a desire to now quickly close the trade deal to show strength domestically could induce Mr. Trump to increase his tariff pressure on India, while on the other, Indian negotiators will likely see this election result as an opportunity to push through a favourable deal for India.
U.S. midterm elections: Follow LIVE updates from the results on November 4, 2026

According to Ajay Srivastava, founder of the trade think-tank Global Trade Research Initiative, this loss will push U.S. President Donald Trump to increase his exercise of his executive powers to pressure India into accepting a deal.
“With foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win,” Mr. Srivastava said. “Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout.”

Leaders in the U.S. and India have repeatedly said over the last few months that the deal between the two countries is nearly ready and is awaiting final approvals. India, in particular, has been holding out until it receives an assurance that it will win a clear advantage over its competitors.

“Trump will now use his executive powers to pressure India for a quick deal that secures market access for U.S. agricultural and industrial goods, alongside other major concessions for U.S. companies,” Mr. Srivastava said.

While the U.S. Supreme Court in February defanged Mr. Trump’s reciprocal tariff policy that had seen tariffs of up to 50% being levied on India, the President has other tools through which he can levy tariffs.

According to Deep Pal, Director of Geopolitics and Policy at the Koan Advisory Group, the implications of these election results might lead to some difficulty for Mr. Trump in gaining support for his policies.

“For this administration, especially after tonight, any decision has to look like a win domestically, to core Republican voters,” Mr. Pal said. “With Congress out of his hands, a lot will depend on how much control Mr. Trump has over the Republican party and if there will be any purchase for his ideas.”
However, Mr. Pal pointed out that the Indian government might view this new reality in the U.S. with greater optimism.

“Indian negotiators, on the other hand, may think that the new realities will make the Trump administration amenable to a better trade deal for India, breaking the current deadlock, and leading to a flurry of new conversations,” Mr. Pal said.

“With foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win,” Mr. Srivastava said. “Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout.”

Leaders in the U.S. and India have repeatedly said over the last few months that the deal between the two countries is nearly ready and is awaiting final approvals. India, in particular, has been holding out until it receives an assurance that it will win a clear advantage over its competitors.

“Trump will now use his executive powers to pressure India for a quick deal that secures market access for U.S. agricultural and industrial goods, alongside other major concessions for U.S. companies,” Mr. Srivastava said.

While the U.S. Supreme Court in February defanged Mr. Trump’s reciprocal tariff policy that had seen tariffs of up to 50% being levied on India, the President has other tools through which he can levy tariffs.

According to Deep Pal, Director of Geopolitics and Policy at the Koan Advisory Group, the implications of these election results might lead to some difficulty for Mr. Trump in gaining support for his policies.

“For this administration, especially after tonight, any decision has to look like a win domestically, to core Republican voters,” Mr. Pal said. “With Congress out of his hands, a lot will depend on how much control Mr. Trump has over the Republican party and if there will be any purchase for his ideas.”

However, Mr. Pal pointed out that the Indian government might view this new reality in the U.S. with greater optimism.

“Indian negotiators, on the other hand, may think that the new realities will make the Trump administration amenable to a better trade deal for India, breaking the current deadlock, and leading to a flurry of new conversations,” Mr. Pal said.

articles.title: Who is Abdul El-Sayed, first Muslim U.S. Senator-elect?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Abdul El-Sayed is set to become the first Muslim to enter the U.S. Senate with his victory over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers in midterm elections

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat on Tuesday (November 4, 2026), according to media projections, becoming the first Muslim elected to the chamber and preserving a crucial Democratic seat in the party’s fight for Senate control.

His victory denied Republicans the chance to fill the seat left vacant by retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters. The 42-year-old former public health official ran on a progressive platform focused ⁠on lowering costs for working families and ⁠reducing corporate influence in politics.
His win marked a breakthrough for the Democratic Party’s progressive wing ‌in this closely contested midterm election cycle.

Abdul El-Sayed was born on October 31 , 1984, in Rochester Hills, Michigan, U.S.. He attended public schools, where he captained his high school football, wrestling and lacrosse teams. He was raised by his father, Mohamed, an Egyptian immigrant and his stepmom, Jackie, whose family has lived in Gratiot County, Michigan since the 1800s. Mr. El-Sayed earned his undergraduate degree with the highest distinction from the University of Michigan where he also played on the Wolverine men’s lacrosse team. He went on to earn a medical degree from Columbia University under an NIH-funded fellowship, as well as a second doctorate from Oxford University as Rhodes Scholer.
He lives in Ann Arbor with his wife, Dr. Sarah Jukaku and their two daughters.

Although trained as a physician, Mr. El-Sayed shifted his focus to public service after realising the political systemic issues that was deteriorating public health, according to his campaign website.

He rebuilt Detroit’s Health Department after bankruptcy and led Wayne County’s Department of Health. Human & Veterans Services, serving 1.8 million residents. His public service spans several achievements, including securing free eyeglasses for children, targeting major environmental polluters, making the life-saving Narcan universally accessible and pioneering a programme projected to cancel up to $700 million in medical debt for 3,00,000 Michiganders, as per the website.

He authored Medicare for All: A Citizen’s Guide and served on former President Biden’s 2020 Unity Task Force for Healthcare to help develop policies aimed at lowering prescription drug costs. His public service earned him recognition as “Public Official of the Year” by the Michigan LCV and also a spot on Crain’s Detroit Business 40 Under 40 list.

Mr. El-Sayed won the U.S. Senate seat in Michigan over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. He launched his campaign to lower living costs and ensure government agencies serve working people rather than billionaires.

Mr. Rogers, 63, ‌a former Congressman and FBI agent, entered ​the race with strong backing from President Trump and national Republicans and sought ⁠to cast Mr. El-Sayed as a radical candidate sympathetic to Islamic extremism through alleged ties to the Muslim ‌Brotherhood, claims that Mr. El-Sayed denies and that remain unsupported by evidence. Democrats said the attacks on Mr. El-Sayed relied on Islamophobic tropes, according to Reuters.

Mr. Rogers also devoted significant effort to courting Jewish voters who may have been uneasy with Mr. El-Sayed’s opposition to U.S. military ‌aid for Israel and his characterisation of Israel’s actions in ​Gaza as genocide.

But Mr. Rogers struggled to overcome voter concerns about the economy and ⁠President Trump’s low ratings. In the closing weeks of ⁠the race, he broke with the President on the war in Iran and the ‌U.S. trade dispute with Canada, arguing that ending both was necessary to help bring down costs ​for businesses and consumers.

articles.title: Apollo Foundation’s hospital in Aragonda blends healthcare with education, nutrition and sanitation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: What if improving the health of a village meant doing more than building a hospital, treating patients and performing surgeries? In Aragonda, a village in Andhra Pradesh’s Chittoor district, an initiative that began with a 50-bed rural hospital has evolved into a community development model that links healthcare with education, nutrition, sanitation and preventive health.

Through its Total Health programme, Apollo Foundation is attempting to address the wider social determinants of health, with interventions spanning different stages of people’s lives, from maternal and child healthcare to youth development, women’s economic independence and elderly care.

The programme’s interventions include 1,200 antenatal and postnatal check-ups for new mothers, training in hygiene practices across 2,600 schools and industry-related and sports skills for more than 545 young people. It has also conducted over two lakh yoga sessions, alongside free screening and care for non-communicable diseases (NCDs), while more than 10.8 lakh meals have been served to elderly people through its geriatric nutrition centres.

Prathap C. Reddy, founder chairman of Apollo Hospitals Group, said the initiative reflected his belief that quality and affordable healthcare should reach every Indian, irrespective of where they lived. While the hospital initially brought modern medicine to his village, the larger vision was to create conditions in which people could lead healthier lives, he said. “Medicine can save lives, but to change the health of a generation, we must also change the conditions in which life is lived,” he added.

Alongside preventive and community healthcare, Apollo Hospitals Aragonda has also expanded its specialised surgical services, completing 1,000 total knee replacement (TKR) procedures. Established as a 50-bed hospital in 2000, it has served more than 1.67 lakh patients and performed over 12,000 surgeries in 26 years.

The knee replacement programme has grown from 100 procedures in 2019 to 500 in 2022 and 1,000 in 2026. “The 1,000 procedures have been completed without a single reported infection,” said Sangita Reddy, joint managing director of Apollo Hospitals.

Telemedicine was another early intervention. With a network of three telephone lines, Apollo connected specialists in cities with patients in rural areas, allowing doctors to examine CT scans and ultrasound images remotely. The initiative enabled specialists to guide local doctors in treating patients who otherwise would have had to travel to distant hospitals. She recalled that former President of US, Bill Clinton, witnessed a telemedicine demonstration from Aragonda during his visit to Hyderabad.

Preetha Reddy, executive vice-chairperson of Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited said the organisation remained committed to narrowing the divide between rural and urban healthcare. “The ability to perform specialised procedures such as knee replacements in a village demonstrates the potential for such models to be replicated in other parts of the world,” she added.

articles.title: APSPDCL deploys over 2,000 staff for restoration works after cyclone damage

fullParagraphs: Amid severe adverse conditions created by cyclones Arnab and Murasu, over 2,000 personnel of the Andhra Pradesh Southern Power Distribution Company Limited (APSPDCL) are working round-the-clock to restore power supply in the jurisdiction of A.P. Eastern Power Discom Limited (APEPDCL),

“The APSPDCL machinery, along with officials from other power discoms, is playing a key role in restoring the power infrastructure damaged by the impact of the cyclones in West Godavari district at the earliest,” said APSPDCL Chairman Siva Sankar Lotheti.

Mr. Siva Sankar Lotheti is the Special Supervisory Officer for West Godavari district. In a statement released to the media, he said, “APSPDCL has mobilised manpower on a large scale for restoration works, including directors, managers, engineers and field-level staff to participate in the massive operation.”

The APSPDCL chief has also been staying in West Godavari district for the past one week, assessing the actual ground-level situation and providing necessary instructions to the officials to complete the restoration works expeditiously.

Not only in the APEPDCL jurisdiction, but the APSPDCL is also extending its support to expedite the restoration of the power infrastructure damaged due to Cyclone Murasu in the APCPDCL jurisdiction, headquartered at Vijayawada.

The Chief Minister and Ministers of the State have appreciated the efforts being made by the Electricity department machinery to restore power supply during the severe and challenging conditions caused by the two consecutive cyclones.

articles.title: In setback to Keralam govt, HC reinstates Milma Thiruvananthapuram union dissolved over Sabarimala ghee row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Division Bench quashes order of Registrar of Co-operative Societies which was upheld by Single Bench

In a setback to the Keralam government, the High Court has directed the reinstatement of members of the dissolved managing committee of the Thiruvananthapuram Regional Co-operative Milk Producers Union, which was allegedly disbanded without notice over the Sabarimala-Milma ghee misappropriation allegations.

A Single Bench had earlier upheld the decision by the Registrar of Co-operative Societies to dissolve the managing committee of the Thiruvananthapuram Regional Co-operative Milk Producers Union, including four districts, Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta and Alappuzha.

The Division Bench of Justices A.K. Jayasankaran Nambiar and A.K. Preetha quashed the Registrar’s order. It also set aside the Single Bench order, which found that the Registrar had sufficient material to substantiate allegations of misappropriation in the supply of ghee to Sabarimala Sannidhanam. The court directed that the reinstated managing committee replace the Administrator appointed in its stead.

The Division Bench found that the Registrar had relied on a report and recommendations made by the Joint Director (General), Directorate of Dairy Development, to supersede the union’s managing committee.

It held that the Joint Director had accessed sufficient material to infer material relating to the allegations against the managing committee members. This meant the members had fully cooperated with the inquiry and there was no question of evidence tampering or suppression, as alleged by the State government. The Division Bench observed that any action by a statutory authority unsupported by required rationale would cast doubt on the good faith of the authority concerned.

The Division Bench observed that the Registrar’s order superseding the committee under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 was passed without consultation with the State Co-operative Union as well. The Registrar had reasoned that issuing a show-cause notice was not practical considering the severity of the allegations.

The members of the dissolved managing committee, through lawyers Ranjith Thampan and P.C. Sasidharan, had argued before the Single Bench that the Registrar had no material to initiate proceedings to supersede the democratically elected committee. They also contended that the order did not follow fair procedure and that dispensing without issuing a show-cause notice was permitted only in exceptional circumstances.

articles.title: Old Marthanda Varma Bridge at Aluva to reopen on Thursday, two days ahead of schedule

fullParagraphs: The old Marthanda Varma Bridge at Aluva, which was closed for maintenance work, will be reopened to traffic on Thursday, Aluva MLA Anwar Sadath said on Wednesday.
He said the bridge was set to reopen as the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) had completed the repair work two days ahead of schedule.

Sources with the Ernakulam Rural police said traffic would be allowed over the bridge on the national highway from 6 a.m. on Thursday. The closure of the bridge and the resultant traffic regulations imposed from October 28 had caused severe congestion in the area. It was announced that the restrictions would remain in place until November 6.

articles.title: APPCB seeks ₹36.17 crore compensation from ONGC over Mori-5 well blowout, serves show-cause notice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The APPCB began the probe after a blowout occurred due to a gas leak in M/s.ONGC Well Mori-5 at Irusumanda Village in Dr.B.R.Ambedkar Konaseema district on January 5, 2026.

The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board has served a show-cause notice to the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), proposing environmental compensation of ₹36.17 crore for operating M/s.ONGC Well Mori-5 without obtaining mandatory environmental clearances for 12,057 days.
The APPCB probed the violation after a blowout due to a gas leak at the Mori-5 well at Irusumanda Village in Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema district on January 5, 2026.

In April, the APPCB’s Monitoring Committee learnt that ONGC had handed over the well to its Production Enhancement Contracts (PEC) contractor i.e., M/s Deep Exploratory Services Pvt Ltd in April 2025 for carrying out workover and production enhancement activities. Later, the Committee noted that M/s.ONGC Well Mori-5 is operating without obtaining mandatory environmental clearances and consents.

In a show-cause notice dated September 15, APPCB Member Secretary S. Srisaravanan stated; “The Board hereby issues a show-cause notice to M/s.ONGC Well Mori-5, as to why the Environmental Compensation of ₹36,17,10,000 shall not be levied on your facility, for operating the well in violation of consent conditions”. A copy of the show-cause notice is with The Hindu .

ONGC has been directed to submit its reply within 15 days of receiving the notice, failing which the environmental compensation of ₹36.17 crore would be imposed for causing environmental damage due to the blowout.

Meanwhile, Konaseema-based environmental activist, Venkatapathi Raja Yenumala, filed a case before the National Green Tribunal, Chennai, on the incident and violations in the operations of the Mori Well-5.

articles.title: Odisha officials intimidating tribal people in Kotia villages, says A.P. Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Andhra Pradesh Minister for Tribal Welfare Gummidi Sandhya Rani has condemned the alleged intimidation of tribal communities in the Kotia villages by Odisha government officials, accusing them of interfering with the fundamental rights and democratic freedoms of tribal people.

In a statement on Wednesday, the Minister alleged that Odisha officials had been creating fear among tribal residents in 29 villages and pressuring them to boycott the elections. She termed the alleged attempts to intimidate tribal voters and candidates as undemocratic and unacceptable.

Questioning the alleged detention and concealment of tribal residents, she asked whether preventing people from exercising their voting rights and restricting their freedom of movement was justified. She also expressed concern over reports that vehicles belonging to tribal residents were being seized over fears that they might travel to cast their votes.

The Minister further alleged that Odisha officials had been creating disturbances in Kotia villages over the past few days and resorting to high-handed behaviour against Andhra Pradesh officials and police personnel. She questioned the urgency being shown over a Supreme Court status quo order that, according to her, had been in existence for a long time.

The Minister maintained that the responsibility for deciding on any postponement of elections rested with the Election Commission and that no one had the right to pressure tribal communities or candidates into boycotting the electoral process.

Emphasising that the freedom and voting rights of innocent tribal people must be protected, she urged Odisha officials to act democratically, refrain from intimidating villagers and respect their constitutional rights. “The Andhra Pradesh government will stand firmly by the tribal communities and will not tolerate any attempts to deprive them of their freedom and voting rights,” the Minister asserted.

Ms. Sandhya Rani’s remarks come amid renewed tensions over the long-standing territorial and administrative dispute surrounding the Kotia group of villages along the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, where competing claims and election-related developments have remained contentious.

articles.title: Kedartal avalanche claims lives of two sisters from Lucknow who shared passion for trekking
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Toll touches four as two more bodies are found on the Kedartal trekking route; four trekkers, all friends from West Bengal, are still missing

A family’s desperate search for two missing daughters ended in heartbreaking tragedy on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) after the bodies of sisters Vartika Verma and Deepika Verma, residents of Lucknow, were recovered following an avalanche on the Kedartal trekking route in Uttarakhand.

The sisters were among the eight trekkers stranded near Kacchi Dhang, on their way to Kedartal. The group of 13 had set out from Gangotri on October 27, but heavy snowfall and avalanches cut off their route, leaving them stranded in the mountains.

The 26-km trek from Gangotri to Kedartal passes through Kedar Kharak and involves narrow, rocky stretches at high altitude. The glacial lake is situated at about 4,700 metres above sea level, surrounded by high mountain peaks.
With the recovery of two more bodies, the death toll in the avalanche has reached four. Rescue teams are continuing their search for the remaining four trekkers, all friends from West Bengal.

‘Please don’t scroll. Please share’ were the words Atul Verma posted on Instagram, alongside an AI-generated photograph of his younger sisters smiling in the front row of a trekking group. He was desperately trying to draw attention to the missing trekkers and reach someone who could help.

“This is not just a photograph of a trekking group. These are eight human lives, eight families waiting for their loved ones to return,” Mr. Atul Verma wrote in his appeal. He urged people to tag authorities, rescue teams and journalists, and asked them to pray for his sisters and the other trekkers. “One share could help this appeal reach someone who can make a difference,” he said.
The family said they had learnt about the incident through social media and not from the trekking agency.

Mr. Atul Verma then rushed to Uttarkashi, hoping there was still a chance of finding his sisters safe. He reached the district headquarters on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) with other relatives, but was eventually informed that both sisters had died.

The Verma sisters shared a love for trekking and had explored several trails across India and Nepal. Vartika Verma, the younger sister, was a freelance influencer, while Deepika Verma worked as a graphic designer with a private firm. Both had considerable trekking experience. Just two months ago, they had returned from a trip to the Valley of Flowers and Hemkund Sahib in Uttarakhand.
“They were well-equipped and experienced,” Mr. Atul Verma said. The family had never imagined that something both sisters loved so much would end in this way.

The family’s appeal has also questioned the arrangements made by the trekking agency. Mr. Atul Verma also questioned whether adequate emergency arrangements and guide support had been provided. He called for an investigation into the agency’s role and demanded accountability.”

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 04 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Kedartal avalanche claims lives of two sisters from Lucknow who shared passion for trekking

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Toll touches four as two more bodies are found on the Kedartal trekking route; four trekkers, all friends from West Bengal, are still missing

A family’s desperate search for two missing daughters ended in heartbreaking tragedy on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) after the bodies of sisters Vartika Verma and Deepika Verma, residents of Lucknow, were recovered following an avalanche on the Kedartal trekking route in Uttarakhand.

The sisters were among the eight trekkers stranded near Kacchi Dhang, on their way to Kedartal. The group of 13 had set out from Gangotri on October 27, but heavy snowfall and avalanches cut off their route, leaving them stranded in the mountains.

The 26-km trek from Gangotri to Kedartal passes through Kedar Kharak and involves narrow, rocky stretches at high altitude. The glacial lake is situated at about 4,700 metres above sea level, surrounded by high mountain peaks.

With the recovery of two more bodies, the death toll in the avalanche has reached four. Rescue teams are continuing their search for the remaining four trekkers, all friends from West Bengal.

‘Please don’t scroll. Please share’ were the words Atul Verma posted on Instagram, alongside an AI-generated photograph of his younger sisters smiling in the front row of a trekking group. He was desperately trying to draw attention to the missing trekkers and reach someone who could help.

“This is not just a photograph of a trekking group. These are eight human lives, eight families waiting for their loved ones to return,” Mr. Atul Verma wrote in his appeal. He urged people to tag authorities, rescue teams and journalists, and asked them to pray for his sisters and the other trekkers. “One share could help this appeal reach someone who can make a difference,” he said.

The family said they had learnt about the incident through social media and not from the trekking agency.

Mr. Atul Verma then rushed to Uttarkashi, hoping there was still a chance of finding his sisters safe. He reached the district headquarters on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) with other relatives, but was eventually informed that both sisters had died.

The Verma sisters shared a love for trekking and had explored several trails across India and Nepal. Vartika Verma, the younger sister, was a freelance influencer, while Deepika Verma worked as a graphic designer with a private firm. Both had considerable trekking experience. Just two months ago, they had returned from a trip to the Valley of Flowers and Hemkund Sahib in Uttarakhand.

“They were well-equipped and experienced,” Mr. Atul Verma said. The family had never imagined that something both sisters loved so much would end in this way.

The family’s appeal has also questioned the arrangements made by the trekking agency. Their appeal asked if weather advisories had been checked, and if the risks of the high-altitude trek were properly assessed by the trekking agency. Mr. Atul Verma also questioned whether adequate emergency arrangements and guide support had been provided. He called for an investigation into the agency’s role and demanded accountability.”

Teams from the State Disaster Response Force and the Nehru Institute of Mountaineering had recovered four bodies till the noon on Wednesday. The search for the remaining missing trekkers continues.

articles.title: Centre earmarks ₹2,814 crore to boost lithium, nickel processing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: In a social media post, Union Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy stated the scheme would help strengthen domestic capabilities, boost manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports.

The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a ₹2,814-crore capital expenditure support scheme to establish domestic processing facilities for lithium and nickel, seeking to strengthen India’s critical mineral ecosystem and reduce import dependence. The scheme will remain in force for five years.

India’s domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure for critical minerals remains limited, with commercial-scale operations constrained by high capital requirements, limited access to suitable technologies and inadequate availability of raw materials, the government said in a statement.
Union Minister for Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy said the scheme would strengthen domestic capabilities, boost manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports.

“It will benefit key sectors such as electronics, semiconductors, batteries, defence, heavy equipment and machinery, while supporting industries across the manufacturing value chain that utilise critical minerals,” he said in a social media post.
Under the scheme, the government will provide a capital subsidy of 30% of the investment required to establish four critical mineral processing plants — two each for lithium and nickel.
The minimum processing capacity will be 30,000 tonnes (30 kt) each for lithium and 50,000 tonnes (50 kt) each for nickel.
The subsidy will be capped at ₹500 crore per beneficiary for lithium projects and ₹900 crore per beneficiary for nickel facilities.

The four beneficiaries will be selected through a least-cost bidding process, with preference given to technically qualified applicants seeking the lowest capital expenditure support. Incentives will be disbursed in three tranches.

Industry body the Federation of Indian Mineral Industries (FIMI) welcomed the initiative, saying it could encourage fresh investments, increase domestic value addition and strengthen supply chains for battery manufacturing and other strategic industries.
However, it said that securing adequate raw materials would be critical to the scheme’s success.
“Ensuring a reliable supply of raw material through domestic mining and overseas sourcing will be equally important for the success of these processing facilities,” the industry body told The Hindu.
It also underlined the need to develop the entire value chain, from mining to processing and refining, to strengthen India’s long-term mineral security.

articles.title: Union Cabinet approves new VISTAR scheme to overhaul India’s statistical system
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The three-pronged scheme is aimed at strengthening data collecting, analysis, the incorporation of AI, as well as provide fresh data on the unorganised sector to make the overall GDP figure more accurate

The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a ₹4,371 crore scheme to overhaul the statistical architecture of the country at both the Central as well as State level, called the Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR) scheme, for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31.

“Aligned with the central objective of Viksit Bharat 2047, the VISTAR Scheme is designed to establish a dynamic, real-time and future-ready official statistical architecture for enhanced timeliness, data granularity, interoperability with harmonised and AI ready datasets,” the government said in a release.

As per the government, the VISTAR scheme will be divided into three components: Comprehensive statistical operations and strengthening of the ecosystem, Support for statistical strengthening, and an Economic Census.

Under the Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem component, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has proposed to conduct 59 surveys during the 16th Finance Commission cycle, as compared to 43 major surveys conducted previously.
This, the government said, could potentially fill “critical data gaps in various sectors” and thereby improve decision-making and enable timely and targeted policy interventions.

“In addition, building on recent digital transformations in technology enabled data collection and user-centric dissemination, MoSPI will focus on the end-to-end digitalisation of statistical processes and embedding Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into regular workflows, primarily for data processing, validation, and analysis,” the government added.

Further, it added that, by mainstreaming alternate sources such as mobile phones, scanners, and e-commerce data, MoSPI will aim to complement traditional surveys, reduce respondent burden, fill data gaps, and strengthen evidence-based policymaking.

Under the support for statistical strengthening (SSS) component, the Centre will provide funds to State governments to help transform the statistical capabilities of States and Union Territories through a redesigned, deliverable-linked framework.

“The vision focuses on building state-level capacity to generate high-quality, granular data at the district and other disaggregated levels, developing indigenous data processing capabilities, and embedding data use cases into localized policymaking,” the government said.

MoSPI will also undertake the 8th Economic Census (EC) in collaboration with the States and Union Territories in order to obtain granular data and activity details of all the non-farm establishments and workers hired down to the gram panchayat and ward levels

This, the government said, would provide an assessment of the unorganised sector of the economy and will serve as the baseline for developing the National Statistical Business Register (SBR) to facilitate targeted enterprise surveys and strategic interventions.

“The economic census data will be extremely useful for planners and policy makers at national and sub-national levels, which will pave the way for estimating the contribution of the unorganised sector to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP),” the government said.
